````javascript
 1: /**
 2:  * Schema versions for the artifacts Impeccable writes, plus the readers and
 3:  * writers for the PRODUCT.md provenance stamp.
 4:  *
 5:  * Why schema versions rather than the skill version: a PRODUCT.md written by
 6:  * v4.0.0 is not stale under v4.0.1, so stamping the release version would make
 7:  * every artifact "old" on every patch. A schema version changes only when the
 8:  * shape changes, which is exactly when a migration is owed. It also gives the
 9:  * writing flows a literal constant to copy instead of a value they would have
10:  * to look up.
11:  *
12:  * DESIGN.md deliberately carries no stamp. It follows the external
13:  * design.md spec that Stitch's linter validates, and an extra frontmatter key
14:  * risks failing that lint for no gain: every DESIGN.md staleness signal
15:  * (sidecar schema version, sidecar mtime, section coverage, git drift) is
16:  * measurable without one.
17:  */
18: /** PRODUCT.md as init.md writes it today: the ten-section v4 record. */
19: export const PRODUCT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1;
20: /** `.impeccable/design.json`, as documented in reference/document.md Step 4b. */
21: export const DESIGN_SIDECAR_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2;
22: /**
23:  * Sections init.md added in v4. A PRODUCT.md carrying none of them, and no
24:  * stamp, predates the current record. Used only as a fallback: an explicit
25:  * stamp always wins.
26:  */
27: export const PRODUCT_V4_SECTIONS = Object.freeze([
28:   'Positioning',
29:   'Operating Context',
30:   'Evidence on Hand',
31:   'Product Principles',
32: ]);
33: /**
34:  * Headings Impeccable used to read and no longer does, with the reason. The
35:  * agent needs the reason: told only that a field is deprecated it tends to
36:  * preserve it "just in case", which is how a v3 register value keeps steering
37:  * v4 output.
38:  */
39: export const PRODUCT_DEPRECATED_SECTIONS = Object.freeze({
40:   Register: 'v4 replaced the brand/product register axis with the four visitor modes '
41:     + '(Persuade, Operate, Read, Experience), which are chosen per surface and persisted in that '
42:     + "surface's brief. Nothing reads `## Register` any more.",
43: });
44: const PRODUCT_STAMP_RE = /^[ \t]*<!--[ \t]*impeccable:product-schema[ \t]+(\d+)[ \t]*-->[ \t]*$/im;
45: /** The literal stamp line, for the init template and for migrations. */
46: export function productStampLine(version = PRODUCT_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
47:   return `<!-- impeccable:product-schema ${version} -->`;
48: }
49: /**
50:  * Schema version stamped in a PRODUCT.md body, or null when unstamped. Null
51:  * means "written before stamping existed", not "invalid".
52:  */
53: export function readProductSchemaVersion(markdown) {
54:   const match = String(markdown || '').match(PRODUCT_STAMP_RE);
55:   if (!match) return null;
56:   const version = Number.parseInt(match[1], 10);
57:   return Number.isInteger(version) ? version : null;
58: }
59: /**
60:  * Add or update the stamp, returning the new body. Idempotent. A stamped file
61:  * keeps the stamp where it already sits so a migration never reorders the
62:  * user's prose; an unstamped file gets it directly under the leading `#`
63:  * heading, or at the top when there is none.
64:  */
65: export function stampProductSchema(markdown, version = PRODUCT_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
66:   const body = String(markdown || '');
67:   const line = productStampLine(version);
68:   if (PRODUCT_STAMP_RE.test(body)) return body.replace(PRODUCT_STAMP_RE, line);
69:   const lines = body.split('\n');
70:   const headingIndex = lines.findIndex((entry) => /^#\s+\S/.test(entry));
71:   if (headingIndex === -1) return `${line}\n\n${body.replace(/^\n+/, '')}`;
72:   lines.splice(headingIndex + 1, 0, '', line);
73:   return lines.join('\n');
74: }
75: /**
76:  * Schema version of a parsed design.json. Returns null for a missing or
77:  * non-numeric field, which is how schemaVersion-1-era sidecars present
78:  * (the field predates the v2 rewrite in some files).
79:  */

81:   const version = sidecar && typeof sidecar === 'object' ? sidecar.schemaVersion : null;

83: }
````

````javascript
321:       errors.push(`review ${id} breadth must be one of ${[...CONCEPT_BREADTHS].join(', ')}`);

330:       } else if (review.allowedModes.some(mode => !SEED_MODES.has(mode))) {

334:       } else if (review.allowedModes.length === SEED_MODES.size) {
335:         errors.push(`review ${id} allowedModes lists every mode; omit the field instead`);

340:   const approved = concepts.filter(concept => reviewData?.reviews?.[concept.id]?.status === 'approved');
341:   const approvedTiers = new Set(

345:       .filter(tier => WELL_TIERS.includes(tier))

351:   return {

353:     warnings,
354:     stats: {

356:       families: familyIds.size,
357:       concepts: concepts.length,
358:       approved: approved.length,
359:       pending: concepts.length - Object.keys(reviewData?.reviews || {}).length,
360:       rejected: Object.values(reviewData?.reviews || {}).filter(review => review?.status === 'rejected').length,
361:     },

364: export function approvedPoolRevision(concepts) {
365:   const payload = concepts
366:     .filter(concept => concept.status === 'approved')
367:     .map(concept => `${concept.familyId}:${concept.id}:${concept.strength}:${concept.form}:${concept.spark}:${JSON.stringify(concept.system)}:${concept.webLeverage}`)
368:     .sort()
369:     .join('\n');
370:   return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(payload).digest('hex').slice(0, 12);
````

````javascript
638: function extractComponents(section) {

701: // ---------- Coverage assessment ----------
702: // Sections whose model is description-plus-rules only (see extractGuidance).
703: const guidanceCoverage = (guidance) =>
704:   guidance
705:     ? {
706:         description: Boolean(guidance.description),
707:         rules: guidance.rules.length,
708:       }

710: function assessCoverage(model) {
711:   const report = {};
712:   report.overview = model.overview
713:     ? {
714:         northStar: Boolean(model.overview.creativeNorthStar),
715:         philosophy: model.overview.philosophy.length > 0,
716:         keyCharacteristics: model.overview.keyCharacteristics.length,
717:       }
718:     : 'missing';
719:   report.colors = model.colors
720:     ? {
721:         groups: model.colors.groups.length,
722:         totalColors: model.colors.groups.reduce((n, g) => n + g.colors.length, 0),
723:         rules: model.colors.rules.length,
724:       }
725:     : 'missing';
726:   report.typography = model.typography
727:     ? {
728:         fonts: Object.keys(model.typography.fonts).length,
729:         hierarchyEntries: model.typography.hierarchy.length,
730:         character: Boolean(model.typography.character),
731:         rules: model.typography.rules.length,
732:       }
733:     : 'missing';
734:   report.layout = guidanceCoverage(model.layout);
735:   report.elevation = model.elevation
736:     ? {
737:         shadows: model.elevation.shadows.length,
738:         rules: model.elevation.rules.length,
739:         description: Boolean(model.elevation.description),
740:       }
741:     : 'missing';
742:   report.shapes = guidanceCoverage(model.shapes);
743:   report.components = model.components
744:     ? {
745:         count: model.components.components.length,
746:         variantTotal: model.components.components.reduce((n, c) => n + c.variants.length, 0),
747:       }
748:     : 'missing';
749:   report.dosDonts = model.dosDonts
750:     ? {
751:         dos: model.dosDonts.dos.length,
752:         donts: model.dosDonts.donts.length,
753:       }
754:     : 'missing';
755:   return report;
756: }
757: // ---------- Main ----------
758: export function parseDesignMd(md) {
759:   const { frontmatter, body } = parseFrontmatter(md);
760:   const { title, sections } = splitSections(body);
761:   return {
762:     schemaVersion: 2,
763:     title,
764:     frontmatter,
765:     overview: extractOverview(sections['Overview']),
766:     colors: extractColors(sections['Colors']),
767:     typography: extractTypography(sections['Typography']),
768:     layout: extractGuidance(sections['Layout']),
769:     elevation: extractElevation(sections['Elevation']),
770:     shapes: extractGuidance(sections['Shapes']),
771:     components: extractComponents(sections['Components']),
772:     dosDonts: extractDosDonts(sections["Do's and Don'ts"]),
773:   };
774: }
775: export { assessCoverage };
````

````javascript
  2:  * font-fingerprint: size-invariant, text-robust shape features for lettering
  3:  * in a raster (a comp crop or a rendered sample). fingerprint(img) returns the
  4:  * feature vector; distance(a, b) compares two vectors over noise-normalized,
  5:  * weighted features. Used by font-match.mjs (comp measurement and ranking)
  6:  * and by the catalog index build (scripts/build-font-index.mjs at the repo root). Depends only on
  7:  * lib/image-metrics.mjs and lib/raster.mjs.
  8:  *
  9:  * Every measure is taken per text line and normalized by R, the line's
 10:  * reference height (median of the tallest column heights above the baseline:
 11:  * the cap line on an all-caps line, the ascender line on a mixed line), so
 12:  * the same face gives the same numbers at any point size; per-glyph measures
 13:  * are medians so the numbers survive a change of text. Small crops are
 14:  * upsampled (bilinear) so R is at least 24px, and stroke runs are measured
 15:  * with antialiased edge pixels counted by coverage, so stem widths do not
 16:  * fatten at small sizes.
 17:  *
 18:  * Features (all in R units unless noted; null when not measurable):
 19:  *   advance/advTall/advX  median glyph width over baseline glyphs / tall glyphs / x-height glyphs
 20:  *   advCV                 spread of glyph widths (std/median): mono ~0.15, sans ~0.3, script > 0.5
 21:  *   gap                   median inter-glyph gap
 22:  *   xRatio                x-line / R (null on all-caps lines)
 23:  *   descRatio             descender depth (90th pct)
 24:  *   stemW                 median horizontal ink run in the x band (stem width)
 25:  *   contrast              stem width / median thin (vertical) run: didone high, grotesque ~1
 26:  *   serif                 foot width / mid-stem width on stems that reach the baseline
 27:  *   roundFrac             fraction of glyphs with bbox aspect > 0.9
 28:  *   densTall / densX      ink / bbox area for tall / x-height glyphs (weight)
 29:  *   runDensity            horizontal ink runs per row per R of line width (stroke busyness)
 30:  *   vprof0..9             normalized vertical ink profile from 0.35R below baseline to 1.05R above

 45:   let sumB = 0, wB = 0, best = 0, thr = 128;
 46:   for (let t = 0; t < 256; t++) {

160: function modeOf(vals, tol) {
161:   let best = null, bestC = -1;
162:   const s = [...vals].sort((a, b) => a - b);
163:   let j = 0;
164:   for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
165:     while (s[i] - s[j] > tol) j++;
166:     const c = i - j + 1;
167:     if (c > bestC) { bestC = c; best = (s[i] + s[j]) / 2; }
168:   }
169:   return { v: best, n: bestC };
170: }
171: /**

173:  * be separable. baseline = mode of column bottoms. R (the reference height)
174:  * is the top line of the tallest cluster: the cap line on an all-caps line,
175:  * the ascender line (or the cap line when caps are taller) on a mixed line.
176:  * The x-line is a second mode of column heights well below R; when there is

178:  */
179: function lineMetrics(bin, ln) {
180:   const { W, ink, cov } = bin;
181:   const cols = [];
182:   for (let x = 0; x < W; x++) {
183:     let top = -1, bot = -1;
184:     for (let yy = ln.y0; yy < ln.y1; yy++) if (ink[yy * W + x]) { if (top < 0) top = yy; bot = yy + 1; }
185:     if (top < 0) continue;

187:     const t = top > 0 ? top - cov((top - 1) * W + x) : top;
188:     const b = bot < bin.H ? bot + cov(bot * W + x) : bot;
189:     cols.push({ x, top: t, bot: b });
190:   }
191:   if (cols.length < 8) return null;
192:   const roughH = pct(cols.map((c) => c.bot - c.top), 0.9);
193:   const tol = Math.max(1, Math.round(roughH * 0.04));
194:   const baseF = modeOf(cols.map((c) => c.bot), tol).v;
195:   const base = Math.round(baseF);
196:   const hs = cols.filter((c) => c.bot <= baseF + tol * 1.5).map((c) => baseF - c.top).filter((h) => h > 0);

204:   if (lowHs.length >= Math.max(6, hs.length * 0.12)) {

208:   const dsc = cols.filter((c) => c.bot > baseF + tol * 1.5 && c.top < baseF - R * 0.3).map((c) => (c.bot - baseF) / R);

212: /** Glyph boxes: column runs of ink inside the x band, so ascender/descender bridges do not merge letters. */
213: function segment(bin, ln, m) {
214:   const { W, ink } = bin;
215:   const bandTop = Math.max(ln.y0, Math.round(m.base - (m.xh || m.cap * 0.6)));

350: /**
351:  * fingerprint(img) -> features, or null when no lettering is found. Upsamples (bilinear) when the
352:  * cap height is under 24px so runs and edges are measured on finer pixels.
353:  */
354: /**
355:  * Keep the dominant lettering in a region crop: the lines whose cap height is
356:  * within `tol` of the tallest, clipped horizontally to their own ink. A comp
357:  * region drawn on a 10x10 grid over-covers: the headline crop carries the
358:  * first line of body copy below it and a slice of the neighbouring column,
359:  * and every one of those small letters pulls stem width, run lengths and the
360:  * x-height vote toward a lighter, wider face. Returns { lines, x0, x1 } in
361:  * the binarized image, or null when nothing survives.
362:  */
363: export function isolateDominant(bin, lines, { tol = 0.28 } = {}) {
364:   const ms = lines.map((ln) => ({ ln, m: lineMetrics(bin, ln) })).filter((x) => x.m);
365:   if (!ms.length) return null;
366:   // The dominant class is the one holding most of the ink, not the tallest
367:   // line: a body-copy crop that clips the last line of the headline above it
368:   // is body copy. Cluster caps within tol of each other and pick the cluster
369:   // with the most ink mass; the tallest wins only a tie.
370:   const clusters = [];
371:   for (const x of [...ms].sort((a, b) => b.m.cap - a.m.cap)) {
372:     const c = clusters.find((cl) => Math.abs(cl.cap - x.m.cap) <= cl.cap * tol);
373:     if (c) { c.items.push(x); c.mass += x.ln.mass || 0; } else clusters.push({ cap: x.m.cap, items: [x], mass: x.ln.mass || 0 });
374:   }
375:   // Mass per line-height, so one heavy display line does not outvote five
376:   // lines of body copy; and a cluster of a single clipped line never wins
377:   // over a cluster of three or more.
378:   for (const c of clusters) { c.rows = c.items.reduce((n, x) => n + (x.ln.y1 - x.ln.y0), 0); c.density = c.mass / Math.max(1, c.rows); c.n = c.items.length; }

381:     if (aMulti !== bMulti) return aMulti ? -1 : 1;
382:     return (b.mass - a.mass) || (b.cap - a.cap);
383:   });
384:   const keep = clusters[0].items;
385:   const capMax = Math.max(...keep.map((x) => x.m.cap));
386:   // horizontal extent of the kept lines' tallest ink columns only: a small
387:   // column of body text beside the headline shares its rows but not its height
388:   const { W, ink } = bin;
389:   let x0 = W, x1 = 0;
390:   for (const { ln, m } of keep) {

407: function maskOutside(bin, x0, x1, lines) {
408:   const { W, H, ink, covA } = bin;
409:   const keepRow = new Uint8Array(H);
410:   for (const ln of lines) for (let y = ln.y0; y < ln.y1; y++) keepRow[y] = 1;

415:   }
416:   return { ...bin, ink: ink2, covA: cov2, cov: (i) => cov2[i] };

418: export function fingerprint(img, { minCap = 24, minGlyphs = 3, isolate = true } = {}) {
419:   let bin = binarize(img);
420:   let { lines } = findLines(bin);
421:   if (!lines.length) return null;
422:   let isolated = 0;
423:   if (isolate && lines.length > 1) {
424:     const iso = isolateDominant(bin, lines);
425:     if (iso && (iso.dropped > 0 || iso.x1 - iso.x0 < bin.W * 0.9)) {
426:       bin = maskOutside(bin, iso.x0, iso.x1, iso.lines);
427:       lines = iso.lines;
428:       isolated = iso.dropped;
429:     }
430:   }
431:   let f = measure(bin, lines);
432:   // fewer than minGlyphs separable glyphs is not lettering (a rule, a solid
433:   // bar, one letterform): callers read null as "no separable lettering"
434:   if (!f || f.glyphs < minGlyphs) return null;
435:   let scale = 1;
436:   if (f.capHeightPx < minCap && f.capHeightPx >= 4) {
437:     scale = Math.min(4, Math.ceil(minCap / f.capHeightPx));
438:     const up = resize(img, img.width * scale, img.height * scale);
439:     bin = binarize(up);
440:     lines = findLines(bin).lines;
441:     // the upsample re-reads the whole crop: isolate again so the clipped
442:     // headline or the drawing does not come back at scale
443:     if (isolate && lines.length > 1) {
444:       const iso2 = isolateDominant(bin, lines);
445:       if (iso2 && (iso2.dropped > 0 || iso2.x1 - iso2.x0 < bin.W * 0.9)) { bin = maskOutside(bin, iso2.x0, iso2.x1, iso2.lines); lines = iso2.lines; isolated = Math.max(isolated, iso2.dropped); }

450:   }
451:   const r = { lines: lines.length, glyphs: f.glyphs, capHeightPx: +(f.capHeightPx / scale).toFixed(1), inkIsDark: bin.inkIsDark, upsampled: scale > 1, allCaps: f.allCaps, isolatedFrom: isolated, weight: f.densTall == null && f.densX == null ? null : +(f.densTall ?? f.densX).toFixed(4) };

453:   return r;
454: }

501: /** Weighted L1 over z-scored features; a feature missing on either side is skipped and the weight mass renormalized. */
502: /**
503:  * The two readings a designer makes before any detail: how wide, how heavy.
504:  * Width from the advance of tall glyphs (all-caps crops) or x-height glyphs;
505:  * weight from ink density of tall glyphs. Both are on the same scale in the

507:  * adds a penalty that grows with the ratio's log: a face 50% wider or 35%
508:  * lighter than the comp cannot rank above one that is right on both, whatever

538:   if (!wsum) return Infinity;
539:   const v = d / wsum;
540:   return p === 1 ? v : Math.sqrt(v);

543: export function _debugLines(img) {
544:   const bin = binarize(img);

547: }
````

````javascript
  5:  *
  6:  * File: skill/scripts/data/font-index.json

  8:  *     schema: 1,
  9:  *     text: "<index text every face was rendered with>",
 10:  *     sizes: [48, 14],            // cap heights (px) the catalog was rendered at
 11:  *     features: [...],            // feature names, in vector order (the fitted-nonzero subset of FEATURES)
 12:  *     categories: ["sans", ...],  // category index -> name
 13:  *     entries: [[family, weight, categoryIdx, variable(0|1), vec48, vec14], ...]
 14:  *   }
 15:  * A vector is a string of 3-char base-36 numbers, one per feature, each the
 16:  * feature value x 1000 (three decimals, clipped at 46.655); "___" is null.
 17:  * That packing keeps ~3,000 faces x 2 sizes x 33 features under 750 KB on
 18:  * disk, which is what makes it shippable inside the skill without gzip.
 19:  *
 20:  * Two sizes because the fingerprint's features are stable within a factor of
 21:  * ~2 in size but not from 48px down to 14px: a crop is routed to the index
 22:  * rendered nearer its own cap height (ROUTE_CAP_PX is the boundary).
 23:  */

 25: import path from 'node:path';
 26: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
 27: import { FEATURES, STATS, distance } from './font-fingerprint.mjs';
 28: export const INDEX_PATH = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', 'data', 'font-index.json');
 29: /** Cap heights the catalog is rendered at. `48c` is the same 48px cap in ALL
 30:  *  CAPS text (schema 2), queried for caps crops; a schema-1 index without it
 31:  *  routes caps crops to the mixed-case 48 as before. */
 32: export const INDEX_SIZES = [48, 14, '48c'];
 33: /** Crops with a cap height under this many px query the 14px index. */
 34: export const ROUTE_CAP_PX = 22;
 35: /** Below this cap height the fingerprint is not trustworthy; callers size by the box instead. */
 36: export const MIN_RANK_CAP_PX = 10;

 43: export function packVector(fp, features = INDEX_FEATURES) {
 44:   return features.map((k) => {
 45:     const v = fp?.[k];
 46:     if (v == null || !Number.isFinite(v)) return NULL_TOKEN;
 47:     return Math.min(MAX_Q, Math.max(0, Math.round(v * 1000))).toString(36).padStart(3, '0');
 48:   }).join('');

 51:   const out = {};

 66:   if (!fs.existsSync(file)) return null;
 67:   const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
 68:   const features = raw.features || INDEX_FEATURES;

 90:  */
 91: /**

 93:  * text, dingbats, symbol fonts, and effect faces (outlines, shades, glitch,
 94:  * pixel, 3D) whose fingerprint lands near heavy condensed text without being

100:   if (!fp || !index) return [];
101:   const size = routeSize(fp.capHeightPx, index.sizes, { allCaps: !!fp.allCaps });
102:   const wantCat = category ? String(category).split(',').map((s) => s.trim().toLowerCase()).filter(Boolean) : null;
103:   const scored = [];
104:   for (const e of index.entries) {
105:     if (wantCat && !wantCat.includes(e.category)) continue;
106:     if (!includeNonText && NON_TEXT_FAMILY.test(e.family)) continue;
107:     const v = e.fp[size];
108:     if (!v) continue;
109:     const d = distance(fp, v);
110:     if (!Number.isFinite(d)) continue;
111:     scored.push({ family: e.family, weight: e.weight, category: e.category, variable: e.variable, d, size });
112:   }
113:   scored.sort((a, b) => a.d - b.d);
114:   const perFam = new Map(); const out = [];
115:   for (const s of scored) {
116:     const c = perFam.get(s.family) || 0;
117:     if (c >= perFamily) continue;
118:     perFam.set(s.family, c + 1); out.push(s);
119:     if (out.length >= n) break;
120:   }
121:   return out;
122: }
````

````javascript
  1: /**
  2:  * Hero-gate checks that name a miss as a number the model can act on.
  3:  *
  4:  * comp-diff scores regions; these read what a designer reads when the two
  5:  * frames sit side by side and says it as numbers: the headline is set at
  6:  * cap 78px where the comp's is 103; it wraps to four lines where the comp
  7:  * has three; its ink is #2a2a2a where the comp's is #a72f1b; it starts
  8:  * 60px lower in its box; the masthead is 92px tall where the comp's is 58;
  9:  * these grid cells carry ink the comp does not have (a kicker, a divider, a
 10:  * second nav row). Every one of those was a pin in the first human review
 11:  * of the third sweep, on builds the region scores had already let through.

'+' : ''}${Math.round(capDelta * 100)}%); set font-size so the cap height renders at ${comp.capHeightPx}px${region.type.chosen ? ` (font-match ranked ${region.type.chosen.family} ${region.type.chosen.weight} at ${region.type.chosen.fontSizePx}px)` : ''}`);

102:     const dx = bb.x - ba.x;
103:     if (Math.abs(dx) > Math.max(12, compCrop.width * 0.15)) findings.push(`text ${region.id}: it starts ${Math.abs(Math.round(dx))}px ${dx > 0 ? 'further right' : 'further left'} than in the comp`);

108: /**
109:  * Rows of a crop that carry a horizontal rule: a row whose gray step from
110:  * the row above (or below) is strong across at least `span` of the width.

176:     // alignment) reads as invented otherwise
177:     let neighbourhood = 0, n = 0;
178:     for (let dr = -1; dr <= 1; dr++) for (let dc = -1; dc <= 1; dc++) { const rr = r + dr, cc = c + dc; if (rr < 0 || cc < 0 || rr >= rows || cc >= cols) continue; neighbourhood += a.cells[rr * cols + cc]; n++; }
179:     if (neighbourhood / n >= floor * 2) continue;
180:     cells.push({ col: c, row: r, label: `${String.fromCharCode(65 + c)}${r}`, comp: +a.cells[i].toFixed(1), build: +b.cells[i].toFixed(1) });
181:   }
182:   return { cells, fraction: cells.length / (cols * rows) };
183: }
184: /**
185:  * A plate cropped by its box: the comp's artwork keeps a margin inside the
186:  * region on some side and the build's ink runs flush to that edge (object-fit:
187:  * cover on a box smaller than the artwork's aspect, or an <img> sized to the
188:  * column). The best build of the fifth sweep passed the hero at 87% with the
189:  * cover arch cut off at the left and bottom; the human review called it a
190:  * bug in one word. Returns the sides clipped, or [].
191:  */
192: export function plateClipCheck(region, compCrop, buildCrop, { margin = 6 } = {}) {
193:   const a = inkBox(compCrop), b = inkBox(buildCrop);
194:   if (!a || !b) return { sides: [] };
195:   const W = compCrop.width, H = compCrop.height;
196:   const sides = [];
197:   const flush = (v) => v <= 1;
198:   if (a.x >= margin && flush(b.x)) sides.push('left');
199:   if (a.y >= margin && flush(b.y)) sides.push('top');
200:   if (W - (a.x + a.w) >= margin && flush(W - (b.x + b.w))) sides.push('right');
201:   if (H - (a.y + a.h) >= margin && flush(H - (b.y + b.h))) sides.push('bottom');
202:   return { sides, comp: a, build: b };
203: }
204: /**
205:  * Inline SVG that is an illustration, not an icon. An icon is small (a
206:  * viewBox or box under `iconPx` on its long side) with a few paths; anything
207:  * with a real path budget is a drawing in code: a diagram, a rack of
208:  * carburetors, staff notation, leader lines with arrows, a "terrible svg
209:  * approximation of the asset". Those ship as plates or as part of the plate
210:  * they annotate. Returns one entry per offending <svg> with a snippet.
211:  *
212:  * `html` is the artifact source. `pathBudget` counts characters of path
213:  * data (d="..."), points, and polyline/polygon points across the element.
214:  */
215: export function svgIllustrations(html, { iconPx = 64, pathBudget = 480, maxPaths = 8 } = {}) {
216:   const out = [];
217:   const re = /<svg\b([^>]*)>([\s\S]*?)<\/svg>/gi;
218:   let m;
219:   while ((m = re.exec(html))) {
220:     const attrs = m[1], body = m[2];
221:     const paths = (body.match(/<path\b/gi) || []).length + (body.match(/<(polyline|polygon|line|circle|ellipse|rect)\b/gi) || []).length;
222:     let budget = 0;
223:     for (const d of body.matchAll(/\sd="([^"]*)"/g)) budget += d[1].length;
224:     for (const pts of body.matchAll(/\spoints="([^"]*)"/g)) budget += pts[1].length;
225:     const vb = /viewBox="\s*[-\d.]+\s+[-\d.]+\s+([\d.]+)\s+([\d.]+)/.exec(attrs);
226:     const w = /\swidth="([\d.]+)(px)?"/.exec(attrs), h = /\sheight="([\d.]+)(px)?"/.exec(attrs);
227:     const long = Math.max(vb ? Math.max(+vb[1], +vb[2]) : 0, w ? +w[1] : 0, h ? +h[1] : 0);
228:     const iconSized = long > 0 && long <= iconPx && paths <= maxPaths;
229:     const uses = /<use\b/i.test(body) && paths === 0; // a sprite reference
230:     if (uses) continue;
231:     if (iconSized && budget <= pathBudget) continue;
232:     if (budget <= pathBudget && paths <= maxPaths && long === 0 && !/<(text|image)\b/i.test(body)) continue; // a tiny inline glyph with no size hint
233:     if (budget > pathBudget || paths > maxPaths || (long > iconPx && paths > 0)) {
234:       const id = /\b(id|class|aria-label|data-region)="([^"]+)"/i.exec(attrs);
235:       out.push({ snippet: `<svg${attrs.slice(0, 80).replace(/\s+/g, ' ')}...> (${paths} shapes, ${budget} chars of path data${long ? `, ${long}px` : ''})`, label: id ? id[2] : null, paths, budget, long });
236:     }
237:   }
238:   return out;
239: }
````

````javascript
  1: /**
  2:  * Perceptual measures for comparing a comp with a build screenshot. Pure
  3:  * functions over `{ width, height, data }` RGBA images; no I/O.
  4:  *
  5:  * Three families, because a build fails a comp in three separable ways:
  6:  *
  7:  * - structure: is the composition the same? Measured as SSIM over a blurred
  8:  *   grayscale downsample, which forgives font hinting and a few pixels of
  9:  *   drift and punishes a moved, missing, or invented region.
 10:  * - color: is the palette and its distribution the same? Histogram
 11:  *   intersection in a coarse quantized space plus a dominant-color extraction,
 12:  *   so a navy page built from a bone comp fails even if the shapes match.
 13:  * - detail: is the material there? Local high-frequency energy per cell. A
 14:  *   comp with an illustration, texture, or photograph carries energy a flat
 15:  *   CSS stand-in does not; the ratio build/comp per region is the most direct
 16:  *   measure of "the plate got replaced by a gradient".
 17:  */
 18: import { resize } from './raster.mjs';
 19: export function toGray(img) {
 20:   const g = new Float32Array(img.width * img.height);
 21:   for (let i = 0, p = 0; i < g.length; i++, p += 4) {
 22:     const a = img.data[p + 3] / 255;
 23:     // composite over white so transparent regions read as the page ground
 24:     const r = img.data[p] * a + 255 * (1 - a), gg = img.data[p + 1] * a + 255 * (1 - a), b = img.data[p + 2] * a + 255 * (1 - a);

 26:   }
 27:   return { width: img.width, height: img.height, data: g };
 28: }
 29: /** Separable box blur on a float gray image, radius r. */
 30: export function blurGray(gray, r) {
 31:   if (r <= 0) return gray;
 32:   const { width, height, data } = gray;
 33:   const tmp = new Float32Array(data.length), out = new Float32Array(data.length);
 34:   const win = 2 * r + 1;
 35:   for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
 36:     let acc = 0;
 37:     for (let x = -r; x <= r; x++) acc += data[y * width + Math.min(width - 1, Math.max(0, x))];
 38:     for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) {
 39:       tmp[y * width + x] = acc / win;
 40:       const outX = x - r, inX = x + r + 1;
 41:       acc += data[y * width + Math.min(width - 1, inX)] - data[y * width + Math.max(0, outX)];
 42:     }
 43:   }
 44:   for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) {
 45:     let acc = 0;
 46:     for (let y = -r; y <= r; y++) acc += tmp[Math.min(height - 1, Math.max(0, y)) * width + x];
 47:     for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
 48:       out[y * width + x] = acc / win;
 49:       const outY = y - r, inY = y + r + 1;
 50:       acc += tmp[Math.min(height - 1, inY) * width + x] - tmp[Math.max(0, outY) * width + x];
 51:     }
 52:   }
 53:   return { width, height, data: out };

 55: /** Global SSIM between two same-size gray images using an 8x8 window grid. */
 56: export function ssim(a, b, win = 8) {
 57:   if (a.width !== b.width || a.height !== b.height) throw new Error('ssim: size mismatch');
 58:   const C1 = (0.01 * 255) ** 2, C2 = (0.03 * 255) ** 2;
 59:   let total = 0, n = 0;
 60:   for (let y = 0; y + win <= a.height; y += win) {
 61:     for (let x = 0; x + win <= a.width; x += win) {
 62:       let ma = 0, mb = 0;
 63:       for (let yy = 0; yy < win; yy++) for (let xx = 0; xx < win; xx++) { const i = (y + yy) * a.width + x + xx; ma += a.data[i]; mb += b.data[i]; }
 64:       ma /= win * win; mb /= win * win;
 65:       let va = 0, vb = 0, cov = 0;
 66:       for (let yy = 0; yy < win; yy++) for (let xx = 0; xx < win; xx++) { const i = (y + yy) * a.width + x + xx; const da = a.data[i] - ma, db = b.data[i] - mb; va += da * da; vb += db * db; cov += da * db; }

 68:       total += ((2 * ma * mb + C1) * (2 * cov + C2)) / ((ma * ma + mb * mb + C1) * (va + vb + C2));
 69:       n++;

 74: /** SSIM of `a` against `b` shifted by (dx, dy); the overlap is compared, edges dropped. */
 75: export function ssimShifted(a, b, dx, dy, win = 8) {
 76:   const w = a.width - Math.abs(dx), h = a.height - Math.abs(dy);
 77:   if (w < win || h < win) return 0;
 78:   const sa = { width: w, height: h, data: new Float32Array(w * h) };
 79:   const sb = { width: w, height: h, data: new Float32Array(w * h) };
 80:   const ax = Math.max(0, -dx), ay = Math.max(0, -dy), bx = Math.max(0, dx), by = Math.max(0, dy);
 81:   for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
 82:     sa.data.set(a.data.subarray((y + ay) * a.width + ax, (y + ay) * a.width + ax + w), y * w);
 83:     sb.data.set(b.data.subarray((y + by) * b.width + bx, (y + by) * b.width + bx + w), y * w);
 84:   }
 85:   return ssim(sa, sb, win);
 86: }
 87: /**
 88:  * Structure score 0..1: SSIM over blurred grayscale at a fixed working width,
 89:  * taking the best of a small translation search so a composition that sits a
 90:  * few pixels off (a different masthead height, a scrollbar) is not read as a
 91:  * different composition. Shifts up to ~4% of the width are forgiven; a moved
 92:  * region is not.
 93:  */
 94: export function structureScore(imgA, imgB, workWidth = 256) {
 95:   const h = Math.max(8, Math.round((imgA.height / imgA.width) * workWidth));
 96:   const a = blurGray(toGray(resize(imgA, workWidth, h)), 2);
 97:   const b = blurGray(toGray(resize(imgB, workWidth, h)), 2);
 98:   const win = Math.min(8, Math.max(2, Math.floor(Math.min(workWidth, h) / 8)));
 99:   let best = ssim(a, b, win);
100:   const maxShift = Math.max(2, Math.round(workWidth * 0.04));
101:   for (const dy of [-maxShift, -maxShift / 2, 0, maxShift / 2, maxShift]) {
102:     for (const dx of [-maxShift, -maxShift / 2, 0, maxShift / 2, maxShift]) {
103:       if (!dx && !dy) continue;
104:       best = Math.max(best, ssimShifted(a, b, Math.round(dx), Math.round(dy), win));
105:     }
106:   }
107:   return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, best));
108: }
109: // ---- color -----------------------------------------------------------------
110: function rgbToLab(r, g, b) {
111:   const lin = (c) => { c /= 255; return c <= 0.04045 ? c / 12.92 : ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4; };
112:   const R = lin(r), G = lin(g), B = lin(b);
113:   const X = (R * 0.4124 + G * 0.3576 + B * 0.1805) / 0.95047;
114:   const Y = (R * 0.2126 + G * 0.7152 + B * 0.0722) / 1.0;
115:   const Z = (R * 0.0193 + G * 0.1192 + B * 0.9505) / 1.08883;
116:   const f = (t) => (t > 0.008856 ? Math.cbrt(t) : 7.787 * t + 16 / 116);
117:   const fx = f(X), fy = f(Y), fz = f(Z);
118:   return [116 * fy - 16, 500 * (fx - fy), 200 * (fy - fz)];
119: }
120: export function deltaE(lab1, lab2) {
121:   return Math.hypot(lab1[0] - lab2[0], lab1[1] - lab2[1], lab1[2] - lab2[2]);
122: }
123: /** Quantized color histogram (4 bits per channel = 4096 bins), normalized. */
124: export function colorHistogram(img, sampleStep = 2) {
125:   const bins = new Float32Array(4096);
126:   let n = 0;
127:   for (let y = 0; y < img.height; y += sampleStep) {
128:     for (let x = 0; x < img.width; x += sampleStep) {
129:       const p = (y * img.width + x) * 4;
130:       if (img.data[p + 3] < 16) continue;
131:       const key = ((img.data[p] >> 4) << 8) | ((img.data[p + 1] >> 4) << 4) | (img.data[p + 2] >> 4);
132:       bins[key]++; n++;
133:     }
134:   }
135:   if (n) for (let i = 0; i < bins.length; i++) bins[i] /= n;
136:   return bins;
137: }
138: export function histogramIntersection(h1, h2) {
139:   let s = 0;
140:   for (let i = 0; i < h1.length; i++) s += Math.min(h1[i], h2[i]);
141:   return s;
142: }
143: /**
144:  * Dominant colors: merge histogram bins greedily by Lab distance into up to
145:  * `k` clusters and return them sorted by coverage.
146:  */
147: export function dominantColors(img, k = 6, sampleStep = 3) {
148:   const hist = colorHistogram(img, sampleStep);
149:   const entries = [];
150:   for (let i = 0; i < hist.length; i++) if (hist[i] > 0.0005) entries.push({ key: i, w: hist[i] });
151:   entries.sort((a, b) => b.w - a.w);
152:   const clusters = [];
153:   for (const e of entries) {
154:     const r = ((e.key >> 8) & 15) * 16 + 8, g = ((e.key >> 4) & 15) * 16 + 8, b = (e.key & 15) * 16 + 8;
155:     const lab = rgbToLab(r, g, b);
156:     let best = null, bestD = Infinity;
157:     for (const c of clusters) { const d = deltaE(c.lab, lab); if (d < bestD) { bestD = d; best = c; } }
158:     if (best && bestD < 14) {
159:       const tw = best.w + e.w;
160:       best.rgb = [(best.rgb[0] * best.w + r * e.w) / tw, (best.rgb[1] * best.w + g * e.w) / tw, (best.rgb[2] * best.w + b * e.w) / tw];
161:       best.lab = rgbToLab(...best.rgb); best.w = tw;
162:     } else clusters.push({ rgb: [r, g, b], lab, w: e.w });
163:   }
164:   clusters.sort((a, b) => b.w - a.w);
165:   const top = clusters.slice(0, k);
166:   const covered = top.reduce((s, c) => s + c.w, 0) || 1;
167:   return top.map((c) => ({ hex: toHex(c.rgb), coverage: +(c.w / covered).toFixed(4), lab: c.lab }));
168: }
169: export function toHex(rgb) {
170:   return '#' + rgb.map((v) => Math.max(0, Math.min(255, Math.round(v))).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
171: }
172: /**
173:  * Palette match 0..1: for each dominant comp color, coverage-weighted best
174:  * Lab match in the build's dominant set (dE 0 -> 1, dE >= 25 -> 0).
175:  */
176: export function paletteMatch(compColors, buildColors) {
177:   if (!compColors.length) return 1;
178:   let s = 0, wsum = 0;
179:   for (const c of compColors) {
180:     let best = Infinity;
181:     for (const b of buildColors) best = Math.min(best, deltaE(c.lab, b.lab));
182:     s += c.coverage * Math.max(0, 1 - best / 25); wsum += c.coverage;
183:   }
184:   return wsum ? s / wsum : 1;
185: }
186: /** Color score 0..1: blend of histogram intersection and dominant-palette match. */
187: export function colorScore(imgA, imgB) {
188:   const inter = histogramIntersection(colorHistogram(imgA), colorHistogram(imgB));
189:   const pm = paletteMatch(dominantColors(imgA), dominantColors(imgB));
190:   return { score: 0.35 * inter + 0.65 * pm, intersection: inter, paletteMatch: pm };
191: }
192: // ---- detail ----------------------------------------------------------------
193: /** Mean absolute gradient (Sobel-lite) per cell over a cols x rows grid. */
194: export function detailGrid(img, cols = 12, rows = 8, workWidth = 512) {
195:   const h = Math.max(rows, Math.round((img.height / img.width) * workWidth));
196:   const g = toGray(resize(img, workWidth, h));
197:   const grid = new Float32Array(cols * rows);
198:   const counts = new Float32Array(cols * rows);
199:   for (let y = 1; y < g.height - 1; y++) {
200:     const cy = Math.min(rows - 1, Math.floor((y / g.height) * rows));
201:     for (let x = 1; x < g.width - 1; x++) {
202:       const cx = Math.min(cols - 1, Math.floor((x / g.width) * cols));
203:       const i = y * g.width + x;
204:       const gx = Math.abs(g.data[i + 1] - g.data[i - 1]);
205:       const gy = Math.abs(g.data[i + g.width] - g.data[i - g.width]);
206:       grid[cy * cols + cx] += gx + gy; counts[cy * cols + cx]++;
207:     }
208:   }
209:   for (let i = 0; i < grid.length; i++) grid[i] = counts[i] ? grid[i] / counts[i] : 0;
210:   return { cols, rows, cells: grid };
211: }
212: /**
213:  * Detail score 0..1 and per-cell ratio. Cells where the comp is nearly flat
214:  * are ignored (nothing to lose); the score is the coverage-weighted mean of
215:  * min(1, build/comp) over cells with comp energy, so extra detail in the
216:  * build (invented chrome) is reported separately as `added`.
217:  */
218: export function detailScore(imgA, imgB, cols = 12, rows = 8) {
219:   const a = detailGrid(imgA, cols, rows), b = detailGrid(imgB, cols, rows);
220:   const floor = 1.5; // energy below this is a flat field at the 512px working width
221:   let s = 0, w = 0, added = 0, addedW = 0;
222:   const ratios = new Float32Array(cols * rows);
223:   for (let i = 0; i < a.cells.length; i++) {
224:     const ca = a.cells[i], cb = b.cells[i];
225:     ratios[i] = ca > floor ? cb / ca : (cb > floor ? Infinity : 1);
226:     // Signed: too much energy is as wrong as too little. Noise, a tile
227:     // shuffle, or a mosaic saturate a one-sided ratio; a real plate does not.
228:     if (ca > floor) { s += Math.min(cb / ca, ca / cb) * ca; w += ca; }
229:     if (cb > ca * 1.8 && cb > floor * 2) { added += 1; }
230:     addedW += 1;
231:   }
232:   const addedFraction = addedW ? added / addedW : 0;
233:   const raw = w ? s / w : 1;
234:   return { score: Math.max(0, raw - 0.5 * addedFraction), rawScore: raw, addedFraction, comp: a, build: b, ratios };
235: }
236: // ---- pixel diff -----------------------------------------------------------
237: /** Per-pixel Lab-ish difference map (0..1) at a working width; blurred a little. */
238: export function diffMap(imgA, imgB, workWidth = 384) {
239:   const h = Math.max(8, Math.round((imgA.height / imgA.width) * workWidth));
240:   const a = resize(imgA, workWidth, h), b = resize(imgB, workWidth, h);
241:   const out = new Float32Array(workWidth * h);
242:   for (let i = 0, p = 0; i < out.length; i++, p += 4) {
243:     const dr = a.data[p] - b.data[p], dg = a.data[p + 1] - b.data[p + 1], db = a.data[p + 2] - b.data[p + 2];
244:     out[i] = Math.min(1, Math.sqrt(dr * dr + dg * dg + db * db) / 200);
245:   }
246:   return blurGray({ width: workWidth, height: h, data: out }, 1);
247: }
248: // ---- bands (horizontal layout structure) ---------------------------------
249: /**
250:  * Detect horizontal band boundaries: rows where the mean color changes
251:  * sharply. Returns normalized y positions (0..1) with strengths. This is the
252:  * "layout grid" read of a page: header / hero / index / footer as bands.
253:  */
254: export function horizontalBands(img, workWidth = 128, minGap = 0.02) {
255:   const h = Math.max(16, Math.round((img.height / img.width) * workWidth));
256:   const s = resize(img, workWidth, h);
257:   const rowMean = new Float32Array(h * 3);
258:   for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
259:     let r = 0, g = 0, b = 0;
260:     for (let x = 0; x < workWidth; x++) { const p = (y * workWidth + x) * 4; r += s.data[p]; g += s.data[p + 1]; b += s.data[p + 2]; }
261:     rowMean[y * 3] = r / workWidth; rowMean[y * 3 + 1] = g / workWidth; rowMean[y * 3 + 2] = b / workWidth;
262:   }
263:   const edges = [];
264:   for (let y = 1; y < h; y++) {
265:     const d = Math.hypot(rowMean[y * 3] - rowMean[(y - 1) * 3], rowMean[y * 3 + 1] - rowMean[(y - 1) * 3 + 1], rowMean[y * 3 + 2] - rowMean[(y - 1) * 3 + 2]);
266:     if (d > 18) edges.push({ y: y / h, strength: Math.min(1, d / 120) });
267:   }
268:   // merge close edges
269:   const merged = [];
270:   for (const e of edges) {
271:     const last = merged[merged.length - 1];
272:     if (last && e.y - last.y < minGap) { if (e.strength > last.strength) { last.y = e.y; last.strength = e.strength; } }
273:     else merged.push({ ...e });
274:   }
275:   return merged;
276: }
277: /** Band agreement 0..1: fraction of comp bands with a build band within tolerance, and vice versa. */
278: export function bandScore(bandsA, bandsB, tol = 0.04) {
279:   if (!bandsA.length && !bandsB.length) return 1;
280:   const match = (from, to) => from.filter((a) => to.some((b) => Math.abs(a.y - b.y) <= tol)).length;
281:   const recall = bandsA.length ? match(bandsA, bandsB) / bandsA.length : 1;
282:   const precision = bandsB.length ? match(bandsB, bandsA) / bandsB.length : 1;
283:   return 0.6 * recall + 0.4 * precision;
284: }
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/lib/impeccable-config.mjs
````javascript
  1: /**
  2:  * CLI-side reader/writer for the unified `.impeccable` config.
  3:  *
  4:  * The CLI (published to npm) and the skill scripts (bundled into the install)
  5:  * live in separate trees and cannot share runtime code, so this duplicates a
  6:  * small slice of skill/scripts/hook-lib.mjs — the config-path layout, detector
  7:  * ignore semantics, and the `.git/info/exclude` handling. Keep the schema,
  8:  * ignore filtering, and exclude marker in sync if either side changes.
  9:  *
 10:  * Schema (config.json shared / config.local.json gitignored, per-developer):
 11:  *   {
 12:  *     "detector": { "ignoreRules": [], "ignoreFiles": [], "ignoreValues": [], "designSystem": { "enabled": true } },
 13:  *     "hook": { "consent": "accepted" | "declined", ... },
 14:  *     "updateCheck": bool
 15:  *   }
 16:  */
 17: import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
 18: import { join, dirname, isAbsolute, relative, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';
 19: export function getConfigPath(root) {
````

````javascript
 1: /**
 2:  * Decide whether a given file is "generated" (regenerated by a build step,
 3:  * unsafe to write variants into) or "source" (safe to edit, changes persist).
 4:  *
 5:  * Why this matters: when the user picks an element on a page whose underlying
 6:  * file is regenerated by a build step (e.g. `scripts/build-sub-pages.js`
 7:  * rewriting `public/docs/*.html`), writing variants or accepted changes into
 8:  * that file is silent data loss — the next build wipes them.
 9:  *
10:  * Signals, in order of reliability:
11:  *   1. Git check-ignore: gitignored files are assumed generated.
12:  *   2. File-header markers ("GENERATED", "DO NOT EDIT", "AUTO-GENERATED")
13:  *      within the first ~300 characters — catches non-git projects.
14:  */
15: import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
16: import fs from 'node:fs';
17: import path from 'node:path';
18: const HEADER_SCAN_BYTES = 300;
19: const HEADER_MARKERS = [
20:   /@generated\b/i,
21:   /\bGENERATED\s+FILE\b/,
22:   /\bAUTO-?GENERATED\b/i,
23:   /\bDO\s+NOT\s+EDIT\b/i,
24: ];
25: /**
26:  * @param {string} filePath - absolute or cwd-relative path
27:  * @param {object} [options]
28:  * @param {string} [options.cwd] - project root (defaults to process.cwd())
29:  */
30: export function isGeneratedFile(filePath, options = {}) {
31:   const cwd = options.cwd || process.cwd();
32:   const absPath = path.isAbsolute(filePath) ? filePath : path.resolve(cwd, filePath);
33:   if (isGitIgnored(absPath, cwd)) return true;
34:   if (hasGeneratedHeader(absPath)) return true;
35:   return false;
36: }
37: function isGitIgnored(absPath, cwd) {
38:   try {
39:     // argv form, never a shell: this runs on every file the live-mode source
40:     // walk reaches, so a hostile filename embedding $(...) or backticks must
41:     // not be interpretable (issue #476). JSON.stringify is not shell quoting.
42:     execFileSync('git', ['check-ignore', '--quiet', absPath], {
43:       cwd,
44:       stdio: 'ignore',
45:     });
46:     return true; // exit 0 = ignored
47:   } catch (err) {
48:     // Exit code 1 = not ignored. Exit code 128 = not a git repo or other error.
49:     // In both cases, treat as "not known to be ignored."
50:     return false;
51:   }
52: }
53: function hasGeneratedHeader(absPath) {
54:   let fd;
55:   try {
56:     fd = fs.openSync(absPath, 'r');
57:     const buf = Buffer.alloc(HEADER_SCAN_BYTES);
58:     const bytesRead = fs.readSync(fd, buf, 0, HEADER_SCAN_BYTES, 0);
59:     const head = buf.slice(0, bytesRead).toString('utf-8');
60:     return HEADER_MARKERS.some((re) => re.test(head));
61:   } catch {
62:     return false;
63:   } finally {
64:     if (fd !== undefined) { try { fs.closeSync(fd); } catch {} }
65:   }
66: }
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/lib/live-path-globs.mjs
````javascript
 1: /**
 2:  * Convert a live-config glob pattern to a RegExp.
 3:  *
 4:  * Supports `**` across path segments, `*` within one segment, and `?` for one
 5:  * character. Callers normalize project-relative paths to forward slashes.
 6:  */
 7: export function livePathGlobToRegex(pattern) {
 8:   let re = '';
 9:   let i = 0;
10:   while (i < pattern.length) {
11:     const c = pattern[i];
12:     if (c === '*') {
13:       if (pattern[i + 1] === '*') {
14:         if (pattern[i + 2] === '/') {
15:           re += '(?:.*/)?';
16:           i += 3;
17:         } else {
18:           re += '.*';
19:           i += 2;
20:         }
21:       } else {
22:         re += '[^/]*';
23:         i += 1;
24:       }
25:     } else if (c === '?') {
26:       re += '[^/]';
27:       i += 1;
28:     } else if (/[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/.test(c)) {
29:       re += `\\${c}`;
30:       i += 1;
31:     } else {
32:       re += c;
33:       i += 1;
34:     }
35:   }
36:   return new RegExp(`^${re}$`);
37: }
````

````javascript
218:   if (data.length !== width * height * 4) throw new Error(`png: data length ${data.length} != ${width}x${height}x4`);
219:   const stride = width * 4;
220:   const raw = Buffer.alloc((stride + 1) * height);
221:   for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
222:     raw[y * (stride + 1)] = 0;
223:     raw.set(data.subarray(y * stride, (y + 1) * stride), y * (stride + 1) + 1);
224:   }
225:   const ihdr = Buffer.alloc(13);
226:   ihdr.writeUInt32BE(width, 0);
227:   ihdr.writeUInt32BE(height, 4);
228:   ihdr[8] = 8; ihdr[9] = 6; ihdr[10] = 0; ihdr[11] = 0; ihdr[12] = 0;
229:   const parts = [SIGNATURE, chunk('IHDR', ihdr)];
230:   if (text) {
231:     for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(text)) {
232:       parts.push(chunk('tEXt', Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(k, 'latin1'), Buffer.from([0]), Buffer.from(String(v), 'utf8')])));
233:     }
234:   }
235:   parts.push(chunk('IDAT', zlib.deflateSync(raw, { level })));
236:   parts.push(chunk('IEND', Buffer.alloc(0)));
237:   return Buffer.concat(parts);
238: }
239: /**
240:  * Read any raster the comp pipeline meets (PNG natively; WebP / JPEG / GIF /
241:  * AVIF through a converter on PATH) as RGBA. Non-PNG input is converted to a
242:  * sibling cache file `<name>.<ext>.png` next to the source, never in place:
243:  * a session that overwrites `comp.webp` with PNG bytes leaves a file the
244:  * next tool cannot trust and a transcript replay cannot reconstruct.
245:  * Returns { image, path } where path is the PNG actually decoded.
246:  */
247: export function loadRaster(file) {
248:   const buf = fs.readFileSync(file);
249:   if (isPng(buf)) return { image: decodePng(buf), path: file };
250:   const cache = `${file}.png`;
251:   if (fs.existsSync(cache)) {
252:     try { const b = fs.readFileSync(cache); if (isPng(b)) return { image: decodePng(b), path: cache }; } catch { /* reconvert */ }
253:   }
254:   const attempts = [
255:     ['dwebp', [file, '-o', cache]],
256:     ['sips', ['-s', 'format', 'png', file, '--out', cache]],
257:     ['magick', [file, cache]],
258:     ['convert', [file, cache]],
259:   ];
260:   let lastErr = null;
261:   for (const [cmd, args] of attempts) {
262:     try { execFileSync(cmd, args, { stdio: 'ignore' }); const b = fs.readFileSync(cache); if (isPng(b)) return { image: decodePng(b), path: cache }; }
263:     catch (e) { lastErr = e; }
264:   }
265:   throw new Error(`png: ${file} is not a PNG and no converter (dwebp, sips, magick, convert) could produce ${cache}${lastErr ? `: ${lastErr.message}` : ''}`);
266: }
````

````javascript
  4:  * bitmap-font label so composites can be captioned without a font stack.
  5:  *
  6:  * An image is `{ width, height, data }` with RGBA8 data (Uint8Array).
  7:  */
  8: export function createImage(width, height, fill = [0, 0, 0, 0]) {
  9:   const data = new Uint8Array(width * height * 4);
 10:   if (fill[0] || fill[1] || fill[2] || fill[3]) {
 11:     for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i += 4) { data[i] = fill[0]; data[i + 1] = fill[1]; data[i + 2] = fill[2]; data[i + 3] = fill[3]; }

 15: export function clampRect(img, x, y, w, h) {
 16:   const x0 = Math.max(0, Math.min(img.width, Math.round(x)));
 17:   const y0 = Math.max(0, Math.min(img.height, Math.round(y)));
 18:   const x1 = Math.max(x0, Math.min(img.width, Math.round(x + w)));
 19:   const y1 = Math.max(y0, Math.min(img.height, Math.round(y + h)));
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/lib/roll-selection.mjs
````javascript
  1: // The one implementation of world-roll selection.
  2: //
  3: // Two copies of this logic used to exist: this repo's concept-seed.mjs and the
  4: // service repo's functions/api/_worldroll-core.js, whose header claimed they
  5: // matched "exactly". They did not. The API had no breadth gate on either pool,
  6: // no rating weighting for compositions, and dealt one composition where the
  7: // seeder dealt three. Because the catalog never ships with the skill, every real
  8: // user rolls through that API, so those gates reached nobody.
  9: //
 10: // Why generators. The two callers cannot agree on a hash: Node has a
 11: // synchronous one, Workers only have async crypto.subtle, and concept-seed's
 12: // local render path is deliberately synchronous so prepared eval sessions and
 13: // tests can call it without awaiting. Rather than fork the logic or force the
 14: // whole seeder async, the selection is written once as a generator that yields
 15: // batches of strings to hash and resumes with their digests. runSyncSelection
 16: // and runAsyncSelection below are the only runtime-specific code, about eight
 17: // lines each. Both digests are the same bytes, so a roll is identical either way.
 18: //
 19: // Nothing here reads a file, an environment variable, or the network: callers
 20: // pass pools in.
 21: export const WELL_TIERS = ['graphic', 'interaction', 'atmosphere'];
 22: // Grain: how much of the product a composition composes. Named grain rather than
 23: // scope because scope already means direction-or-surface on every roll, and
 24: // 'surface' is already a register value, so a scope of 'surface' would collide
 25: // with both.
 26: //
 27: // This axis is framed by what the skill can be asked for, not by what the
 28: // catalog happens to hold. A user asks for a docs site, an onboarding flow, a
 29: // landing page, or a data table, and those are four different amounts of
 30: // product. Register says what kind of work it is; grain says how much of it.
 31: // Without grain, a request for a hero section can be dealt a whole-site
 32: // navigation structure and nothing notices.
 33: //
 34: // Measured when this was added: 137 of 173 approved compositions were view
 35: // grain, product grain was empty, and flow grain held one entry. That is why an
 36: // onboarding request had nothing to draw.
 37: export const COMPOSITION_GRAINS = [
 38:   'product', // a whole site or app: its information architecture
 39:   'flow',    // a sequence of views with one outcome: onboarding, checkout, setup
 40:   'view',    // one page or screen
 41:   'region',  // a section inside a view: a hero, a feature grid, a table
 42: ];
 43: // Delivery targets a composition can survive. Mirrors the skill's platform axis
 44: // minus 'adaptive', which is a project-level value meaning both native targets
 45: // rather than something a single composition is authored for.
 46: //
 47: // A composition that leans on hover, a pointer, or a wide viewport does not
 48: // survive a phone, and nothing in the schema could say so before this.
 49: export const COMPOSITION_PLATFORMS = ['web', 'ios', 'android'];
 50: // Both fields are optional and absence means eligible everywhere, so no entry
 51: // has to be backfilled before this ships and no existing roll changes.
 52: export function isGrain(value) {
 53:   return COMPOSITION_GRAINS.includes(value);
 54: }
 55: export function isPlatform(value) {
 56:   return COMPOSITION_PLATFORMS.includes(value);
 57: }
 58: /**
 59:  * Drives a selection generator with a synchronous hash.
 60:  * @param {Generator} generator yields string[] to hash, resumes with hex string[]
 61:  * @param {(input: string) => string} hash
 62:  */
 63: export function runSyncSelection(generator, hash) {
 64:   let step = generator.next();
 65:   while (!step.done) step = generator.next(step.value.map(hash));
 66:   return step.value;
 67: }
 68: /**
 69:  * Drives a selection generator with an asynchronous hash.
 70:  * @param {Generator} generator
 71:  * @param {(input: string) => Promise<string>} hash
 72:  */
 73: export async function runAsyncSelection(generator, hash) {
 74:   let step = generator.next();
 75:   while (!step.done) step = generator.next(await Promise.all(step.value.map(hash)));
 76:   return step.value;
 77: }
 78: // Ranks items by the digest of `${input}:${id}`, descending, with the id as a
 79: // stable tiebreak. Yields every needed digest in one batch so the async driver
 80: // can resolve them concurrently.
 81: function* rank(items, input, idFor = item => item.id) {
 82:   const ids = items.map(idFor);
 83:   const digests = yield ids.map(id => `${input}:${id}`);
 84:   return items
 85:     .map((item, index) => ({ item, id: ids[index], score: digests[index] }))
 86:     .sort((a, b) => b.score.localeCompare(a.score) || a.id.localeCompare(b.id))
 87:     .map(entry => entry.item);
 88: }
 89: // Rating sets how many tickets a world holds; breadth decides whether it draws
 90: // at all. A niche world leaves the pool however good it is, keeping its approval
 91: // for direct briefs. Breadth was split out of rating because the only way to
 92: // hold a narrow world back used to be calling it marginal, which made "excellent
 93: // but narrow" unrecordable and corrupted ratings as a calibration signal.
 94: //
 95: // Two tickets for a 3-star, one for everything else, was too sharp. Measured
 96: // against the catalog as it stood: 3-star worlds absorbed 57% of the graphic
 97: // draw from 65 of 163 eligible worlds, 46% of atmosphere from 13 of 43, and
 98: // 75% of interaction from 15 of 25. The reviewer's complaint, that the same
 99: // worlds keep coming back, is what a rating multiplier does to a pool whose
100: // thinnest tier holds 25 worlds.
101: //
102: // So a 3-star no longer outdraws a 2-star, and a 1-star draws at half rather
103: // than not at all. A marginal keep is still worth showing sometimes: the
104: // judgement it records is "narrow or unexceptional", not "wrong", and excluding
105: // it entirely made a rating do a job breadth already does properly.
106: const RATING_TICKETS = { 1: 1, 2: 2, 3: 2 };
107: const ticketsForRating = rating => RATING_TICKETS[rating] ?? 2;
108: function challengerTickets(pool) {
109:   return pool.flatMap(concept => {
110:     if (concept.review?.breadth === 'niche') return [];
111:     return Array.from({ length: ticketsForRating(concept.review?.rating) },
112:       (_, ticket) => ({ concept, ticket }));
113:   });
114: }
115: function compositionTickets(pool) {
116:   return pool.flatMap(composition => Array.from(
117:     { length: ticketsForRating(composition.review?.rating) },
118:     (_, ticket) => ({ composition, ticket })));
119: }
120: /**
121:  * Six challengers, two per translation tier, from an explicit approved pool.
122:  * Drive with runSyncSelection or runAsyncSelection.
123:  *
124:  * @param {object} options
125:  * @param {'direction'|'surface'} options.scope
126:  * @param {string} options.key              same key reproduces the roll
127:  * @param {number} [options.reroll]         round of the re-roll chain
128:  * @param {number|null} [options.minRating] optional floor, skipped per tier it would empty
129:  * @param {Array} options.concepts          merged concepts with status, review, wellTier, familyId
130:  * @returns {Generator<string[], {approved: Array, picks: Array}, string[]>}
131:  */
132: // A world with no allowedModes is eligible everywhere, which is what keeps this
133: // additive: nothing has to be backfilled for the filter to be safe.
134: function modeAllows(concept, mode) {
135:   const allowed = concept.review?.allowedModes;

137:   return allowed.includes(mode);

139: export function* selectApprovedChallengers({ scope, key, reroll = 0, minRating = null, mode = null, concepts }) {
140:   const approved = concepts.filter(concept => concept.status === 'approved');
141:   // Direction chooses a durable identity, so it draws worlds; surface designs
142:   // one page inside a committed identity, so it draws compositions. Duals serve
143:   // both. A tier with no matching-strength approvals falls back to its full
144:   // approved pool rather than starving the roll.
145:   const wanted = scope === 'direction'
146:     ? new Set(['world', 'dual'])
147:     : new Set(['composition', 'dual']);
148:   const approvedByTier = new Map();
149:   for (const concept of approved) {
150:     const tier = approvedByTier.get(concept.wellTier) || [];
151:     tier.push(concept);
152:     approvedByTier.set(concept.wellTier, tier);
153:   }
154:   if (WELL_TIERS.some(tier => !(approvedByTier.get(tier) || []).length)) {
155:     throw new Error('concept-seed: every challenger tier needs at least one approved concept');
156:   }
157:   // Optional minimum-rating gate, applied per tier and skipped for any tier it
158:   // would empty, so a thin tier degrades to its full approved pool.
159:   if (minRating) {
160:     for (const [tier, pool] of approvedByTier) {
161:       const rated = pool.filter(concept => (concept.review?.rating || 0) >= minRating);
162:       if (rated.length > 0) approvedByTier.set(tier, rated);
163:     }
164:   }
165:   // Mode eligibility, per tier and skipped where it would empty a tier. Worlds
166:   // used to be drawn with no mode awareness at all, so a build asking for an app
167:   // UI could get six worlds that only make sense on a landing page. A world is an
168:   // identity and identities transfer further than compositions do, so this is a
169:   // ceiling the reviewer sets rather than a category assignment: eligible
170:   // everywhere until someone says otherwise.
171:   if (mode) {
172:     for (const [tier, pool] of approvedByTier) {
173:       const eligible = pool.filter(concept => modeAllows(concept, mode));
174:       if (eligible.length > 0) approvedByTier.set(tier, eligible);
175:     }
176:   }
177:   for (const [tier, pool] of approvedByTier) {
178:     const matching = pool.filter(concept => wanted.has(concept.strength));
179:     if (matching.length > 0) approvedByTier.set(tier, matching);
180:   }
181:   // Two challengers per tier, so every roll carries near-zero-translation
182:   // graphic systems beside instrument languages and atmosphere worlds, with the
183:   // second pick preferring a different family. Tier order is rolled too, to
184:   // avoid positional bias.

186:     const salt = round === 0 ? '' : `:reroll-${round}`;
187:     const tierOrder = (yield* rank(
188:       WELL_TIERS.map(id => ({ id })),
189:       `${scope}:${key}:tiers${salt}`
190:     )).map(item => item.id);
191:     const picks = [];
192:     for (const [index, tier] of tierOrder.entries()) {
193:       let pool = approvedByTier.get(tier).filter(concept => !excluded.has(concept.id));
194:       // A tier exhausted by prior rounds falls back to reuse over starvation.
195:       if (pool.length === 0) pool = approvedByTier.get(tier);
196:       let tickets = challengerTickets(pool);
197:       if (tickets.length === 0) tickets = pool.map(concept => ({ concept, ticket: 0 }));
198:       const ranked = yield* rank(
199:         tickets,
200:         `${scope}:${key}:challenger-${index}${salt}`,
201:         entry => `${entry.concept.id}#${entry.ticket}`
202:       );
203:       const order = [];
204:       const seen = new Set();
205:       for (const entry of ranked) {
206:         if (seen.has(entry.concept.id)) continue;
207:         seen.add(entry.concept.id);
208:         order.push(entry.concept);
209:       }
210:       const first = order[0];
211:       const second = order.find(concept => concept.familyId !== first.familyId)

213:       picks.push(...(second ? [first, second] : [first]));

216:   }
217:   // Round n of a re-roll chain excludes everything rounds 0..n-1 drew, so the
218:   // same base key reproduces the whole chain.
219:   const excluded = new Set();
220:   let picks = yield* pickRound(0, excluded);
221:   for (let round = 1; round <= reroll; round += 1) {

228:   return { grain: grain ?? null, atGrain: grain ? 0 : null, grainAvailable: grain ? 0 : null, platform: platform ?? null, platformExcluded };

230: /**
231:  * Three identity-free composition inputs from an explicit approved pool.
232:  * Drive with runSyncSelection or runAsyncSelection.
233:  *
234:  * One input was too weak a counterweight to a model's habitual page skeleton:
235:  * it became a single optional flourish beside six identity challengers rather
236:  * than a real search over composition. Distinct composition families are preferred
237:  * so a roll tests materially different hierarchy, sequence, and interaction

239:  * returns nothing rather than borrowing. Re-rolls exclude every earlier set
240:  * until the pool runs out.

247:  * @param {string|null} [options.grain]     how much of the product is in play
248:  * @param {string|null} [options.platform]  delivery target the result has to survive
249:  * @param {Array} options.compositions  merged compositions with status, review, surface, familyId

254:   // Compositions honour the same breadth gate as worlds: one too specific to serve
255:   // an arbitrary build stays approved for direct briefs and leaves the
256:   // challenger pool. Falls back to the full approved set rather than returning

261:   if (approved.length === 0) return { picks: [], match: emptyMatch(grain, platform) };
262:   if (mode) {
263:     const matching = approved.filter(composition => composition.surface === mode);
264:     if (matching.length === 0) return { picks: [], match: emptyMatch(grain, platform) };

266:   }
267:   // Platform is a hard filter, unlike grain. A composition that needs hover or a
268:   // pointer does not degrade on a phone into something slightly worse; it stops

270:   // platforms means it survives anywhere.
271:   let platformExcluded = 0;
272:   if (platform) {
273:     const survives = approved.filter(composition => {
274:       const only = composition.platforms;
275:       return !Array.isArray(only) || only.length === 0 || only.includes(platform);
276:     });

279:     // is worse than dealing nothing, and an empty deal is a visible gap.
280:     approved = survives;
281:     if (approved.length === 0) return { picks: [], match: emptyMatch(grain, platform, platformExcluded) };
282:   }

284:   let picks = [];
285:   for (let round = 0; round <= reroll; round += 1) {
286:     const available = approved.filter(composition => !prior.has(composition.id));
287:     const base = available.length >= Math.min(count, approved.length) ? available : approved;
288:     // Rating weights the draw as it does for worlds. It matters more here
289:     // because the per-surface pools are small, so an unweighted shuffle repeats
290:     // a weak composition far more often. Each ticket carries its index so the rank
291:     // sees a distinct key per ticket: ranking bare duplicates would hash
292:     // identically and the pick loop's id-dedupe would silently discard the
293:     // second copy, making the weighting a no-op.
294:     let tickets = compositionTickets(base);
295:     // A pool of nothing but 1-star keeps still has to yield compositions.
296:     if (tickets.length === 0) tickets = base.map(composition => ({ composition, ticket: 0 }));
297:     const ranked = (yield* rank(
298:       tickets,
299:       // The salt keeps the word "staging" deliberately. It is hash input, so
300:       // renaming it would re-deal every roll anyone has ever reproduced by key.
301:       round === 0 ? `${scope}:${key}:staging` : `${scope}:${key}:staging:reroll-${round}`,

303:     )).map(entry => entry.composition);
304:     // Grain is a preference, not a filter: requesting an onboarding flow deals
305:     // flow-grain compositions first and tops up from the rest of the register
306:     // rather than dealing fewer than three. A stable partition of an already
307:     // deterministic ranking is still deterministic.
308:     //
309:     // The top-up is why match is reported. Dealing three plausible view-grain
310:     // compositions against a flow request, with no signal that none matched, is

312:     // model would improvise the flow structure while believing it was handed one.
313:     const ordered = grain

315:          ...ranked.filter(composition => composition.grain !== grain)]
316:       : ranked;
317:     const families = new Set();
318:     picks = [];
319:     for (const composition of ordered) {
320:       const family = composition.familyId ?? composition.id;
321:       if (families.has(family)) continue;
322:       picks.push(composition);
323:       families.add(family);
324:       if (picks.length >= count) break;
325:     }
326:     for (const composition of ordered) {
327:       if (picks.length >= count) break;
328:       if (!picks.some(pick => pick.id === composition.id)) picks.push(composition);
329:     }
330:     if (round < reroll) picks.forEach(composition => prior.add(composition.id));
331:   }
332:   const atGrain = grain ? picks.filter(composition => composition.grain === grain).length : null;
333:   return {
334:     picks,
335:     match: {
336:       grain: grain ?? null,
337:       // How many of the dealt compositions actually sit at the requested grain.
338:       // 0 with a grain requested means every pick is a borrowed structure.
339:       atGrain,
340:       grainAvailable: grain ? approved.filter(composition => composition.grain === grain).length : null,
341:       platform: platform ?? null,
342:       platformExcluded,
343:     },
344:   };
345: }
````

````javascript
265:   const expanded = token.replace(/\$\{CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\}/g, root);
266:   // Any placeholder or shell variable still present is one we can't map.
267:   if (/\$\{[^}]*\}|\$[A-Za-z_]/.test(expanded)) return null;
268:   return path.isAbsolute(expanded) ? expanded : path.join(root, expanded);

270: /**
271:  * A hook whose script path does not resolve is a silent no-op, and the user
272:  * believes the project is covered. Also catches the contradiction of an
273:  * installed manifest against `hook.enabled: false`.
274:  */
275: export function checkHookInstallation({ projectRoot, repoRoot, providerId }) {
276:   const findings = [];
277:   const manifests = HOOK_MANIFESTS_BY_PROVIDER[providerId] || [];
278:   if (!manifests.length) return findings;
279:   const roots = [...new Set([projectRoot, repoRoot].filter(Boolean).map((root) => path.resolve(root)))];
280:   let installedAt = null;
281:   for (const root of roots) {
282:     for (const rel of manifests) {
283:       const manifestPath = path.join(root, rel);
284:       const raw = readJson(manifestPath);
285:       if (!raw?.hooks) continue;
286:       const commands = collectHookCommands(raw.hooks);
287:       if (!commands.length) continue;
288:       installedAt = toRelative(manifestPath, projectRoot || root);
289:       const broken = commands.filter((command) => {
290:         const token = hookScriptTokenFrom(command);
291:         if (!token) return false;
292:         const abs = resolveHookScriptPath(token, root);
293:         // Unresolvable placeholder or command substitution: never assert missing.
294:         if (!abs) return false;
295:         return !fs.existsSync(abs);
296:       });
297:       if (broken.length) {
298:         findings.push(finding({
299:           id: 'hook-script-missing',
300:           artifact: 'hook manifest',
301:           filePath: installedAt,
302:           severity: 'mention',
303:           summary: `${installedAt} installs the design hook, but its script path does not exist: `
304:             + `${broken.map((command) => `\`${command}\``).join(', ')}. The hook runs as a no-op, so UI edits `
305:             + 'have been going unscanned while the project looks covered.',
306:           fix: `Reinstall with \`impeccable hooks on\`, which rewrites the manifest against the skill's current location.`,
307:         }));
308:       }
309:     }
310:   }
311:   if (installedAt) {
312:     for (const root of roots) {
313:       for (const name of ['config.json', 'config.local.json']) {
314:         const raw = readJson(path.join(root, '.impeccable', name));
315:         if (raw?.hook && raw.hook.enabled === false) {
316:           findings.push(finding({
317:             id: 'hook-enabled-conflict',
318:             artifact: 'config.json',
319:             filePath: toRelative(path.join(root, '.impeccable', name), projectRoot || root),
320:             severity: 'mention',
321:             summary: `${installedAt} installs the design hook while this config sets \`hook.enabled: false\`, `
322:               + 'so the hook fires and then declines to scan.',
323:             fix: 'Ask which was intended: `impeccable hooks on` to enable, or `impeccable hooks off` to uninstall '
324:               + 'the manifest entry as well.',
325:           }));
326:           return findings;
327:         }
328:       }
329:     }
330:   }
331:   return findings;
332: }
333: // ─── retired locations ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
334: export function checkLegacyLiveState({ projectRoot }) {
335:   if (!projectRoot) return [];
336:   const present = LEGACY_LIVE_PATHS.filter((rel) => fs.existsSync(path.join(projectRoot, rel)));
337:   if (!present.length) return [];
338:   return [finding({
339:     id: 'legacy-live-state',
340:     artifact: 'live state',
341:     filePath: present.join(', '),
342:     severity: 'auto',
343:     summary: `Live-mode state sits in retired location(s): ${present.map((rel) => `\`${rel}\``).join(', ')}. `
344:       + 'Current live mode writes under `.impeccable/live/`.',
345:     fix: 'These are read only through backward-compatible fallbacks and are safe to delete once no live session '
346:       + 'is running. No user decision is needed.',
347:   })];
348: }
349: // ─── monorepo sweep ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
350: /**
351:  * Per-workspace context, plus the case worth acting on: a workspace with
352:  * native build files inheriting a repo-root PRODUCT.md that says web. Each
353:  * such app gets web guidance and never loads the native references, and
354:  * nothing at boot reports it because the root record parses cleanly.

359:   if (!repoRoot || !candidates.length) return { findings: [], workspaces: [] };
360:   const findings = [];
361:   const workspaces = [];
362:   for (const candidate of candidates) {
363:     const workspaceRoot = path.join(repoRoot, candidate.path);
364:     const productPath = candidate.productPath ? path.join(repoRoot, candidate.productPath) : null;
365:     const product = productPath && readFile ? readFile(productPath) : null;
366:     const platform = extractPlatform ? extractPlatform(product) : null;
367:     workspaces.push({
368:       name: candidate.name,
369:       path: candidate.path,
370:       productStatus: candidate.productStatus,
371:       productPath: candidate.productPath,
372:       designStatus: candidate.designStatus,
373:       designPath: candidate.designPath,
374:       platform: platform || (product ? 'web (default)' : null),
375:     });
376:     if (!checkNativePlatformEvidence) continue;
377:     const native = checkNativePlatformEvidence({
378:       projectRoot: workspaceRoot,
379:       platform,
380:       product,
381:       productPath: candidate.productPath,
382:     });
383:     for (const entry of native) {
384:       findings.push(finding({
385:         id: 'workspace-platform-native-evidence',
386:         artifact: 'PRODUCT.md',
387:         filePath: candidate.productPath || `${candidate.path}/PRODUCT.md`,
388:         severity: 'mention',
389:         summary: `Workspace \`${candidate.path}\` ${
390:           candidate.productStatus === 'inherited'
391:             ? 'inherits the repo-root PRODUCT.md'
392:             : 'has a PRODUCT.md'
393:         } that resolves to web, but the workspace itself carries native build files. ${entry.summary}`,
394:         fix: candidate.productStatus === 'inherited'
395:           ? `Give \`${candidate.path}\` its own PRODUCT.md with the right \`## Platform\`. `
396:             + 'An inherited record cannot describe two platforms at once.'
397:           : entry.fix,
398:       }));
399:     }
400:   }
401:   const inherited = workspaces.filter((entry) => entry.productStatus === 'inherited');
402:   if (inherited.length) {
403:     findings.push(finding({
404:       id: 'workspace-context-inherited',
405:       artifact: 'PRODUCT.md',
406:       filePath: null,
407:       severity: 'mention',
408:       summary: `${inherited.length} of ${workspaces.length} workspace(s) inherit the repo-root PRODUCT.md: `
409:         + `${inherited.map((entry) => `\`${entry.path}\``).join(', ')}. Inheritance is intended; whether one `
410:         + 'record truthfully describes these apps is not something this check can tell.',
411:       fix: 'Ask the user whether the inherited record describes each app. Where it does not, `init` in that '
412:         + 'workspace writes a child PRODUCT.md that overrides it.',
413:     }));
414:   }
415:   return { findings, workspaces };
416: }
417: // ─── rule registry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
418: /**
419:  * Rule ids from the bundled detector, or null when it cannot be resolved (a
420:  * partial install, or a harness that ships the skill without the engine).
421:  * Null means "cannot check", which the ignore-rule check treats as skip rather
422:  * than as every id being unknown.
423:  */
424: export async function loadKnownRuleIds(scriptsDir = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..')) {
425:   // Same two locations detect.mjs resolves: the bundled copy in an installed
426:   // skill, then the source-repo engine when running from a checkout.
427:   const candidates = [
428:     path.join(scriptsDir, 'detector', 'detect-antipatterns.mjs'),
429:     path.join(scriptsDir, '..', '..', 'cli', 'engine', 'detect-antipatterns.mjs'),
430:   ];
431:   const detectorPath = candidates.find((candidate) => fs.existsSync(candidate));
432:   if (!detectorPath) return null;
433:   try {
434:     const { ANTIPATTERNS } = await import(pathToFileURL(detectorPath).href);
435:     if (!Array.isArray(ANTIPATTERNS)) return null;
436:     return new Set(ANTIPATTERNS.map((rule) => String(rule.id).toLowerCase()));
437:   } catch {
438:     return null;
439:   }
440: }
````
