## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/lib/staleness-notice.mjs
````javascript
  1: /**
  2:  * Notice throttling and directive rendering for staleness findings.
  3:  *
  4:  * The boot path already carries PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, a surface brief,
  5:  * RESOLVED_CONTEXT, the detector fallback, native platform references, and the
  6:  * update directive. An unthrottled staleness block would push real context out
  7:  * of attention and train the agent to open every session with housekeeping, so
  8:  * the rules here are deliberately strict:
  9:  *
 10:  *   - One directive for the whole set, never one per finding.
 11:  *   - A 'mention' or 'route' finding surfaces at most once a week per project,
 12:  *     mirroring the update check's anti-nag window. A finding the user has
 13:  *     already declined to act on must not reappear tomorrow.
 14:  *   - 'auto' findings are not throttled and are not shown to the user. They are
 15:  *     migrations the next write performs anyway, so the agent needs the note
 16:  *     every session until the write happens, and the user needs it never.
 17:  *
 18:  * State lives in the user's home dir alongside the update cache rather than in
 19:  * the project, so no gitignore entry is owed and a clone does not inherit
 20:  * someone else's dismissals.
 21:  */
 22: import fs from 'node:fs';
 23: import os from 'node:os';
 24: import path from 'node:path';
 25: const RENOTIFY_INTERVAL_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
 26: // Resolved per call rather than at import so a test (or a sandboxed run) can
 27: // redirect the cache without reloading the module.
 28: function cachePath() {
 29:   return process.env.IMPECCABLE_STALENESS_CACHE
 30:     || path.join(os.homedir(), '.impeccable', 'staleness-check.json');
 31: }
 32: function readCache() {
 33:   try {
 34:     const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(cachePath(), 'utf-8'));
 35:     return raw && typeof raw === 'object' && raw.projects ? raw : { projects: {} };
 36:   } catch {
 37:     return { projects: {} };
 38:   }
 39: }
 40: /**
 41:  * Drop project entries whose newest stamp has aged past the renotify window.
 42:  * They would be re-notified on the next boot anyway, so keeping them only lets
 43:  * the file accumulate one entry per directory Impeccable has ever booted in
 44:  * (scratch dirs and test fixtures included).
 45:  */
 46: function pruneCache(cache, now) {
 47:   const projects = {};
 48:   for (const [key, entries] of Object.entries(cache.projects || {})) {
 49:     if (!entries || typeof entries !== 'object') continue;
 50:     const stamps = Object.values(entries).filter((value) => typeof value === 'number');
 51:     if (stamps.length && now - Math.max(...stamps) < RENOTIFY_INTERVAL_MS) projects[key] = entries;
 52:   }
 53:   return { projects };
 54: }
 55: function writeCache(cache) {
 56:   try {
 57:     const filePath = cachePath();
 58:     fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true });
 59:     fs.writeFileSync(filePath, JSON.stringify(cache));
 60:   } catch {
 61:     // Best-effort. A read-only home dir means the notice repeats next session,
 62:     // which is strictly better than failing the boot.
 63:   }
 64: }
 65: function readJson(filePath) {
 66:   try {
 67:     return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8'));
 68:   } catch {
 69:     return null;
 70:   }
 71: }
 72: /**
 73:  * Opt out with IMPECCABLE_NO_STALENESS_CHECK=1 or `"stalenessCheck": false` in
 74:  * .impeccable/config.json. Local config overrides shared, matching how
 75:  * updateCheck resolves.
 76:  */
 77: export function stalenessCheckDisabled(roots = [process.cwd()]) {
 78:   if (process.env.IMPECCABLE_NO_STALENESS_CHECK) return true;
 79:   let value;
 80:   for (const root of roots) {
 81:     if (!root) continue;
 82:     for (const name of ['config.json', 'config.local.json']) {
 83:       const raw = readJson(path.join(root, '.impeccable', name));
 84:       if (raw && typeof raw === 'object' && typeof raw.stalenessCheck === 'boolean') {
 85:         value = raw.stalenessCheck;
 86:       }
 87:     }
 88:   }
 89:   return value === false;
 90: }
 91: /**
 92:  * Drop findings already surfaced for this project inside the renotify window,
 93:  * and stamp the ones that survive. 'auto' findings pass through untouched and
 94:  * unstamped: they are for the agent, not the user, and repeat until fixed.
 95:  */
 96: export function filterFreshFindings(findings, { projectRoot, now = Date.now() } = {}) {
 97:   if (!findings.length) return [];
 98:   const auto = findings.filter((entry) => entry.severity === 'auto');
 99:   const notifiable = findings.filter((entry) => entry.severity !== 'auto');
100:   if (!notifiable.length) return auto;
101:   const key = path.resolve(projectRoot || process.cwd());
102:   const cache = readCache();
103:   const seen = cache.projects[key] && typeof cache.projects[key] === 'object' ? cache.projects[key] : {};
104:   const fresh = notifiable.filter((entry) => {
105:     const last = seen[entry.id];
106:     return !(typeof last === 'number' && now - last < RENOTIFY_INTERVAL_MS);
107:   });
108:   // Forget stamps for findings that no longer fire, so a recurrence after a
109:   // real fix is reported again instead of being suppressed by an old stamp.
110:   // This has to run even when nothing is fresh: the common shape is one
111:   // finding fixed while another is still inside its window.
112:   const live = new Set(notifiable.map((entry) => entry.id));
113:   const next = Object.fromEntries(
114:     Object.entries(seen).filter(([id]) => live.has(id)),
115:   );
116:   for (const entry of fresh) next[entry.id] = now;
117:   const changed = JSON.stringify(next) !== JSON.stringify(seen);
118:   if (changed) {
119:     const pruned = pruneCache(cache, now);
120:     pruned.projects[key] = next;
121:     writeCache(pruned);
122:   }
123:   return [...auto, ...fresh];
124: }
125: /**
126:  * Render the single boot directive, or null when nothing survived throttling.
127:  */
128: export function buildStalenessDirective(findings) {
129:   if (!findings.length) return null;
130:   const payload = findings.map((entry) => ({
131:     id: entry.id,
132:     artifact: entry.artifact,
133:     path: entry.path,
134:     severity: entry.severity,
135:     summary: entry.summary,
136:     fix: entry.fix,
137:   }));
138:   const hasReportable = findings.some((entry) => entry.severity !== 'auto');
139:   const lines = [
140:     `CONTEXT_STALE:\n${JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2)}`,
141:     "Impeccable's own project files have drifted from what this version reads. "
142:       + 'Do not stop, reorder, or expand the requested task for any of this.',
143:     'By severity: `auto` is a migration the next write to that file performs anyway, so apply it then and do not '
144:       + 'raise it with the user. `mention` gets one short line in your reply with the offered fix. `route` names the '
145:       + 'command that owns the repair; offer it, and run it only if the user asks.',
146:     'A finding that reports a deprecated field is binding: treat that field as absent for every decision in this '
147:       + 'session, whatever value it holds.',
148:   ];
149:   if (hasReportable) {
150:     lines.push('Surface the reportable findings once, after the task response, in at most two sentences. '
151:       + 'They are already throttled, so say them plainly rather than hedging about whether they matter.');
152:   }
153:   return lines.join(' ');
154: }
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/lib/staleness.mjs
````javascript
  1: /**
  2:  * Staleness detection for Impeccable's own project artifacts: PRODUCT.md,
  3:  * DESIGN.md and its `.impeccable/design.json` sidecar, `.impeccable/config.json`,
  4:  * and persisted surface briefs.
  5:  *
  6:  * Three kinds of drift live under "out of date", and they want different
  7:  * handling:
  8:  *
  9:  *   1. Tool version drift. The installed skill is older than the published one.
 10:  *      Owned by computeUpdateDirective in context.mjs, not by this module.
 11:  *   2. Schema drift. An artifact was written by an older Impeccable: fields it
 12:  *      no longer reads, fields it now expects, files in retired locations.
 13:  *      Deterministic, and mostly fixable without asking anyone.
 14:  *   3. Truth drift. The code moved on and the document no longer describes it.
 15:  *      Not mechanical. `document` and `init` own the rewrite; the most this
 16:  *      module does is measure a proxy and name it as a proxy.
 17:  *
 18:  * Two tiers, because the boot path runs on every session:
 19:  *
 20:  *   Tier 1 (collectBootFindings) spends only what a boot already spends. It
 21:  *   parses markdown context.mjs has in memory, stats a bounded set of paths,
 22:  *   and reads the two small JSON files the boot reads anyway. No directory
 23:  *   walks, no git, no cross-workspace sweep.
 24:  *
 25:  *   Tier 2 (the doctor pass) is on demand and may walk, shell out to git, and
 26:  *   compare declared tokens against real CSS.
 27:  *
 28:  * Findings are data, not prose, so both tiers and the JSON output render the
 29:  * same set. Severity says what should happen, not how bad it is:
 30:  *
 31:  *   'auto'    fix it silently the next time that file is written anyway
 32:  *   'mention' state it once, offer the fix, carry on with the user's task
 33:  *   'route'   needs a specific command, so name the command and the gap
 34:  */
 35: import fs from 'node:fs';
 36: import path from 'node:path';
 37: import {
 38:   PRODUCT_SCHEMA_VERSION,
 39:   PRODUCT_DEPRECATED_SECTIONS,
 40:   PRODUCT_V4_SECTIONS,
 41:   DESIGN_SIDECAR_SCHEMA_VERSION,
 42:   readProductSchemaVersion,
 43:   readSidecarSchemaVersion,
 44: } from './artifact-schema.mjs';
 45: // Top-level keys any reader honors: `hook` and `detector` subtrees (hook-lib's
 46: // readConfig), `updateCheck` (context.mjs), `projectRoots` (context.mjs's
 47: // monorepo resolution), `buildPath` (context.mjs's build-path directive), plus
 48: // `stalenessCheck` below. `$schema` and `version` are allowed as conventional
 49: // metadata nobody reads.
 50: const KNOWN_CONFIG_KEYS = new Set([
 51:   'hook',
 52:   'detector',
 53:   'updateCheck',
 54:   'stalenessCheck',
 55:   'projectRoots',
 56:   'buildPath',
 57:   '$schema',
 58:   'version',
 59: ]);
 60: // The only two values context.mjs and new-work honor. A near miss reads as a
 61: // working preference and silently rides the opposite path, so it is worth
 62: // reporting rather than coercing.
 63: const BUILD_PATH_VALUES = Object.freeze(['comp', 'code']);
 64: // Evidence that this project does the kind of work `buildPath` governs. A
 65: // project that only ever ran polish or audit has no use for the setting and
 66: // should never be told it exists. Two stats, so Tier 1 can afford it.
 67: const DIRECTION_WORK_PATHS = Object.freeze([
 68:   path.join('.impeccable', 'surfaces'),
 69:   path.join('.impeccable', 'mocks', 'decision'),
 70: ]);
 71: // `detector` is a closed set, so a typo here is worth reporting. `hook` is not
 72: // checked: it carries runtime settings from several writers and the false
 73: // positive rate would outweigh the catch.
 74: const KNOWN_DETECTOR_KEYS = new Set([
 75:   'ignoreRules',
 76:   'ignoreFiles',
 77:   'ignoreValues',
 78:   'designSystem',
 79:   'extensions',
 80: ]);
 81: // Evidence that a project ships a native app. Checked only to catch a
 82: // PRODUCT.md that says web (or says nothing, which resolves to web) on a
 83: // project that is plainly not: that combination silently skips the iOS and
 84: // Android references for the whole session.
 85: const NATIVE_EVIDENCE_PATHS = Object.freeze([
 86:   { rel: 'pubspec.yaml', platform: 'adaptive', reason: 'a Flutter pubspec.yaml' },
 87:   { rel: 'ios/Podfile', platform: 'ios', reason: 'an ios/Podfile' },
 88:   { rel: 'android/build.gradle', platform: 'android', reason: 'an android/build.gradle' },
 89:   { rel: 'android/build.gradle.kts', platform: 'android', reason: 'an android/build.gradle.kts' },
 90:   { rel: 'ios/Runner.xcodeproj', platform: 'ios', reason: 'an ios/Runner.xcodeproj' },
 91: ]);
 92: const NATIVE_EVIDENCE_DEPENDENCIES = Object.freeze([
 93:   { name: 'react-native', platform: 'adaptive', reason: 'a react-native dependency' },
 94:   { name: 'expo', platform: 'adaptive', reason: 'an expo dependency' },
 95:   { name: '@react-native/metro-config', platform: 'adaptive', reason: 'a React Native metro config dependency' },
 96: ]);
 97: function finding({ id, artifact, filePath = null, severity, summary, fix }) {
 98:   return { id, artifact, path: filePath, severity, summary, fix };
 99: }
100: /**
101:  * Every location a design sidecar may live, canonical first. Pure so that both
102:  * impeccable-paths (which resolves the project root) and context.mjs (which
103:  * cannot import impeccable-paths without a cycle) share one definition of
104:  * where the retired locations are.
105:  */
106: export function designSidecarCandidatesFor(projectRoot, contextDir = projectRoot) {
107:   const candidates = [
108:     path.join(projectRoot, '.impeccable', 'design.json'),
109:     path.join(projectRoot, 'DESIGN.json'),
110:   ];
111:   const contextLegacy = path.join(contextDir || projectRoot, 'DESIGN.json');
112:   if (!candidates.includes(contextLegacy)) candidates.push(contextLegacy);
113:   return candidates;
114: }
115: function readJson(filePath) {
116:   try {
117:     return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8'));
118:   } catch {
119:     return null;
120:   }
121: }
122: function mtimeMs(filePath) {
123:   try {
124:     return fs.statSync(filePath).mtimeMs;
125:   } catch {
126:     return null;
127:   }
128: }
129: function hasSection(markdown, heading) {
130:   const escaped = heading.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
131:   return new RegExp(`^##\\s+${escaped}\\s*$`, 'im').test(String(markdown || ''));

133: function toRelative(filePath, root) {
134:   if (!filePath) return null;
135:   const rel = path.relative(root, filePath);
136:   return rel && !rel.startsWith('..') && !path.isAbsolute(rel)
137:     ? rel.split(path.sep).join('/')
138:     : filePath;
139: }
140: // ─── PRODUCT.md ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
141: /**
142:  * Pure: schema drift visible in a PRODUCT.md body. `productPath` is used for
143:  * reporting only.
144:  */
145: export function checkProduct(product, productPath = 'PRODUCT.md') {
146:   if (!product) return [];
147:   const findings = [];
148:   for (const [heading, reason] of Object.entries(PRODUCT_DEPRECATED_SECTIONS)) {
149:     if (!hasSection(product, heading)) continue;
150:     findings.push(finding({
151:       id: `product-deprecated-${heading.toLowerCase()}`,
152:       artifact: 'PRODUCT.md',
153:       filePath: productPath,
154:       severity: 'mention',
155:       summary: `PRODUCT.md still carries a \`## ${heading}\` section. ${reason}`,
156:       fix: `Treat \`## ${heading}\` as absent for every decision this session. `
157:         + 'Offer to delete the section; do not let its value influence the work either way.',
158:     }));
159:   }
160:   const stamped = readProductSchemaVersion(product);
161:   if (stamped === null && !PRODUCT_V4_SECTIONS.some((section) => hasSection(product, section))) {
162:     findings.push(finding({
163:       id: 'product-schema-legacy',
164:       artifact: 'PRODUCT.md',
165:       filePath: productPath,
166:       severity: 'route',
167:       summary: 'PRODUCT.md has no schema stamp and none of the sections the current record adds '
168:         + `(${PRODUCT_V4_SECTIONS.join(', ')}), so it predates this version of the product record.`,
169:       fix: 'Offer `init`, which preserves confirmed answers and fills the gaps by interview. '
````

````javascript
 2: const SLUG_MAX = 50;
 3: /** Derive one clone-stable slug from a concrete file path or URL. */
 4: export function slugFromTarget(resolved, { cwd = process.cwd() } = {}) {
 5:   if (!resolved || typeof resolved !== 'string') return null;
 6:   const trimmed = resolved.trim();
 7:   if (!trimmed) return null;
 8:   if (/^https?:\/\//i.test(trimmed)) {
 9:     let url;
10:     try { url = new URL(trimmed); } catch { return null; }
11:     return kebab(`${url.hostname}${url.pathname}`);
12:   }
13:   const abs = path.isAbsolute(trimmed) ? trimmed : path.resolve(cwd, trimmed);
14:   let rel = path.relative(cwd, abs);
15:   if (rel.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(rel)) rel = path.basename(abs);
16:   if (!rel || rel === '.') return null;
17:   return kebab(rel);

19: export function kebab(value) {
20:   const slug = String(value || '')
21:     .toLowerCase()
22:     .replace(/[/\\.]+/g, '-')
23:     .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]+/g, '-')
24:     .replace(/-+/g, '-')
25:     .replace(/^-|-$/g, '');
26:   if (!slug) return null;
27:   return slug.length <= SLUG_MAX ? slug : slug.slice(slug.length - SLUG_MAX).replace(/^-/, '');
````

````javascript
 1: /**
````

````javascript
12:   const file = path.join(cwd, 'package.json');
13:   try {

15:     return {
16:       ...(pkg.dependencies || {}),

18:       ...(pkg.peerDependencies || {}),
19:     };
20:   } catch {
21:     return {};
22:   }

34:   } catch {
35:     return null;
36:   }
37: }
````

````javascript
156:   if (!journal) return { healed: [], kept: [] };

171:   if (kept.length) {

173:   } else {
174:     clearInjectJournal(cwd);
````

````javascript
14:   'src/app/layout.tsx', 'src/app/layout.jsx', 'src/app/layout.ts', 'src/app/layout.js',
15:   'pages/_app.tsx', 'pages/_app.jsx', 'pages/_app.ts', 'pages/_app.js',
16:   'pages/_document.tsx', 'pages/_document.jsx',
17:   'src/pages/_app.tsx', 'src/pages/_app.jsx',
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/live/frameworks/script-src.mjs
````javascript
 1: /**
 2:  * The one place that builds the `/live.js` URL the browser loads.
 3:  *
 4:  * Every injection path needs it (the generic script tag, the Nuxt client
 5:  * plugin, the SvelteKit root component, the TanStack mount component), and a
 6:  * separate module keeps that shared leaf free of import cycles: the framework
 7:  * entries import it, and nothing here imports a framework entry.
 8:  */
 9: /**
10:  * When a token is supplied it rides as a `?token=...` query param so the
11:  * server's token-gated /live.js handler authorizes the fetch.
12:  */
13: export function buildLiveScriptSrc(port, token) {
14:   const base = 'http://localhost:' + port + '/live.js';
15:   return token ? base + '?token=' + encodeURIComponent(token) : base;
16: }
````

````javascript
  1: /**
````

````javascript
  7:  * inserting it at the configured anchor, removing it again, and the
  8:  * Content-Security-Policy meta patch that keeps the cross-origin load allowed.

 11:  * `is:inline`, for instance) arrives as the `scriptAttrs` argument, resolved
 12:  * from the registry by the caller, so nothing here has to branch on a file
 13:  * extension or a project shape.
 14:  */

 17: export const MARKER_CLOSE_TEXT = 'impeccable-live-end';

 31:   const close = commentClose(syntax);

109: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
110: // Content-Security-Policy meta-tag patcher

130:   const out = [];

152:   }
````

````javascript
 1: /**
 2:  * Generic Vite registry entry: a bundled app with a real `index.html` entry

 4:  * a plain TanStack Router SPA all land here — the marker-wrapped script block
 5:  * goes straight into the HTML entry.

 8:  * static-html sits below it.

15:   if (hasAnyDependency(cwd, ['vite'])) return { configFile: null, via: 'package' };

19:     return { configFile: null, via: 'zero-config' };
````

````javascript
  1: /**
  2:  * Accept-time CSS reconciliation for live mode.
  3:  *
  4:  * The old accept path appended the chosen variant's whole <style> body in
  5:  * front of the component's existing rules, which preserved every superseded
  6:  * declaration (the "old divider borders survive the accept" bug) and left
  7:  * dead parameter branches in source. This module makes acceptance a merge:
  8:  *
  9:  *   reconcileCss      replace rules whose selectors match, append new ones
 10:  *   bakeParamValues   collapse --p-* vars and [data-p-*] branches to the
 11:  *                     user's chosen values, driven by the declared param
 12:  *                     kinds from params.json (not regex sniffing)
 13:  *   pruneUnusedSelectors  use the framework compiler's own unused-selector
 14:  *                     warnings to delete rules the accepted markup no longer
 15:  *                     references
 16:  *
 17:  * The parser is hand-rolled on purpose: skill scripts run standalone inside
 18:  * user projects and cannot rely on this repo's node_modules. It is a small
 19:  * recursive block parser (comment- and string-aware), not a spec-complete
 20:  * CSS parser; everything it emits round-trips byte-for-byte through raw
 21:  * slices except the rules deliberately changed.
 22:  */
 23: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 24: // Parsing
 25: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 26: /**
 27:  * Parse a stylesheet into a flat tree.
 28:  * Node shapes:
 29:  *   { type: 'rule', prelude, body, start, end, preludeStart }
 30:  *   { type: 'at', name, prelude, children|body, start, end }  (children when
 31:  *     the block contains rules: media/supports/layer/container/scope)
 32:  *   { type: 'comment', text, start, end }

 34: export function parseStylesheet(css, offset = 0) {
 35:   const text = String(css || '');
 36:   const nodes = [];
 37:   let i = 0;
 38:   const skipWs = () => { while (i < text.length && /\s/.test(text[i])) i++; };
 39:   while (i < text.length) {
 40:     skipWs();
 41:     if (i >= text.length) break;
 42:     if (text[i] === '/' && text[i + 1] === '*') {
 43:       const start = i;
 44:       const close = text.indexOf('*/', i + 2);
 45:       i = close === -1 ? text.length : close + 2;
 46:       nodes.push({ type: 'comment', text: text.slice(start, i), start: offset + start, end: offset + i });
 47:       continue;
 48:     }
 49:     const preludeStart = i;
 50:     const boundary = scanToBlockOrStatementEnd(text, i);
 51:     if (boundary.kind === 'none') break; // trailing garbage / declarations at top level
 52:     if (boundary.kind === 'statement') {
 53:       // Block-less at-statement (@import, @charset, @layer names;). Emitted
 54:       // as its own node so the FOLLOWING rule still indexes for
 55:       // reconciliation instead of being folded into this prelude.
 56:       const raw = text.slice(preludeStart, boundary.index + 1).trim();
 57:       if (raw) {
 58:         nodes.push({
 59:           type: 'at',
 60:           name: (raw.match(/^@([A-Za-z-]+)/) || [])[1] || '',

 62:           statement: true,
 63:           start: offset + preludeStart,
 64:           end: offset + boundary.index + 1,
 65:         });
 66:       }
 67:       i = boundary.index + 1;
 68:       continue;
 69:     }
 70:     const braceIdx = boundary.index;
 71:     const prelude = text.slice(preludeStart, braceIdx).trim();
 72:     const bodyStart = braceIdx + 1;
 73:     const bodyEnd = scanBlockEnd(text, bodyStart);
 74:     const body = text.slice(bodyStart, bodyEnd);
 75:     const nodeEnd = Math.min(text.length, bodyEnd + 1);
 76:     if (prelude.startsWith('@')) {
 77:       const name = (prelude.match(/^@([A-Za-z-]+)/) || [])[1] || '';
 78:       if (['media', 'supports', 'layer', 'container', 'scope'].includes(name)) {
 79:         nodes.push({
 80:           type: 'at',
 81:           name,
 82:           prelude,

 84:           start: offset + preludeStart,

 90:           name,
 91:           prelude,

 97:     } else if (prelude) {

 99:         type: 'rule',
100:         prelude,
101:         body,
102:         start: offset + preludeStart,
103:         end: offset + nodeEnd,
104:         preludeStart: offset + preludeStart,
105:       });
106:     }
107:     i = nodeEnd;
108:   }
109:   return nodes;
110: }
111: /**
112:  * Scan for the next structural boundary: the `{` opening a block, or the `;`

114:  * comment-aware). Returns { kind: 'block' | 'statement' | 'none', index }.
115:  */
116: function scanToBlockOrStatementEnd(text, from) {
117:   let i = from;
118:   let quote = null;
119:   while (i < text.length) {
120:     const ch = text[i];
121:     if (quote) {
122:       if (ch === '\\') i++;

124:     } else if (ch === '"' || ch === "'") {

128:       i = close === -1 ? text.length : close + 1;
129:     } else if (ch === '{') {

138: function scanBlockEnd(text, from) {
139:   let i = from;
140:   let depth = 1;
141:   let quote = null;
142:   while (i < text.length) {
143:     const ch = text[i];
144:     if (quote) {
145:       if (ch === '\\') i++;
146:       else if (ch === quote) quote = null;
147:     } else if (ch === '"' || ch === "'") {
148:       quote = ch;
149:     } else if (ch === '/' && text[i + 1] === '*') {
150:       const close = text.indexOf('*/', i + 2);
151:       i = close === -1 ? text.length : close + 1;
152:     } else if (ch === '{') {
153:       depth++;
154:     } else if (ch === '}') {
155:       depth--;
156:       if (depth === 0) return i;

158:     i++;
159:   }

163:   const out = [];
164:   for (const node of nodes) {
165:     if (node.type === 'comment') {
166:       out.push(indent + node.text);
167:     } else if (node.type === 'rule') {
168:       out.push(`${indent}${node.prelude} {${formatBody(node.body, indent)}}`);
169:     } else if (node.type === 'at' && node.children) {

171:       out.push(serializeNodes(node.children, indent + '  '));

173:     } else if (node.type === 'at' && node.statement) {

175:     } else if (node.type === 'at') {
176:       out.push(`${indent}${node.prelude} {${formatBody(node.body, indent)}}`);
177:     }
178:   }
179:   return out.join('\n');
180: }
181: function formatBody(body, indent) {
182:   const trimmed = String(body || '').trim();
183:   if (!trimmed) return ' ';
184:   const lines = trimmed.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter(Boolean);
185:   if (lines.length === 1 && lines[0].length < 60) return ` ${lines[0]} `;
186:   return '\n' + lines.map((l) => `${indent}  ${l}`).join('\n') + `\n${indent}`;

188: export function normalizeSelector(prelude) {
189:   return String(prelude || '')

194: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
195: // Reconciliation
196: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
197: /**
198:  * Merge variant CSS into existing CSS. Rules whose (at-context, normalized
199:  * selector) match an existing rule REPLACE that rule's body in place; new
200:  * rules append at the end under their at-context. Returns { css, replaced,
201:  * appended }.
202:  */
203: export function reconcileCss(existingCss, variantCss) {
204:   const existing = parseStylesheet(existingCss);
205:   const incoming = parseStylesheet(variantCss);
206:   let replaced = 0;
207:   let appended = 0;
208:   const mergeLevel = (existingNodes, incomingNodes) => {
209:     const index = new Map();
210:     for (const node of existingNodes) {
211:       if (node.type === 'rule') index.set(normalizeSelector(node.prelude), node);
212:     }
213:     const atIndex = new Map();
214:     for (const node of existingNodes) {
215:       if (node.type === 'at' && node.children) atIndex.set(normalizeSelector(node.prelude), node);
216:     }
217:     // Baking can leave several incoming rules with the same selector (e.g. a
218:     // base rule plus a stripped param branch). The first one REPLACES the
219:     // existing body; later same-selector rules extend it, never clobber it.
220:     const touched = new Set();
221:     for (const node of incomingNodes) {
222:       if (node.type === 'comment') continue;
223:       if (node.type === 'rule') {

225:         const match = index.get(key);
226:         if (match) {
227:           if (touched.has(key)) {

229:           } else if (match.body.trim() !== node.body.trim()) {

231:             replaced++;
232:           }
233:           touched.add(key);
234:         } else {

239:           const appendedNode = { ...node };

242:           else existingNodes.splice(firstAt, 0, appendedNode);

244:           touched.add(key);

254:           atIndex.set(key, existingNodes[existingNodes.length - 1]);

256:         }
257:       } else {

263:   mergeLevel(existing, incoming);

266: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
267: // Parameter baking
268: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
269: /**
270:  * Replace every `var(--p-<id>, fallback)` / `var(--p-<id>)` occurrence with a
271:  * literal value. Paren-aware: fallbacks containing calc()/nested vars are
272:  * handled, unlike the old `[^)]+` regex.

274: export function substituteParamVar(css, id, value) {

282:     const after = idx + needle.length;

284:     if (after < text.length && text[after] !== ')' && text[after] !== ',') {
285:       out += text.slice(i, after);
286:       i = after;
287:       continue;
288:     }
289:     let j = after;
290:     let depth = 1; // we are inside var(
291:     while (j < text.length && depth > 0) {

304: function isToggleOn(value) {

307: /**

326:     // the literal "on" form match while on; every other valued form
327:     // (["false"], ["0"], ...) never matched and is dead regardless of state.
328:     if (expected != null && expected !== 'on') {

330:       return '';

346: /**
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/live/accept-verify.mjs

````javascript
 1: /**
 2:  * Postcondition scanner for accepted/carbonized source. The carbonize
 3:  * contract used to exist only as prose in reference/live.md; nothing checked
 4:  * that an accept actually left the file clean, so dead param branches,
 5:  * preview attributes, and marker comments accumulated across sessions. This
 6:  * scanner is the mechanical form of that contract. live-complete refuses to
 7:  * mark a carbonize session complete while the file is dirty, and the
 8:  * mechanical Svelte accept runs it on its own output as a self-check.
 9:  */
10: // Param patterns are anchored to the exact shapes live mode writes
11: // (attribute-with-value / selector forms, var() references), not bare
12: // substrings, so user tokens that merely share the prefix cannot trip the
13: // completion gate.
14: const FORBIDDEN = [
15:   { marker: 'impeccable-variants-start', why: 'variant wrapper comment left in source' },
16:   { marker: 'impeccable-variants-end', why: 'variant wrapper comment left in source' },
17:   { marker: 'impeccable-carbonize-start', why: 'carbonize block not rewritten into permanent form' },
18:   { marker: 'impeccable-carbonize-end', why: 'carbonize block not rewritten into permanent form' },
19:   { marker: 'impeccable-param-values', why: 'param-values comment not baked and removed' },
20:   { marker: 'data-impeccable-', why: 'live-mode plumbing attribute left on markup' },
21:   { marker: /\bdata-p-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\s*(?:=|\])/, label: 'data-p-*', why: 'preview parameter attribute left on markup' },
22:   { marker: /var\(\s*--p-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\s*[,)]/, label: 'var(--p-*)', why: 'preview parameter variable not baked to a literal' },
23:   { marker: '--impeccable-variant-ready', why: 'preview readiness sentinel left in CSS' },
24: ];
25: /**
26:  * Scan file text for live-mode leftovers. Returns { clean, findings } where
27:  * each finding is { marker, line, excerpt, why }.
28:  */
29: export function verifyAcceptedSource(text) {
30:   const findings = [];
31:   const lines = String(text || '').split('\n');
32:   for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
33:     const line = lines[i];
34:     for (const { marker, label, why } of FORBIDDEN) {
35:       const hit = marker instanceof RegExp ? marker.test(line) : line.includes(marker);
36:       if (hit) {
37:         findings.push({
38:           marker: label || String(marker),
39:           line: i + 1,
40:           excerpt: line.trim().slice(0, 120),
41:           why,
42:         });
43:       }
44:     }
45:   }
46:   return { clean: findings.length === 0, findings };
47: }
48: /** Convenience wrapper for CLI callers: read + scan, tolerating a missing file. */
49: export function verifyAcceptedFile(fs, filePath) {
50:   let text;
51:   try {
52:     text = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');
53:   } catch {
54:     return { clean: true, findings: [], missing: true };
55:   }
56:   return { ...verifyAcceptedSource(text), missing: false };
57: }
````

````javascript
 9: export function completionTypeForAcceptResult(eventType, acceptResult) {
10:   if (eventType === 'discard') return acceptResult?.handled === true ? 'discarded' : 'error';
11:   if (acceptResult?.handled === true && acceptResult?.carbonize === true) return 'agent_done';
12:   if (acceptResult?.handled === true) return 'complete';
13:   if (acceptResult?.mode === 'error') return 'error';

20:     ack.final = false;

23:     ack.message = 'Carbonize cleanup must be verified, then the session must be completed explicitly before polling again.';
24:   }
````

````javascript
392:     marginTop: parseFloat(placeholder.style?.marginTop || '') || 0,
````

````javascript
792:       } else if (fs.existsSync(absolute)) {
793:         fs.rmSync(absolute);

814: export function summarizeManualApplyEvent(event = {}, batch = event.batch, cwd = process.cwd()) {

816:   const opCount = entries.reduce((sum, entry) => sum + (Array.isArray(entry.ops) ? entry.ops.length : 0), 0);
817:   return {

825: export function summarizeManualApplyFailures(failed, cwd = process.cwd()) {

834:     candidates: summarizeManualDiagnostics(item.candidates, cwd),

838:   if (!Array.isArray(items) || items.length === 0) return undefined;
839:   return items.slice(0, 12).map((item) => ({
840:     reason: item.reason || item.kind || undefined,
841:     detail: compactManualLogText(item.detail, 220),
842:     message: compactManualLogText(item.message, 300),
843:     file: summarizeManualLogFile(item.file || item.relativeFile, cwd),
844:     line: item.line || undefined,
845:     ref: compactManualLogText(item.ref, 180),
846:     marker: compactManualLogText(item.marker, 120),
847:     files: Array.isArray(item.files) ? item.files.slice(0, 8).map((file) => summarizeManualLogFile(file, cwd)).filter(Boolean) : undefined,
848:   }));

850: export function summarizeManualLogFile(file, cwd = process.cwd()) {
851:   if (!file || typeof file !== 'string') return undefined;
852:   if (!path.isAbsolute(file)) return file;
853:   const relative = path.relative(cwd, file);
854:   return relative && !relative.startsWith('..') && !path.isAbsolute(relative) ? relative : file;

856: export function compactManualLogText(value, max = 200) {
857:   if (typeof value !== 'string') return undefined;
858:   const normalized = value.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
859:   if (normalized.length <= max) return normalized;
860:   return normalized.slice(0, max) + `... [truncated ${normalized.length - max} chars]`;
861: }
````

````javascript
 2:   if (event.type === 'accept' || event.type === 'discard' || event.type === 'exit') return 0;

 9:   return entries
10:     .filter((entry) => !(entry.leaseUntil && entry.leaseUntil > now))
11:     .filter((entry) => !allowed || allowed.has(entry.event?.type))
````

````javascript
 11:  *                 just as it reports nothing through the CLI and the hook.

 16:  *                 and that rule would suppress site-wide (issue #639).

 30:  * additive across roots, matching readConfig's own union of config.json and
 31:  * config.local.json.
````

````javascript
 90: /** Collect names bound by a destructuring pattern (each contexts, const tags). */

102:       return out;
103:     case 'ArrayPattern':
104:       for (const el of pattern.elements || []) if (el) collectPatternNames(el, out);
105:       return out;
106:     case 'AssignmentPattern':
107:       collectPatternNames(pattern.left, out);
108:       return out;
109:     case 'RestElement':
110:       collectPatternNames(pattern.argument, out);

113:       return out;

116: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
117: // Template analysis
118: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
119: class Analysis {
120:   constructor(source) {
121:     this.source = source;
122:     this.replacements = []; // { start, end, prop } source ranges to swap
123:     this.contract = [];     // [{ prop, expr, kind, ... }]
124:     this.byExpr = new Map(); // expr text -> contract entry
125:     this.usedNames = new Set();
126:     this.unsupported = null;
127:   }
128:   fail(reason) {
129:     if (!this.unsupported) this.unsupported = reason;
130:   }
131:   propFor(exprText, kind, extra = {}) {
132:     const existing = this.byExpr.get(exprText);
133:     if (existing) return existing;
134:     const base = derivePropName(exprText);
135:     let name = base;
136:     let n = 2;
137:     while (this.usedNames.has(name)) name = `${base}${n++}`;
138:     this.usedNames.add(name);
139:     const entry = { prop: name, expr: exprText, kind, ...extra };
140:     this.byExpr.set(exprText, entry);
141:     this.contract.push(entry);
142:     return entry;
143:   }
144: }
145: // A derived prop name lands in `let { <name> } = $props()`; a reserved word

147: const RESERVED_PROP_NAMES = new Set([
148:   'await', 'break', 'case', 'catch', 'class', 'const', 'continue', 'debugger',
149:   'default', 'delete', 'do', 'else', 'enum', 'export', 'extends', 'false',
150:   'finally', 'for', 'function', 'if', 'implements', 'import', 'in',
151:   'instanceof', 'interface', 'let', 'new', 'null', 'package', 'private',
152:   'protected', 'public', 'return', 'static', 'super', 'switch', 'this',
153:   'throw', 'true', 'try', 'typeof', 'undefined', 'var', 'void', 'while',
154:   'with', 'yield',
155: ]);
156: export function derivePropName(expr) {
157:   const tail = String(expr).match(/(?:\.|\[["']?)([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)["']?\]?\s*$/);

161:   return RESERVED_PROP_NAMES.has(candidate) ? `${candidate}Value` : candidate;

163: function exprText(source, node) {

166: // Identifiers that resolve in ANY module scope. They are neither hydratable

172:   'Object', 'Map', 'Set', 'Promise', 'RegExp', 'NaN', 'Infinity', 'undefined',

177: function classifyRoots(node, scopes) {

180:   let free = 0;
181:   for (const name of roots) {

188: function isFree(node, scopes) {

192: /**
193:  * An expression mixing loop-bound and outer free identifiers (e.g.

199:  */

201:   const { bound, free } = classifyRoots(node, scopes);

205:   }

207: }
208: /**

212: function analyzeFragment(fragment, analysis, scopes) {

226: function analyzeNode(node, analysis, scopes) {

320:     case 'KeyBlock': {

364:     case 'RenderTag':

382: function analyzeAttributes(node, analysis, scopes) {

394:           const entry = analysis.propFor(text, kind);

397:         break;
398:       }

401:         if (expr && failOnMixedExpression(expr, scopes, analysis, analysis.source)) return;

465: /**

496:   // transform ({Math.round(r.score)} hydrates `score`). Shapes it cannot
497:   // represent split two ways: CRASHY ones would throw at mount time against a

501:   // also fall back in text position, where the damage is visible.

521:       }

532:         }
533:         case 'MemberExpression': {

535:             !node.computed

537:             && boundAs(node.object.name, scopeInfos) === 'item'

540:             touches = true;

542:             if (ctx.memberObject || ctx.callee) { crashy = true; return; }
543:             keys.add(node.property.name);
544:             return;
545:           }
546:           visit(node.object, { memberObject: true });
547:           if (node.computed) visit(node.property, {});
548:           return;
549:         }
550:         case 'CallExpression':

554:         case 'ArrowFunctionExpression':

560:         }
561:         case 'Property':
562:           if (node.computed) visit(node.key, {});
563:           visit(node.value, {});
564:           return;

566:           for (const key of Object.keys(node)) {
567:             if (key === 'type' || key === 'start' || key === 'end' || key === 'loc' || key === 'range' || key === 'parent') continue;
568:             visit(node[key], {});
569:           }
570:         }
571:       }
572:     };
573:     visit(expression, {});
574:     if (crashy) return { crashy: true };
575:     if (lossy || keys.size > 1) return { lossy: true };
576:     if (!touches || keys.size === 0) return { skip: true };
577:     return { key: [...keys][0] };

588:     return classes;
589:   };
590:   const scopeInfoOf = (eachNode) => {
591:     const names = new Set();
592:     if (eachNode.context) collectPatternNames(eachNode.context, names);
593:     return {
594:       names,
595:       itemName: eachNode.context?.type === 'Identifier' ? eachNode.context.name : null,
596:       indexName: eachNode.index || null,
````

````javascript
108: export function patchTanStackRoot(content, componentImport) {
109:   let out = String(content || '');
110:   const importStatement = `import ImpeccableLiveRoot from '${componentImport}';`;
111:   if (!out.includes(importStatement)) {
112:     out = insertAfterLastImport(out, importStatement);
113:   }
114:   if (!out.includes(TANSTACK_MARKER_OPEN)) {
115:     const block =
116:       `${TANSTACK_MARKER_OPEN}\n`
117:       + `        <ImpeccableLiveRoot />\n`
118:       + `        ${TANSTACK_MARKER_CLOSE}\n        `;
119:     // Anchor before <Scripts …/> (the stable TanStack Start document marker);
120:     // fall back to before </body>.
121:     const scriptsMatch = out.match(/<Scripts\b/);
122:     if (scriptsMatch) {
123:       out = out.slice(0, scriptsMatch.index) + block + out.slice(scriptsMatch.index);
124:     } else {
125:       const bodyClose = out.lastIndexOf('</body>');
126:       if (bodyClose !== -1) {
127:         out = out.slice(0, bodyClose) + block + out.slice(bodyClose);
128:       }
129:     }
130:   }
131:   return out;
132: }
133: export function unpatchTanStackRoot(content) {
134:   let out = String(content || '');
135:   // Remove exactly the inserted block (open marker → component → close marker →
136:   // trailing newline + the indent that leads back to the anchor). Leaving the
137:   // leading indent before the open marker intact hands it back to the anchor
138:   // (e.g. `<Scripts />`) so the file round-trips byte-for-byte.
139:   const blockRe = new RegExp(
140:     escapeRegExp(TANSTACK_MARKER_OPEN)
141:     + '\\s*<ImpeccableLiveRoot\\s*/>\\s*'
142:     + escapeRegExp(TANSTACK_MARKER_CLOSE)
143:     + '\\r?\\n?[ \\t]*',
144:     'g',
145:   );
146:   out = out.replace(blockRe, '');
147:   // Remove only the managed import line — not any following blank line.
148:   out = out.replace(
149:     new RegExp("^import ImpeccableLiveRoot from '[^']*';[ \\t]*\\r?\\n", 'gm'),
150:     '',
151:   );
152:   return out;
153: }
154: export function buildTanStackLiveRootComponent(port, token) {
155:   const liveSrc = buildLiveScriptSrc(Number(port), token);
156:   return `/* impeccable-live-tanstack-start */
157: import { useEffect } from 'react';
158: const LIVE_SRC = '${liveSrc}';
159: const LIVE_SELECTOR = 'script[data-impeccable-live-tanstack]';
160: // Dev-only mount for Impeccable Live. TanStack Start server-renders the root
161: // document, so this appends the live-mode bundle from the client after
162: // hydration (mirrors the Nuxt/SvelteKit adapters). Renders nothing on the
163: // server, so there is no hydration mismatch.
164: export default function ImpeccableLiveRoot() {
165:   useEffect(() => {
166:     if (typeof document === 'undefined') return;
167:     const expected = new URL(LIVE_SRC, window.location.href).href;
168:     let script = document.querySelector(LIVE_SELECTOR);
169:     if (script && script.src === expected) return;
170:     if (script) script.remove();
171:     script = document.createElement('script');
172:     script.src = LIVE_SRC;
173:     script.async = true;
174:     script.setAttribute('data-impeccable-live-tanstack', '');
175:     script.setAttribute('data-impeccable-live-script', 'true');
176:     document.head.appendChild(script);
177:     return () => {
178:       if (script && script.isConnected) script.remove();
179:     };
180:   }, []);
181:   return null;
182: }
183: `;
184: }
185: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
186: // helpers
187: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
188: // The managed mount component carries the `impeccable-live-tanstack` marker in
189: // its leading comment and its script data-attribute; user files never do.
190: function isManagedComponent(content) {
191:   return String(content || '').includes('impeccable-live-tanstack');
192: }
193: function relativeImportSpecifier(fromFile, toFile) {
194:   const rel = path.posix.relative(
195:     path.posix.dirname(fromFile.split(path.sep).join('/')),
196:     toFile.split(path.sep).join('/'),
197:   ).replace(/\.(tsx|ts|jsx|js)$/, '');
198:   return rel.startsWith('.') ? rel : `./${rel}`;
199: }
200: function insertAfterLastImport(content, importStatement) {
201:   const importRe = /^import\b[^\n]*\n/gm;
202:   let lastEnd = -1;
203:   let m;
204:   while ((m = importRe.exec(content)) !== null) {
205:     lastEnd = m.index + m[0].length;
206:   }
207:   if (lastEnd === -1) {
208:     return `${importStatement}\n${content}`;
209:   }
210:   return content.slice(0, lastEnd) + importStatement + '\n' + content.slice(lastEnd);
211: }
212: function pruneEmptyDir(dir, stopDir) {
213:   let current = dir;
214:   while (current.startsWith(stopDir) && current !== stopDir) {
215:     try {
216:       if (fs.readdirSync(current).length > 0) return;
217:       fs.rmdirSync(current);
218:       current = path.dirname(current);
219:     } catch {
220:       return;
221:     }
222:   }
223: }
224: function escapeRegExp(value) {
225:   return String(value).replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
226: }
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/build-phase.mjs
````javascript
  1: #!/usr/bin/env node
  2: /**
  3:  * build-phase: the comp-led build as a state machine on disk, so the phases
  4:  * new-work.md names are gated by scripts instead of remembered by the model.
  5:  *
  6:  * State lives at .impeccable/build/state.json. Phases, in order:
  7:  *
  8:  *   comps     the comp round: three comps of the chosen direction under
  9:  *             .impeccable/mocks/ with prompt sidecars, one approved by the
 10:  *             user (sidecar "approved": true). Skipped when start names an
 11:  *             approved --comp (a surface round already locked one).
 12:  *   spec      the approved comp is measured (comp-spec.mjs wrote spec.json)
 13:  *   plates    every raster region in the spec has its plate on disk
 14:  *   hero      the first viewport is reproduced: comp-diff of hero-repro.png
 15:  *             against the comp clears the gate
 16:  *   sections  the rest of the surface is built inside the spec's system
 17:  *   motion    interaction, reveals, motion
 18:  *   responsive the other viewports
 19:  *   review    the finish reviewer ran; disposition recorded
 20:  *
 21:  *   node build-phase.mjs start --comp <approved.png> [--breakpoint 1440x900] [--artifact index.html]
 22:  *   node build-phase.mjs start --direction <seed key>      # no comp yet: opens the comps phase first
 23:  *   node build-phase.mjs status                # human-readable, plus NEXT line
 24:  *   node build-phase.mjs status --json
 25:  *   node build-phase.mjs advance               # try to close the current phase; runs its gate
 26:  *   node build-phase.mjs advance --force --reason "<why>"   # skip a gate; recorded, never silent
 27:  *   node build-phase.mjs record hero --build .impeccable/review/hero-repro.png   # run the hero gate explicitly
 28:  *   node build-phase.mjs note "<text>"         # append a note to the current phase
 29:  *   node build-phase.mjs finish --disposition ship|fix|rebuild|recapture
 30:  *
 31:  * Gates:
 32:  *   comps     -> >= 3 comp rasters (png/webp/jpg) directly under
 33:  *                .impeccable/mocks/ (decision/ excluded), each with a .json
 34:  *                sidecar, and exactly one sidecar carrying "approved": true;
 35:  *                closing records that file as the state's comp.
 36:  *   spec      -> spec.json exists and has >= 1 region
 37:  *   plates    -> every region with medium raster has its plate file, decodable,
 38:  *                at least 1.5x the comp region's pixel width (textures
 39:  *                exempt), and reads as the region against the masked comp
 40:  *                crop: structure >= PLATE_STRUCTURE_MIN and comp-diff overall
 41:  *                >= PLATE_MIN (textures: palette + grain only). Structure is
 42:  *                the floor because it is what a wrong-but-busy plate cannot
 43:  *                fake: noise, a mirror, a mosaic, another region all keep
 44:  *                the palette and the energy and lose structure. A missing
 45:  *                or thin plate names itself.
 46:  *   hero      -> every plate is referenced by a source file (the artifact
 47:  *                named at start, else a bounded walk of the project), and
 48:  *                .impeccable/review/hero-repro.png exists and comp-diff overall
 49:  *                >= HERO_MIN (default 0.72) with no region `missing`. The
 50:  *                score, the report path, and the attempt count are recorded.
 51:  *   responsive -> .impeccable/review/desktop.png and mobile.png exist, and
 52:  *                the desktop capture still scores >= RESPONSIVE_MIN against
 53:  *                the comp with no region missing: a first viewport that only
 54:  *                holds at the comp's exact width is not built.
 55:  *   sections / motion -> no mechanical gate; advancing records the moment,
 56:  *                and the finish reviewer reads the timeline.
 57:  *
 58:  * Exit codes: 0 ok / advanced, 2 gate failed (state unchanged, reasons
 59:  * printed), 1 usage.
 60:  *
 61:  * Nothing here needs a browser. Screenshots come from the harness; this
 62:  * script only measures them.
 63:  */
 64: import fs from 'node:fs';
 65: import path from 'node:path';
 66: import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
 67: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
 68: import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
 69: import { decodePng, loadRaster } from './lib/png.mjs';
 70: const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
 71: import { crop, createImage, blit, resize } from './lib/raster.mjs';
 72: import { structureScore } from './lib/image-metrics.mjs';
 73: import { compare, verdictFor, alignBuild, bestShift } from './comp-diff.mjs';
 74: import { textRegionCheck, chromeStripCheck, inventedInk, plateClipCheck, svgIllustrations } from './lib/hero-checks.mjs';
 75: import { SPEC_PATH, BUILD_DIR, loadSpec, plateReference } from './comp-spec.mjs';
 76: import { choiceStamped } from './font-match.mjs';
 77: const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
 78: export const STATE_PATH = path.join(BUILD_DIR, 'state.json');
 79: export const PHASES = ['comps', 'spec', 'plates', 'hero', 'sections', 'motion', 'responsive', 'review'];
 80: export const MOCKS_DIR = path.join('.impeccable', 'mocks');
 81: export const HERO_MIN = 0.72;
 82: export const RESPONSIVE_MIN = 0.65;
 83: export const PLATE_MIN = 0.4;
 84: export const PLATE_STRUCTURE_MIN = 0.4;
 85: export const HERO_REPRO = path.join('.impeccable', 'review', 'hero-repro.png');
 86: function arg(name, fallback = null) {
 87:   const i = process.argv.indexOf(`--${name}`);
 88:   if (i === -1) return fallback;
 89:   const v = process.argv[i + 1];
 90:   return v && !v.startsWith('--') ? v : fallback;
 91: }
 92: const flag = (name) => process.argv.includes(`--${name}`);
 93: const now = () => new Date().toISOString();
 94: /** The recorded build path (config.local.json over config.json), or null. */
 95: export function readBuildPath(cwd = process.cwd()) {
 96:   let value = null;
 97:   for (const name of ['config.json', 'config.local.json']) {
 98:     try {
 99:       const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(cwd, '.impeccable', name), 'utf8'));
100:       if (raw?.buildPath === 'comp' || raw?.buildPath === 'code') value = raw.buildPath;
101:     } catch { /* absent */ }
102:   }
103:   return value;
104: }
105: /**
106:  * Whether a direction was dealt and the build never started, or started and
107:  * stopped before the hero gate: the condition context.mjs and detect.mjs
108:  * report as COMP_ROUND_OPEN when page code exists. Returns null when the
109:  * build path is code-led (no round owed) or nothing is pending.
110:  */
111: export function compRoundOpen(cwd = process.cwd()) {
112:   const buildPath = readBuildPath(cwd);
113:   if (buildPath === 'code') return null;
114:   const pending = path.join(cwd, BUILD_DIR, 'pending.json');
115:   const statePath = path.join(cwd, STATE_PATH);
116:   if (fs.existsSync(pending) && !fs.existsSync(statePath)) return { reason: 'a direction was chosen (concept-seed rolled) but build-phase.mjs start never ran', pending };
117:   if (fs.existsSync(statePath)) {
118:     try {
119:       const st = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(statePath, 'utf8'));
120:       const idx = PHASES.indexOf(st.phase);
121:       if (idx !== -1 && idx <= PHASES.indexOf('hero') && st.phases?.comps?.status !== 'skipped' && st.phases?.comps?.status !== 'closed') return { reason: `build-phase is at ${st.phase}; the comps phase never closed`, state: statePath };
122:       if (idx !== -1 && idx <= PHASES.indexOf('hero')) return { reason: `build-phase is at ${st.phase}; the hero gate has not passed`, state: statePath };
123:     } catch { /* unreadable: say nothing */ }
124:   }
125:   return null;
126: }
127: export function loadState(statePath = STATE_PATH) {
128:   if (!fs.existsSync(statePath)) return null;
129:   return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(statePath, 'utf8'));
130: }
131: export function saveState(state, statePath = STATE_PATH) {
132:   fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(statePath), { recursive: true });
133:   fs.writeFileSync(statePath, JSON.stringify(state, null, 2));
134: }
135: export function newState({ comp = null, breakpoint = null, artifact = null, direction = null }) {
136:   const first = comp ? 'spec' : 'comps';
137:   const phases = Object.fromEntries(PHASES.map((p) => [p, { status: p === first ? 'open' : 'pending', openedAt: p === first ? now() : null, closedAt: null, attempts: 0, notes: [], gate: null, forced: null }]));
138:   if (comp) { phases.comps.status = 'skipped'; phases.comps.notes.push({ at: now(), text: 'started with an approved comp; the comp round happened before this state (surface round or manual)' }); }
139:   return {
140:     tool: 'build-phase',
141:     version: 2,
142:     startedAt: now(),
143:     comp,
144:     direction,
145:     breakpoint,
146:     artifact,
147:     phase: first,
148:     phases,
149:     finish: null,
150:   };
151: }
152: // ---- gates -----------------------------------------------------------------
153: /** Comp rasters directly under the mocks dir, with their sidecars. */
154: export function listComps(mocksDir = MOCKS_DIR) {
155:   if (!fs.existsSync(mocksDir)) return [];
156:   const out = [];
157:   for (const name of fs.readdirSync(mocksDir)) {
158:     if (!/\.(png|webp|jpe?g)$/i.test(name)) continue;
159:     const file = path.join(mocksDir, name);
160:     if (!fs.statSync(file).isFile()) continue;
161:     const sidecarPath = `${file}.json`;
162:     let sidecar = null;
163:     if (fs.existsSync(sidecarPath)) { try { sidecar = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(sidecarPath, 'utf8')); } catch { sidecar = null; } }
164:     out.push({ file, sidecarPath, sidecar, approved: !!(sidecar && sidecar.approved === true) });
165:   }
166:   return out;
167: }
168: export function gateComps(state, { mocksDir = MOCKS_DIR } = {}) {
169:   const comps = listComps(mocksDir);
170:   const reasons = [];
171:   if (comps.length < 3) reasons.push(`${comps.length} comp${comps.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} under ${mocksDir}; the comp round puts three compositional options of the chosen direction in front of the user (reference/visualize.md). Generate the missing ones (harness image tool or generate-image.mjs), each with a .json sidecar holding its prompt.`);
172:   const noSidecar = comps.filter((c) => !c.sidecar);
173:   if (noSidecar.length) reasons.push(`no prompt sidecar for: ${noSidecar.map((c) => path.basename(c.file)).join(', ')} (write <file>.json with { "prompt": "..." }; generate-image.mjs does this itself)`);
174:   const approved = comps.filter((c) => c.approved);
175:   if (approved.length === 0) reasons.push('no comp is approved: put the three comps in front of the user (decision page via serve-question.mjs, or the structured question tool), then set "approved": true in the chosen comp\'s sidecar. A delegated pick is recorded the same way and disclosed.');
176:   if (approved.length > 1) reasons.push(`${approved.length} comps carry "approved": true; exactly one is the approved comp: ${approved.map((c) => path.basename(c.file)).join(', ')}`);
177:   return { ok: reasons.length === 0, reasons, summary: `${comps.length} comps, ${approved.length} approved`, approved: approved.length === 1 ? approved[0].file : null };
178: }
179: export function gateSpec(state, { specPath = SPEC_PATH } = {}) {
180:   const spec = loadSpec(specPath);
181:   if (!spec) return { ok: false, reasons: [`no spec at ${specPath}: run comp-spec.mjs --comp ${state.comp} --grid, name the regions, then --regions regions.json`] };
182:   if (!spec.regions || spec.regions.length < 1) return { ok: false, reasons: ['spec has no regions'] };
183:   if (spec.comp && state.comp && path.resolve(spec.comp) !== path.resolve(state.comp)) {
184:     return { ok: false, reasons: [`spec measures ${spec.comp}, but this build started on ${state.comp}; re-run comp-spec on the approved comp`] };
185:   }
186:   const plates = spec.regions.filter((r) => r.medium === 'raster').length;
187:   // A plate box that cuts its artwork is a plate the page will crop.
188:   const cut = spec.regions.filter((r) => r.medium === 'raster' && r.clipped && r.clipped.length);
189:   if (cut.length) return { ok: false, reasons: cut.map((r) => `region ${r.id}: the comp's artwork runs off its box on the ${r.clipped.join(' and ')}; widen the region's span so the box holds the whole shape with a margin (or set "bleed": true if the page really crops it there), then re-run comp-spec.mjs --regions`) };
190:   // Type is measured, not guessed: the largest text region must carry a
191:   // font-match measurement and a ranked choice before page code exists.
192:   // Three of six misses a human called on a first-round build were the
193:   // headline face wider and lighter than the comp's, the parts list smaller,
194:   // the footer heavier: ratios font-match reads off pixels.
195:   // The lead text region is the display type: the region whose measured cap
196:   // height is largest (a headline), not the biggest box (a table of rows).
197:   // Unmeasured regions sort by box height as a proxy until measured.
198:   const textRegions = spec.regions.filter((r) => r.kind === 'text').sort((a, b) => {
199:     const ca = a.type && a.type.comp ? a.type.comp.capHeightPx : a.px.h * 0.4;
200:     const cb = b.type && b.type.comp ? b.type.comp.capHeightPx : b.px.h * 0.4;
201:     return cb - ca;
202:   });
203:   const reasons = [];
204:   if (textRegions.length) {
205:     // when nothing is measured yet, ask for all measurements first; the lead
206:     // is only knowable once cap heights exist
207:     const anyMeasured = textRegions.some((r) => r.type);
208:     if (!anyMeasured) {
209:       reasons.push(`measure the type before closing the spec: node ${HERE}/font-match.mjs --measure <id> for each text region (${textRegions.map((r) => r.id).join(', ')}); the region with the largest cap height is the lead and gets --rank.`);
210:       return { ok: false, reasons };
211:     }
212:     const measurable = textRegions.filter((r) => r.type && r.type.comp);
213:     const lead = measurable[0] || textRegions[0];
214:     if (!lead.type) reasons.push(`the lead text region ${lead.id} has no type measurement: run node ${HERE}/font-match.mjs --measure ${lead.id} (and --rank ${lead.id} --text "<its first words>" to choose the face by metrics). Set font-size from the printed cap height; do not pick a face by name.`);
215:     else if (lead.type.comp && !lead.type.chosen) reasons.push(`the lead text region ${lead.id} is measured (${lead.type.widthClass} ${lead.type.weightClass}, cap ${lead.type.comp.capHeightPx}px) but no face is ranked: run node ${HERE}/font-match.mjs --rank ${lead.id} --text "<its first words>" [--candidates "Family:weight,..."] and use the USE line.`);
216:     else if (lead.type.comp && lead.type.chosen && !choiceStamped(lead.id, lead.type.chosen)) reasons.push(`the lead text region ${lead.id} carries a "chosen" face that font-match did not write (${lead.type.chosen.family || '?'}). A face typed into spec.json is the guess this gate exists to refuse; run node ${HERE}/font-match.mjs --rank ${lead.id} --text "<its first words>" and let it record the choice (with no browser it records the catalog's nearest face).`);
217:     const unmeasured = textRegions.slice(1).filter((r) => !r.type).map((r) => r.id);
218:     if (unmeasured.length && !reasons.length) reasons.push(`measure the other text regions too, each sets its own font-size and weight class: node ${HERE}/font-match.mjs --measure <id> for ${unmeasured.join(', ')}`);
219:   }
220:   if (reasons.length) return { ok: false, reasons };
221:   return { ok: true, reasons: [], summary: `${spec.regions.length} regions, ${plates} plates, ${textRegions.length} text regions measured` };
222: }
223: /**
224:  * The one plate rule, shared by the plates gate and generate-image's
225:  * PLATE-WARN so they never disagree. `score` is compare().whole against the
226:  * masked comp crop under cover alignment.
227:  */
228: export function plateVerdict(region, score) {
229:   const isTexture = region.kind === 'texture';
230:   const reasons = [];
231:   if (isTexture) {
232:     const effective = 0.5 * score.color + 0.5 * Math.min(1, score.detail / 0.6);
233:     if (effective < PLATE_MIN) reasons.push(`scores ${(effective * 100).toFixed(0)}% as the material of region ${region.id} (color ${(score.color * 100).toFixed(0)}%, detail ${(score.detail * 100).toFixed(0)}%); crop a clean patch of the comp region (comp-spec.mjs --crop ${region.id} --raw) and mirror-tile it, generate only when no clean patch exists`);
234:     return { ok: reasons.length === 0, reasons, effective };
235:   }
236:   // Added detail is invented material only when the comp region is calm;
237:   // a paper sleeve is grainy in the comp too, and its plate is allowed the
238:   // same grain. Comp energy travels on the region (comp-spec's detail.energy).
239:   const compCalm = !region.detail || region.detail.energy < 12;
240:   if (compCalm && score.detailAdded > 0.45) reasons.push(`carries detail the comp region ${region.id} does not have (added-detail ${(score.detailAdded * 100).toFixed(0)}% of cells): noise, grain, or a busier subject where the comp is calm; regenerate from the crop reference without adding texture`);
241:   if (score.structure < PLATE_STRUCTURE_MIN) reasons.push(`structure ${(score.structure * 100).toFixed(0)}% against the comp region ${region.id}: the composition of the plate is not the region's (different subject, orientation, or crop); regenerate with comp-spec.mjs --crop ${region.id} as the reference image`);
242:   if (score.overall < PLATE_MIN) reasons.push(`scores ${(score.overall * 100).toFixed(0)}% against the comp region ${region.id} (structure ${(score.structure * 100).toFixed(0)}%, color ${(score.color * 100).toFixed(0)}%, detail ${(score.detail * 100).toFixed(0)}%); regenerate with the crop as --ref and the comp-spec plate prompt`);
243:   return { ok: reasons.length === 0, reasons, effective: score.overall };
244: }
245: export function gatePlates(state, { specPath = SPEC_PATH } = {}) {
246:   const spec = loadSpec(specPath);
247:   if (!spec) return { ok: false, reasons: ['no spec'] };
248:   const rasterRegions = spec.regions.filter((r) => r.medium === 'raster');
249:   if (!rasterRegions.length) return { ok: true, reasons: [], summary: 'no plates owed', plates: [] };
250:   let comp = null;
251:   try { comp = loadRaster(spec.comp).image; } catch { /* scored without the comp crop below */ }
252:   const reasons = [], plates = [];
253:   for (const r of rasterRegions) {
254:     const file = r.plate;
255:     if (!file || !fs.existsSync(file)) { reasons.push(`plate missing for ${r.id}: expected ${file || '(no path)'}; produce it from comp-spec.mjs --crop ${r.id} with generate-image.mjs --plate`); plates.push({ id: r.id, file, status: 'missing' }); continue; }
256:     let img;
257:     try { img = decodePng(fs.readFileSync(file)); } catch (e) { reasons.push(`plate ${file} is not a decodable PNG: ${e.message}`); plates.push({ id: r.id, file, status: 'unreadable' }); continue; }
258:     // A texture tiles, so it owes no size floor and no structural match:
259:     // it is judged on palette and grain only. Every other plate must be at
260:     // least 1.5x the region (capped at 1536px, the largest size the
261:     // generators emit; past that the region is a full-bleed field the page
262:     // scales) and read as the region under object-fit: cover.
263:     const isTexture = r.kind === 'texture';
264:     const minW = Math.min(1536, r.px.w * 1.5);
265:     if (!isTexture && img.width < minW) reasons.push(`plate ${file} is ${img.width}px wide; the comp region is ${r.px.w}px and a shipping plate needs at least ${Math.round(minW)}px. Regenerate at asset size, do not crop the comp.`);
266:     let score = null;
267:     if (comp) {
268:       const ref = plateReference(comp, spec, r);
269:       // a keyed (alpha) plate ships over the page ground: score it composited
270:       // over the region's sampled ground, the way it will show
271:       let build = img;
272:       let transparent = 0; for (let i = 3; i < img.data.length; i += 4) if (img.data[i] < 128) transparent++;
273:       if (transparent > (img.data.length / 4) * 0.05) {
274:         const g = (r.palette && r.palette[0] && r.palette[0].hex) || '#ffffff';
275:         const m = /^#?([0-9a-f]{2})([0-9a-f]{2})([0-9a-f]{2})$/i.exec(g);
276:         const ground = m ? [parseInt(m[1], 16), parseInt(m[2], 16), parseInt(m[3], 16), 255] : [255, 255, 255, 255];
277:         const over = createImage(img.width, img.height, ground);
278:         blit(over, img, 0, 0);
279:         build = over;
280:       }
281:       const res = compare({ comp: ref, build, align: 'cover', spec: null, kind: r.kind });
282:       score = res.whole;
283:       const v = plateVerdict(r, score);
284:       for (const reason of v.reasons) reasons.push(`plate ${file}: ${reason}`);
285:       // A plate that matches the comp crop almost exactly is the comp crop,
286:       // upscaled past the size floor: the comp's grain, its neighbours'
287:       // edges, and its resolution ship as the artwork. Crops are never
288:       // plates; the crop is the reference the plate is generated from.
289:       // A fake-mode plate (offline pipelines, eval fixtures) IS the crop by
290:       // design and says so in its tEXt; the identity refusal is for models
291:       // shipping the comp's pixels as artwork, not for the deterministic
292:       // stand-in.
293:       const isFake = img.text && img.text['impeccable:fake'] === '1';
294:       if (!isTexture && !isFake) {
295:         const raw = crop(comp, r.px.x, r.px.y, r.px.w, r.px.h);
296:         const same = structureScore(raw, resize(img, raw.width, raw.height));
297:         if (same >= 0.95) reasons.push(`plate ${file} is the comp crop of region ${r.id} (structure ${(same * 100).toFixed(0)}% against the raw region, a resample of the same pixels): a crop of the comp is never a plate; generate the plate from the crop as reference (generate-image.mjs --plate ${r.id})`);
298:       }
299:     }
300:     plates.push({ id: r.id, file, status: 'ok', size: `${img.width}x${img.height}`, score: score ? score.overall : null });
301:   }
302:   return { ok: reasons.length === 0, reasons, summary: `${plates.filter((p) => p.status === 'ok').length}/${rasterRegions.length} plates`, plates };
303: }
304: /** Source files that could reference a plate: bounded walk, skipping deps and build output. */
305: function sourceFiles(root = '.', limit = 400) {
306:   const out = [];
307:   // `assets` is walked: the extension filter already keeps binaries out, and
308:   // a stylesheet at assets/hero.css may be the one file that references a
309:   // plate (Greptile P1 on #599: the gate refused a valid build for it).
310:   const skip = new Set(['node_modules', '.git', 'dist', 'build', 'out', '.next', '.svelte-kit', '.impeccable', 'coverage']);
311:   const exts = /\.(html?|css|scss|jsx?|tsx?|svelte|vue|astro|mdx?|php|erb|hbs)$/i;
312:   const walk = (dir, depth) => {
313:     if (out.length >= limit || depth > 6) return;
314:     let entries = [];
315:     try { entries = fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }); } catch { return; }
316:     for (const e of entries) {
317:       if (out.length >= limit) return;
318:       if (e.isDirectory()) { if (!skip.has(e.name) && !e.name.startsWith('.')) walk(path.join(dir, e.name), depth + 1); }
319:       else if (exts.test(e.name)) out.push(path.join(dir, e.name));
320:     }
321:   };
322:   walk(root, 0);
323:   return out;
324: }
325: /** Plates the artifact never references: a plate on disk that no source names ships nothing. */
326: export function unreferencedPlates(spec, artifact = null) {
327:   const plates = (spec?.regions || []).filter((r) => r.medium === 'raster' && r.plate);
328:   if (!plates.length) return [];
329:   // The artifact narrows nothing: a plate may be referenced only from a
330:   // stylesheet the artifact links, so the source walk runs either way, the
331:   // artifact keeps a seat in the corpus, and the stylesheets it links are
332:   // added by name (resolved against the artifact's own directory), which
333:   // covers a stylesheet outside the walk's root, depth, or file limit.
334:   const linked = [];
335:   if (artifact && fs.existsSync(artifact)) {
336:     linked.push(artifact);
337:     try {
338:       const html = fs.readFileSync(artifact, 'utf8');
339:       for (const m of html.matchAll(/<link\b[^>]*href=["']([^"']+)["'][^>]*>/gi)) {
340:         const href = m[1];
341:         if (/^(https?:|data:|\/\/)/i.test(href)) continue;
342:         if (!/rel=["']?stylesheet/i.test(m[0]) && !/\.css(\?|$)/i.test(href)) continue;
343:         const clean = href.split('?')[0];
344:         // a root-relative href serves from the project root, not the drive
345:         // root: try the working directory and the artifact's own directory
346:         // (unreadable candidates are skipped by the corpus loop)
347:         if (clean.startsWith('/')) { linked.push(path.join(process.cwd(), clean), path.join(path.dirname(artifact), clean)); }
348:         else linked.push(path.resolve(path.dirname(artifact), clean));
349:       }
350:     } catch { /* the artifact still counts */ }
351:   }
352:   const files = [...new Set([...linked, ...sourceFiles()])];
353:   let corpus = '';
354:   for (const f of files) { try { corpus += fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8') + '\n'; } catch { /* skip */ } }
355:   const missing = [];
356:   for (const r of plates) {
357:     const base = path.basename(r.plate);
358:     const stem = base.replace(/\.[a-z0-9]+$/i, '');
359:     // a data URI inline copy counts when the region id or file stem is named beside it
360:     if (corpus.includes(base) || (corpus.includes('data:image/') && (corpus.includes(stem) || corpus.includes(r.id)))) continue;
361:     missing.push(r);
362:   }
363:   return missing;
364: }
365: /** Organic clip-path findings whose selector's element the artifact places (by class/id name) on a raster region. Cheap heuristic: the finding's selector or the surrounding rule mentions the region id or its plate stem. */
366: export function organicClipRegions(artifactFile, spec) {
367:   let scan;
368:   try {
369:     const mod = require(path.join(HERE, '..', '..', 'cli', 'engine', 'rules', 'checks.mjs'));
370:     scan = mod.scanCssTextForOrganicClipPath;
371:   } catch { scan = null; }
372:   if (!scan) return [];
373:   let html = '';
374:   try { html = fs.readFileSync(artifactFile, 'utf8'); } catch { return []; }
375:   const findings = scan(html);
376:   if (!findings.length) return [];
377:   const rasterRegions = (spec.regions || []).filter((r) => r.medium === 'raster');
378:   const out = [];
379:   for (const f of findings) {
380:     const sel = String(f.selector || '').toLowerCase();
381:     for (const r of rasterRegions) {
382:       const stem = path.basename(r.plate || '', path.extname(r.plate || '')).toLowerCase();
383:       if ((sel && (sel.includes(r.id.toLowerCase()) || (stem && sel.includes(stem)))) || rasterRegions.length === 1) { out.push({ id: r.id, snippet: f.snippet }); break; }
384:     }
385:   }
386:   return out;
387: }
388: /**
389:  * The scaffold: the measured layout as CSS custom properties and one
390:  * reference page. Positions in % of the comp so the frame scales; plates at
391:  * their boxes with object-fit: contain (never cover: cover is how the arch
392:  * lost its left side); text slots sized from the measured cap height (cap /
393:  * 0.70 as the em estimate when font-match gave no size) in the ranked face.
394:  * A reference for a builder that cannot lay out to a box, and a check for
395:  * one that can; the gate reads pixels either way.
396:  */
397: export function writeScaffold(spec, state, { dir = path.join(BUILD_DIR, 'scaffold') } = {}) {
398:   fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
399:   const W = spec.compSize.width, H = spec.compSize.height;
400:   const pct = (v) => `${(v * 100).toFixed(3)}%`;
401:   const vars = [':root {'];
402:   const rules = [];
403:   const bodyParts = [];
404:   const fontLinks = new Set();
405:   for (const r of spec.regions) {
406:     if (r.kind === 'band') continue;
407:     const b = r.box, id = r.id;
408:     vars.push(`  --r-${id}-x: ${pct(b.x)}; --r-${id}-y: ${pct(b.y)}; --r-${id}-w: ${pct(b.w)}; --r-${id}-h: ${pct(b.h)};`);
409:     const type = r.type || {};
410:     const cap = type.comp && type.comp.capHeightPx;
411:     const chosen = type.chosen || null;
412:     const fontPx = chosen && chosen.fontSizePx ? chosen.fontSizePx : (cap ? Math.round(cap / 0.7) : null);
413:     if (cap) vars.push(`  --r-${id}-cap: ${cap}px;${fontPx ? ` --r-${id}-font: ${fontPx}px;` : ''}${chosen ? ` --r-${id}-family: '${chosen.family}'; --r-${id}-weight: ${chosen.weight};` : ''}`);
414:     if (chosen && chosen.family) fontLinks.add(`${chosen.family}:${chosen.weight}`);
415:     rules.push(`.r-${id} { position: absolute; left: var(--r-${id}-x); top: var(--r-${id}-y); width: var(--r-${id}-w); height: var(--r-${id}-h); }`);
416:     const label = (r.note || id).replace(/</g, '&lt;');
417:     if (r.medium === 'raster' && r.kind !== 'texture') {
418:       const src = r.plate ? path.relative(dir, r.plate) : '';
419:       bodyParts.push(`  <figure class="r-${id} region plate" data-region="${id}"><img src="${src}" alt="" style="width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:contain;object-position:${r.kind === 'image' ? 'center' : 'top left'}"></figure>`);
420:     } else if (r.kind === 'texture') {
421:       const src = r.plate ? path.relative(dir, r.plate) : '';

452: export const INVENTED_MIN = 0.04;

454:  * Text, chrome and invented-ink readings for the hero: the comp and the

458: export function heroReadings(state, spec, buildPath) {
459:   if (!spec || !state.comp) return null;
460:   const comp = loadRaster(state.comp).image;
461:   const build = loadRaster(buildPath).image;
462:   let aligned = alignBuild(comp, build, 'top');
463:   const shift = bestShift(comp, aligned);
464:   if (shift.dx || shift.dy) { const shifted = createImage(aligned.width, aligned.height, [255, 255, 255, 255]); blit(shifted, aligned, -shift.dx, -shift.dy); aligned = shifted; }
465:   const text = [], chrome = [], plates = [];
466:   for (const r of spec.regions) {
467:     if (!r.px) continue;
468:     const a = crop(comp, r.px.x, r.px.y, r.px.w, r.px.h), b = crop(aligned, r.px.x, r.px.y, r.px.w, r.px.h);

470:     else if (r.kind === 'chrome' || r.kind === 'control') { const c = chromeStripCheck(r, a, b); chrome.push(...c.findings); }
471:     else if (r.kind === 'plate' || r.kind === 'image') {
472:       const c = plateClipCheck(r, a, b);
473:       if (c.sides.length) plates.push(`plate ${r.id} is clipped at the ${c.sides.join(' and ')}: the comp's artwork keeps a margin there (ink box ${c.comp.w}x${c.comp.h} at ${c.comp.x},${c.comp.y} in the region) and the build's runs to the edge (${c.build.w}x${c.build.h} at ${c.build.x},${c.build.y}); size the box to the artwork's aspect and use object-fit: contain, or place the <img> at the artwork's own size, never cover on a narrower box`);
474:     }
475:   }
476:   const invented = inventedInk(comp, aligned);
477:   return { text, chrome, plates, invented };
478: }
````
