````javascript
684:     worst: worstRegions.map((r) => `${r.id} ${r.verdict} ${(r.score.overall * 100).toFixed(0)}%`),
685:     worstIds: worstRegions.map((r) => r.id),
686:     worstCrops: worstRegions.map((r) => ({ id: r.id, verdict: r.verdict, score: r.score, file: path.join(regionDir, `${r.id}.png`) })),
687:     advisories,
688:     regionVerdicts: Object.fromEntries(report.regions.map((r) => [r.id, r.verdict])),
689:   };
690: }
691: /**
692:  * The hero attempt loop: after two failed advances where the same region is
693:  * still missing/contradicted and the artifact changed only in CSS values,
694:  * refuse a third of the same kind. Missing material is not a layout
695:  * tolerance problem; the fix is a plate, a placed plate, or a rebuilt region.
696:  */
697: export function heroLoopVerdict(state, gate, artifactPath) {
698:   const p = state.phases.hero;
699:   const history = p.history || [];
700:   const entry = { at: now(), score: gate.score ?? null, worstIds: gate.worstIds || [], regionVerdicts: gate.regionVerdicts || {}, artifactHash: hashFile(artifactPath) };
701:   history.push(entry);
702:   p.history = history.slice(-6);
703:   if (history.length < 3) return null;
704:   const last3 = history.slice(-3);
705:   const stuck = last3[0].worstIds[0] && last3.every((h) => h.worstIds[0] === last3[0].worstIds[0]);
706:   const scores = last3.map((h) => h.score ?? 0);
707:   const noProgress = Math.max(...scores) - Math.min(...scores) < 0.03;
708:   if (stuck && noProgress) {
709:     return `region ${last3[0].worstIds[0]} has been the worst region for three attempts and the score moved less than 3 points: value edits are not reaching it. Open ${path.join('.impeccable', 'review', 'diff', 'hero', 'regions', `${last3[0].worstIds[0]}.png`)} and rebuild that region from the comp crop (place its plate, or produce one with generate-image.mjs --plate, or re-derive its structure from the spec box), then recapture.`;
710:   }
711:   return null;
712: }
713: function hashFile(file) {
714:   try {
715:     const crypto = require('node:crypto');
716:     return crypto.createHash('sha1').update(fs.readFileSync(file)).digest('hex').slice(0, 12);
717:   } catch { return null; }
718: }
719: /**
720:  * Responsive gate: the desktop capture (whatever common width the build
721:  * used, 1440 typically) must still read as the comp. A first viewport that
722:  * only holds at the comp's exact width and collapses to one column 96px
723:  * narrower passed every earlier gate in the first simulated round.
724:  */
725: export function gateResponsive(state, { specPath = SPEC_PATH, min = RESPONSIVE_MIN, outDir = path.join('.impeccable', 'review', 'diff', 'desktop') } = {}) {
726:   const desktop = path.join('.impeccable', 'review', 'desktop.png');
727:   const mobile = path.join('.impeccable', 'review', 'mobile.png');
728:   const reasons = [];
729:   if (!fs.existsSync(desktop)) reasons.push(`no ${desktop}: capture the page at a common desktop width (1440 wide, full page) into that path`);
730:   if (!fs.existsSync(mobile)) reasons.push(`no ${mobile}: capture the page at 390 wide, full page, into that path`);
731:   if (reasons.length) return { ok: false, reasons };
732:   const script = path.join(HERE, 'comp-diff.mjs');
733:   const args = [script, '--comp', state.comp, '--build', desktop, '--out-dir', outDir, '--label', 'desktop', '--json'];
734:   if (loadSpec(specPath)) args.push('--spec', specPath);
735:   const res = spawnSync(process.execPath, args, { encoding: 'utf8' });
736:   let report;
737:   try { report = JSON.parse(res.stdout); } catch { return { ok: false, reasons: [`comp-diff failed on ${desktop}: ${res.stderr || res.stdout}`] }; }
738:   // A texture read at 1440 differs from itself at 1536 by resampling alone;
739:   // it passed at the hero and cannot block responsive on its own.
740:   // Likewise a plate or image that passed the plates gate: it read 'missing'
741:   // on detail at 1440 in a run where the hero had just accepted it at 1536,
742:   // structure 94%. Only a region with no energy in its box is missing here.
743:   const missing = report.regions.filter((r) => {
744:     if (r.verdict !== 'missing' || r.kind === 'texture') return false;
745:     const passed = state.plates && state.plates[r.id] && state.plates[r.id].status === 'ok';
746:     if ((r.kind === 'plate' || r.kind === 'image') && passed) {
747:       const present = r.score.detailRaw != null ? r.score.detailRaw >= 0.3 : r.score.detail >= 0.3;
748:       if (present && r.score.structure >= 0.5) return false;
749:     }
750:     return true;
751:   });
752:   // A plate placed and passed at the hero is not re-litigated at 1440: the
753:   // rescale alone drops SSIM on a busy region. Text can still contradict
754:   // (a wrapped headline is a different composition).
755:   const contradictedDirection = report.regions.filter((r) => r.verdict === 'contradicted' && r.kind === 'text');
756:   if (report.overall < min) reasons.push(`the desktop capture (${report.buildSize}; the top ${report.compSize} rows scaled to the comp's width are compared, a full-page capture is fine) scores ${(report.overall * 100).toFixed(0)}% against the comp, under ${(min * 100).toFixed(0)}%: the first viewport does not survive a common desktop width. The hero passed at ${state.breakpoint || 'the comp size'}; the layout must hold from ~1280 up, not only at the comp's exact width (grid columns in fr / minmax, not fixed px that overflow and wrap).`);
757:   for (const r of missing) reasons.push(`at desktop width, region ${r.id} is missing`);
758:   for (const r of contradictedDirection) reasons.push(`at desktop width, region ${r.id} (${r.kind}) is contradicted (structure ${(r.score.structure * 100).toFixed(0)}%)`);
759:   return { ok: reasons.length === 0, reasons, summary: `desktop ${(report.overall * 100).toFixed(0)}% (${report.verdict})`, score: report.overall, sideBySide: report.files ? report.files.sideBySide : null };
760: }
761: const GATES = { comps: gateComps, spec: gateSpec, plates: gatePlates, hero: gateHero, responsive: gateResponsive };
762: // ---- transitions -----------------------------------------------------------
763: export function runGate(state, phase, opts = {}) {
764:   const gate = GATES[phase];
765:   if (!gate) return { ok: true, reasons: [], summary: 'no mechanical gate' };
766:   // A gate that throws is a bug in the gate, never a verdict on the build:
767:   // return it as a refusal that names itself, so the model sees one line
768:   // and the state stays consistent instead of a stack trace and a half-run.
769:   try { return gate(state, opts); }
770:   catch (e) { return { ok: false, reasons: [`gate ${phase} errored (${e.message}); this is a tool bug, not a finding about the page. Re-run with the same inputs; if it repeats, note it and continue with build-phase.mjs advance --force --reason "user: gate ${phase} errored, proceeding" so the run is not lost.`], error: String(e && e.stack || e) }; }
771: }
772: /** Reasons a gate may be forced past. The user downgrading the comp's authority
773:  *  in words is the only one; the parent quotes it. A reason that does not name
774:  *  the user is a model talking itself past its own gate, and it is refused. */
775: export function forceAllowed(reason) {
776:   if (typeof reason !== 'string' || reason.trim().length < 20) return false;
777:   if (/gate \w+ errored/i.test(reason)) return true;
778:   const namesUser = /\buser\b|\bthey (said|asked|told|chose|picked)\b|\bpaul\b/i.test(reason);
779:   // The user must be downgrading the comp itself, not "approving" a
780:   // translation the model proposed. A reason that keeps the comp's
781:   // topology/palette while dropping "pixel-level" is a translation, and
782:   // translation is what the gate measures; it is not a downgrade.
783:   const aboutComp = /\b(comp|mock|mockup|composition|fidelity|plate|region)\b/i.test(reason);
784:   const isTranslationDodge = /truthful|semantic|pixel-level|prioriti[sz]e (facts|semantics|accessibility)/i.test(reason) && !/(drop|skip|remove|without|not needed|don't need|do not need|ignore) (the )?(comp|plate|region|fidelity)/i.test(reason);
785:   // The user's words have to be a downgrade of the comp, said as such: a
786:   // brief line quoted back ("should feel like an extension of her artwork")
787:   // is the direction the comp already serves, not permission to leave it.
788:   // One session forced two gates on that sentence. Ask for a downgrade verb
789:   // in the same reason as the comp noun.
790:   const downgrades = /\b(don't|do not|doesn't|does not|no longer|not) (need|have to|want|care|require|match|follow|hold)|\b(drop|skip|remove|ignore|waive|relax|override|approve|approved|accept|accepted|fine|okay|ok|good enough|ship it|move on|proceed|go ahead|instead of|rather than)\b/i.test(reason);
791:   // and the user's words are quoted or reported, not paraphrased into a
792:   // principle ("the user made the artwork binding" is the model's reading)
793:   const reported = /["'\u201c\u2018].{6,}["'\u201d\u2019]|\b(user|they|paul) (said|says|asked|asks|told|wrote|replied|answered|chose|picked|approved|confirmed)\b/i.test(reason);
794:   const briefQuoteOnly = /\b(should feel|feel like|not a .* page|extension of)\b/i.test(reason) && !/\b(comp|mock|fidelity|gate|plate)\b.*\b(approved|accept|fine|ok|okay|skip|drop|waive|relax|override|move on|proceed)\b/i.test(reason);
795:   return namesUser && aboutComp && downgrades && reported && !isTranslationDodge && !briefQuoteOnly;
796: }
797: export function advance(state, { force = false, reason = null, gateOpts = {} } = {}) {
798:   const phase = state.phase;
799:   const idx = PHASES.indexOf(phase);
800:   if (idx === -1 || phase === 'review') return { ok: false, reasons: [`phase ${phase} cannot advance; use finish`] };
801:   const p = state.phases[phase];
802:   p.attempts += 1;
803:   const gate = runGate(state, phase, gateOpts);
804:   const { plates: _p, ...gateRecord } = gate;
805:   p.gate = { ...gateRecord, at: now() };
806:   // the plates gate's per-plate scores are what the hero gate reads to tell
807:   // a placed plate from a missing one, so they travel on the state
808:   if (phase === 'plates' && Array.isArray(gate.plates)) state.plates = Object.fromEntries(gate.plates.map((pl) => [pl.id, { status: pl.status, score: pl.score, size: pl.size }]));
809:   if (!gate.ok && force && !forceAllowed(reason)) {
810:     p.status = 'open';
811:     return { ok: false, phase, reasons: [...gate.reasons, `--force refused: "${reason || ''}" does not quote the user downgrading the comp. A single-file deliverable, a missing tool, or difficulty is not a reason, and a refused force is not the end of the phase: the readings above are the edits, each one a CSS value; make them, recapture, advance. Ask the user only when a reading contradicts something they said about this comp.`], gate };
812:   }
813:   if (phase === 'hero' && (gate.score != null)) {
814:     const stuck = heroLoopVerdict(state, gate, gateOpts.artifact || state.artifact || 'index.html');
815:     if (stuck && !gate.ok) gate.reasons = [stuck, ...gate.reasons];
816:   }
817:   if (!gate.ok && !force) { p.status = 'open'; return { ok: false, phase, reasons: gate.reasons, gate }; }
818:   if (!gate.ok && force) p.forced = { at: now(), reason, reasons: gate.reasons };
819:   p.status = 'closed'; p.closedAt = now();
820:   if (phase === 'comps' && gate.approved) {
821:     state.comp = gate.approved;
822:     if (!state.breakpoint) { try { const i = loadRaster(gate.approved).image; state.breakpoint = `${i.width}x${i.height}`; } catch { /* non-png comp: breakpoint stays unset */ } }
823:   }
824:   const next = PHASES[idx + 1];
825:   state.phase = next;
826:   state.phases[next].status = 'open'; state.phases[next].openedAt = now();
827:   return { ok: true, phase, next, gate, forced: !!p.forced };
828: }
829: export function nextInstruction(state) {
830:   switch (state.phase) {
831:     case 'comps': return `Comp round for the chosen direction${state.direction ? ` (seed ${state.direction})` : ''}: read reference/visualize.md, generate three compositional comps of the requested surface at its own viewport into ${MOCKS_DIR}/ (each with a prompt sidecar), put them in front of the user, and set "approved": true in the chosen comp's sidecar. Then build-phase.mjs advance. No page code before this closes.`;
832:     case 'spec': return `Measure the comp: node comp-spec.mjs --comp ${state.comp} --grid, open ${path.join(BUILD_DIR, 'comp-grid.png')}, write regions.json (every illustration, photo, texture as its own plate region; every text block its own text region), run comp-spec.mjs --comp ${state.comp} --regions regions.json. Then measure the type: node font-match.mjs --measure <id> for each text region (cap height, width class, weight class) and font-match.mjs --rank <lead text region> --text "<its first words>" to choose the headline face by metrics (the USE line is the CSS; with no browser it records the catalog's nearest face, which is the choice; do not install one, and do not write a chosen face into the spec by hand). Then build-phase.mjs advance.`;
833:     case 'plates': return 'Produce every plate in the spec (comp-spec.mjs --print lists them). Illustrations, photos, figures: node generate-image.mjs --plate <id>, one call per plate. It crops the comp region itself, sends the crop as the edit reference, sizes the plate, keys ink-on-ground to alpha, scores the result against the crop (PLATE-SCORE) and embeds the prompt; nothing else does all of that. Only when it errors (no key, no network) fall back to the harness image tool with comp-spec.mjs --crop <id> as its reference image and comp-spec.mjs --plate-prompt <id> as its prompt, then embed-prompt.mjs; do not post-process a plate with magick or write your own keying. A generation takes 30 to 90 seconds: run it with a long wait (a 90 s yield, or all plates in one command joined with &&) rather than polling an open session turn after turn. A line drawing or figure on flat ground is keyed to alpha automatically (PLATE-CHROMA): place it with a plain <img> over the page\'s own ground, never on a second paper. An opaque plate whose ground differs from the page goes in with mix-blend-mode: multiply. Textures (paper, cloth, grain): do not generate first; crop a clean patch of the comp region (comp-spec.mjs --crop <id> --raw, then cut a patch free of ink), mirror-tile it to the plate size, and save it as the plate; generate only when no clean patch exists. The gate scores a texture against its whole region box, so a texture region should be drawn around clean ground (a sample cell), not around the ink it sits under; the page tiles it wherever the material goes. Then build-phase.mjs advance. Write no page code before this passes.';
834:     case 'hero': return `Run build-phase.mjs scaffold first: it writes the measured layout as CSS custom properties (.impeccable/build/scaffold/layout.css, --r-<id>-x/y/w/h in % of the comp, plus cap height, font-size, family, and weight where measured) and a reference page with every region at its box. Bind those numbers to your own markup (an element per region, its box from the properties); the reference is a check, not the page, and overlapping boxes are overlapping boxes. Build only the first viewport at ${state.breakpoint || 'the comp size'}. Copy the comp's words verbatim in this phase (headline, labels, table cells, footer): the user approved that comp with those words, and rewriting is a later, stated decision, never a silent one here. Set every text region's font-size from its measured cap height and its face from the ranking. Plates first: place every plate at its spec box (comp-spec.mjs --print lists boxes as percentages of the viewport) with object-fit: cover before writing a line of text or a control, capture into ${HERO_REPRO}, and run build-phase.mjs record hero (not advance) once so you see the plate regions read as match before text exists; then lay the semantic layer (text, controls, rules) over the plates from the spec's palette and boxes, capture, advance. When it fails, open the region crops it lists first, in order, then fix; do not build past the hero until it passes.`;
835:     case 'sections': return 'Build the remaining sections inside the spec system (same corner language, rules, and palette; nothing the comp does not show). The hero passed with the comp\'s words verbatim; from here, content beyond the comp is yours to author at full fidelity, and any change to words the comp showed is a stated decision in your report, never silent. Then build-phase.mjs advance.';
836:     case 'motion': return 'Add the signature interaction, reveals, and motion. Then build-phase.mjs advance.';
837:     case 'responsive': return 'Build the other viewports (mobile first if the surface is mobile). The first viewport must hold at common desktop widths (1280 to 1600), not only at the comp\'s exact size: fluid columns, no fixed-px grid that wraps 96px narrower. Settle or disable entrance motion before capturing (an element mid-animation reads as missing). Capture desktop.png (1440 wide, full page) and mobile.png (390 wide, full page) into .impeccable/review/; the gate diffs the top of desktop.png (scaled to the comp\'s width) against the comp. Then build-phase.mjs advance.';
838:     case 'review': return 'Spawn the finish reviewer with the state file, the hero diff report, and the captures; record its disposition with build-phase.mjs finish --disposition <word>.';
839:     default: return '';
840:   }
841: }
842: export function renderStatus(state) {
843:   const lines = [`BUILD-PHASE ${state.phase.toUpperCase()}  comp ${state.comp || '(pending comp round)'}${state.direction ? `  direction ${state.direction}` : ''}${state.breakpoint ? `  breakpoint ${state.breakpoint}` : ''}`];
844:   for (const p of PHASES) {
845:     const s = state.phases[p];
846:     let line = `  ${p.padEnd(11)} ${s.status.padEnd(8)}`;
847:     if (s.gate && s.gate.summary) line += ` ${s.gate.summary}`;
848:     if (s.attempts > 1) line += ` (${s.attempts} attempts)`;
849:     if (s.forced) line += `  FORCED: ${s.forced.reason}`;
850:     lines.push(line);
851:   }
852:   if (state.finish) lines.push(`  finish      ${state.finish.disposition} at ${state.finish.at}`);
853:   lines.push(`NEXT ${nextInstruction(state)}`);
854:   return lines.join('\n');
855: }
856: async function main() {
857:   const cmd = process.argv[2];
858:   if (!cmd || flag('help')) {
859:     console.error('usage: build-phase.mjs start --comp <png> [--breakpoint WxH] | status [--json] | advance [--force --reason "..."] | record hero --build <png> | scaffold | note "<text>" | finish --disposition <word>');
860:     process.exit(1);
861:   }
862:   if (cmd === 'start') {
863:     const comp = arg('comp');
864:     const direction = arg('direction');
865:     if (!comp && !direction) { console.error('build-phase: start needs --comp <approved comp png> (comp already approved) or --direction <seed key> (comp round still to run)'); process.exit(1); }
866:     if (comp && !fs.existsSync(comp)) { console.error(`build-phase: comp ${comp} does not exist`); process.exit(1); }
867:     // The direction choice ping rides on start (see concept-seed.mjs): one
868:     // command records the choice and opens the phases. Never fatal.
869:     if (direction && arg('kind')) {
870:       try {
871:         const { pingChosen } = await import('./concept-seed.mjs');
872:         const sent = await pingChosen({ chosenId: arg('chosen') || undefined, key: direction, scope: 'direction', mode: arg('mode') || undefined, kind: arg('kind'), register: arg('register') || undefined });
873:         console.log(sent ? 'choice recorded' : 'choice ping skipped');
874:       } catch { console.log('choice ping skipped'); }
875:     }
876:     // Clear the roll's pending marker: the build has started.
877:     try { fs.rmSync(path.join(BUILD_DIR, 'pending.json'), { force: true }); } catch { /* absent */ }

879:     const buildPath = readBuildPath();
880:     if (direction && !comp && buildPath === 'code') {
881:       console.log('CODE-LED (from .impeccable config): no comp round and no phase gates. Write the direction contract (reference/new-work.md section 5), build, and finish per section 7. The chosen decision comp, if any, rides to the finish review as the critique reference.');
882:       return;
883:     }
884:     let breakpoint = arg('breakpoint');

886:     const existing = loadState();
887:     if (existing && !flag('reset')) {
888:       console.log(`build-phase: state exists (phase ${existing.phase}); pass --reset to start over`);
889:       console.log(renderStatus(existing));
890:       return;
891:     }
892:     const state = newState({ comp, breakpoint, artifact: arg('artifact'), direction });
893:     saveState(state);
894:     console.log(renderStatus(state));
895:     return;
896:   }
897:   const state = loadState();
898:   if (!state) { console.error(`build-phase: no state at ${STATE_PATH}; run build-phase.mjs start --comp <approved comp>`); process.exit(1); }
899:   if (cmd === 'status') {
900:     if (flag('json')) console.log(JSON.stringify(state, null, 2)); else console.log(renderStatus(state));
901:     return;
902:   }
903:   if (cmd === 'scaffold') {
904:     const spec = loadSpec();
905:     if (!spec) { console.error(`build-phase: no spec at ${SPEC_PATH}; run comp-spec.mjs first`); process.exit(1); }
906:     const out = writeScaffold(spec, state);
907:     console.log(`SCAFFOLD ${out.dir}`);
908:     console.log(`  ${out.css}   one custom property set per region (--r-<id>-x/y/w/h in % of the comp; --r-<id>-cap, --r-<id>-font, --r-<id>-weight where measured); bind these to your own markup`);
909:     console.log(`  ${out.html}  a reference page: every region positioned at its box inside a ${state.breakpoint || spec.compSize.width + 'x' + spec.compSize.height} frame, plates placed with object-fit: contain, text slots at the measured cap height in the ranked face`);
910:     console.log('  The reference is a check, not the page: keep your own semantic structure and bind the numbers to it (an element per region, its box from the properties). Overlapping boxes are overlapping boxes. What the gate reads is pixels; a page that lands each region at its box passes whatever markup it uses.');
911:     return;
912:   }
913:   if (cmd === 'note') {
914:     const text = process.argv.slice(3).filter((a) => !a.startsWith('--')).join(' ');
915:     state.phases[state.phase].notes.push({ at: now(), text });
916:     saveState(state);
917:     console.log(`noted on ${state.phase}`);
918:     return;
919:   }
920:   if (cmd === 'record') {
921:     const which = process.argv[3];
922:     if (which !== 'hero') { console.error('build-phase: record hero --build <png>'); process.exit(1); }
923:     const gate = gateHero(state, { buildPath: arg('build', HERO_REPRO), min: arg('min') ? parseFloat(arg('min')) : HERO_MIN });
924:     // record is a look, not an attempt: the plates-only capture is expected
925:     // to fail on every text region, and counting it muddied the tally.
926:     state.phases.hero.records = (state.phases.hero.records || 0) + 1;
927:     state.phases.hero.gate = { ...gate, at: now() };
928:     saveState(state);
929:     // record is the look, advance is the gate: on the plates-only capture,
930:     // every text region reads missing by design, so say what the plates did.
931:     const plateRows = Object.entries(gate.regionVerdicts || {}).filter(([id]) => { const spec = loadSpec(); const r = spec && spec.regions.find((x) => x.id === id); return r && r.medium === 'raster'; });
932:     if (plateRows.length) console.log(`PLATES ${plateRows.map(([id, v]) => `${id}:${v}`).join(' ')}`);
933:     console.log(`${gate.ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'} ${gate.summary || ''} (record: nothing advanced)`);
934:     for (const r of gate.reasons) console.log(`  - ${r}`);
935:     if (gate.advisories) for (const a of gate.advisories) console.log(`  ${a}`);
936:     if (gate.worst) console.log(`  worst: ${gate.worst.join('; ')}`);
937:     if (gate.sideBySide) console.log(`  open ${gate.sideBySide}`);
938:     process.exit(gate.ok ? 0 : 2);
939:   }
940:   if (cmd === 'advance') {
941:     const gateOpts = {};
942:     if (arg('build')) gateOpts.buildPath = arg('build');
943:     if (arg('min')) gateOpts.min = parseFloat(arg('min'));
944:     if (arg('artifact')) gateOpts.artifact = arg('artifact');
945:     const res = advance(state, { force: flag('force'), reason: arg('reason'), gateOpts });
946:     saveState(state);
947:     if (!res.ok) {
948:       console.log(`GATE ${res.phase ? res.phase.toUpperCase() : ''} FAILED (state unchanged)`);
949:       if (res.gate && res.gate.worstCrops && res.gate.worstCrops.length) {
950:         console.log('  LOOK FIRST, in this order, before editing anything (comp on the left, your build on the right):');
951:         for (const c of res.gate.worstCrops) console.log(`    ${c.file}   ${c.id}: ${c.verdict} ${(c.score.overall * 100).toFixed(0)}% (structure ${(c.score.structure * 100).toFixed(0)}%, color ${(c.score.color * 100).toFixed(0)}%, detail ${(c.score.detail * 100).toFixed(0)}%)`);
952:         console.log('  A region scored missing needs its material (a plate placed, or produced), not a value change; contradicted needs its structure re-derived from the spec box; drift is where padding and size edits belong. When a thin chrome strip (masthead, breadcrumb, table header) is the worst region, check its box height in the spec against the comp first: a strip one grid row tall in the spec but 53px in the comp compares your build against ground it never had.');
953:       }
954:       for (const r of res.reasons) console.log(`  - ${r}`);
955:       if (res.gate && res.gate.advisories && res.gate.advisories.length) for (const a of res.gate.advisories) console.log(`  ${a}`);
956:       if (res.gate && res.gate.sideBySide) console.log(`  then ${res.gate.sideBySide} for the whole viewport`);
957:       process.exit(2);
958:     }
959:     console.log(`ADVANCED ${res.phase} -> ${res.next}${res.forced ? ' (FORCED; recorded)' : ''}${res.gate.summary ? `  ${res.gate.summary}` : ''}`);
960:     if (res.gate && res.gate.advisories && res.gate.advisories.length) for (const a of res.gate.advisories) console.log(`  ${a}`);
961:     console.log(`NEXT ${nextInstruction(state)}`);
962:     return;
963:   }
964:   if (cmd === 'finish') {
965:     const disposition = arg('disposition');
966:     if (!['ship', 'fix', 'rebuild', 'recapture'].includes(disposition)) { console.error('build-phase: finish --disposition ship|fix|rebuild|recapture'); process.exit(1); }
967:     // A ship cannot be recorded over an open phase. The model can still stop
968:     // talking, but it cannot write "ship" into the state with the hero open;
969:     // sessions did exactly that and summarised the build as complete.
970:     const openBefore = PHASES.filter((ph) => ph !== 'review' && state.phases[ph] && state.phases[ph].status !== 'closed' && state.phases[ph].status !== 'skipped');
971:     if (disposition === 'ship' && openBefore.length) {
972:       console.error(`build-phase: finish --disposition ship refused: ${openBefore.join(', ')} ${openBefore.length === 1 ? 'is' : 'are'} not closed (phase ${state.phase}). Record fix or rebuild, or close the phases first; a page shipped over an open hero is a page shipped against its own gate.`);
973:       process.exit(2);
974:     }
975:     state.finish = { disposition, at: now(), phaseAtFinish: state.phase };
976:     if (state.phase === 'review') { state.phases.review.status = 'closed'; state.phases.review.closedAt = now(); }
977:     saveState(state);
978:     console.log(renderStatus(state));
979:     return;
980:   }
981:   console.error(`build-phase: unknown command ${cmd}`);
982:   process.exit(1);
983: }
984: // realpath on both sides: a skill mounted through a symlink (Cursor, a
985: // worktree, an eval stage) must still run as a CLI.
986: const isMain = (() => {
987:   try { return !!process.argv[1] && fs.realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === fs.realpathSync(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); }
988:   catch { return !!process.argv[1] && path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === path.resolve(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname); }
989: })();
990: if (isMain) main();
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/comp-diff.mjs
````javascript
  1: #!/usr/bin/env node
  2: /**
  3:  * comp-diff: measure a build screenshot against its approved comp and produce
  4:  * the evidence a reviewer (human or model) needs to judge fidelity without
  5:  * trusting anyone's memory of the image.
  6:  *
  7:  *   node comp-diff.mjs --comp .impeccable/mocks/approved.png --build .impeccable/review/hero-repro.png
  8:  *   node comp-diff.mjs --comp comp.png --build desktop.png --spec .impeccable/build/spec.json --out-dir .impeccable/review/diff
  9:  *   node comp-diff.mjs ... --json            # machine-readable report on stdout
 10:  *   node comp-diff.mjs ... --threshold 0.75  # exit 3 when the overall score is below
 11:  *
 12:  * Inputs: two PNGs. The build capture may be taller than the comp (a full-page
 13:  * screenshot); it is scaled to the comp's width and the top comp-height rows
 14:  * are compared, because the comp is the first viewport. `--align stretch`
 15:  * squashes the whole build onto the comp instead, for a comp that covers a
 16:  * whole page.
 17:  *
 18:  * Outputs (in --out-dir, default .impeccable/review/diff):
 19:  *   side-by-side.png   comp | build, same size, labeled, with the score
 20:  *   heatmap.png        build with the difference painted over it (red = wrong)
 21:  *   regions/<id>.png   paired crops per region at legible scale, scored
 22:  *   report.json        every number below, plus per-region rows
 23:  *
 24:  * Scores (0..1): structure (blurred SSIM: is the composition the same?),
 25:  * color (histogram + dominant palette: is it the same palette at the same
 26:  * coverage?), detail (high-frequency energy ratio: did the material survive,
 27:  * or did an illustration become a gradient?), bands (do the horizontal
 28:  * sections line up?). `overall` weights them 0.35 / 0.25 / 0.25 / 0.15.
 29:  *
 30:  * Regions come from --spec (comp-spec.mjs output: normalized boxes) or, with
 31:  * none, from the comp's own horizontal bands, so the per-region crops exist
 32:  * either way. Every region row carries the same four scores plus `verdict`:
 33:  * match (>= 0.8), drift (>= 0.6), missing (detail ratio < 0.35 with structure
 34:  * < 0.6), or contradicted (everything else). The words are the finish
 35:  * reviewer's fidelity vocabulary on purpose.
 36:  *
 37:  * Exit codes: 0 measured (and above threshold when one is given), 1 usage or
 38:  * unreadable input, 3 below threshold.
 39:  */
 40: import fs from 'node:fs';
 41: import path from 'node:path';
 42: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
 43: import { decodePng, encodePng, loadRaster } from './lib/png.mjs';
 44: import { crop, resize, fit, blit, createImage, fillRect, strokeRect, drawLabel } from './lib/raster.mjs';
 45: import { structureScore, colorScore, detailScore, diffMap, horizontalBands, bandScore, dominantColors, toGray, blurGray, ssimShifted } from './lib/image-metrics.mjs';
 46: function arg(name, fallback = null) {
 47:   const i = process.argv.indexOf(`--${name}`);
 48:   if (i === -1) return fallback;
 49:   const v = process.argv[i + 1];
 50:   return v && !v.startsWith('--') ? v : fallback;
 51: }
 52: const flag = (name) => process.argv.includes(`--${name}`);
 53: export function readPng(file) {
 54:   return loadRaster(file).image;
 55: }
 56: /**
 57:  * Scale the build to the comp's width; take the top comp-height rows
 58:  * (align=top), squash the whole build onto the comp (align=stretch), or scale
 59:  * to cover and center-crop (align=cover, the way `object-fit: cover` will show
 60:  * a plate whose aspect differs from its region).
 61:  */
 62: export function alignBuild(comp, build, align = 'top') {
 63:   if (align === 'stretch') return resize(build, comp.width, comp.height);
 64:   if (align === 'cover') {
 65:     const s = Math.max(comp.width / build.width, comp.height / build.height);
 66:     const scaled = resize(build, build.width * s, build.height * s);
 67:     return crop(scaled, (scaled.width - comp.width) / 2, (scaled.height - comp.height) / 2, comp.width, comp.height);
 68:   }
 69:   const scaled = build.width === comp.width ? build : resize(build, comp.width, Math.round((build.height / build.width) * comp.width));
 70:   if (scaled.height === comp.height) return scaled;
 71:   if (scaled.height > comp.height) return crop(scaled, 0, 0, comp.width, comp.height);
 72:   // shorter than the comp: pad with white so a short page reads as missing content, not as a resize
 73:   const out = createImage(comp.width, comp.height, [255, 255, 255, 255]);
 74:   blit(out, scaled, 0, 0);
 75:   return out;
 76: }
 77: /** Weights per region kind: what a region is made of decides what losing it looks like. */
 78: const WEIGHTS = {
 79:   default: { structure: 0.35, color: 0.25, detail: 0.25, bands: 0.15 },
 80:   plate: { structure: 0.25, color: 0.2, detail: 0.5, bands: 0.05 },
 81:   image: { structure: 0.25, color: 0.2, detail: 0.5, bands: 0.05 },
 82:   texture: { structure: 0.15, color: 0.35, detail: 0.5, bands: 0 },
 83:   text: { structure: 0.5, color: 0.25, detail: 0.15, bands: 0.1 },
 84:   control: { structure: 0.45, color: 0.35, detail: 0.2, bands: 0 },
 85: };
 86: export function scorePair(a, b, kind = null) {
 87:   const structure = structureScore(a, b);
 88:   const color = colorScore(a, b);
 89:   const detail = detailScore(a, b);
 90:   const bandsA = horizontalBands(a), bandsB = horizontalBands(b);
 91:   const bands = bandScore(bandsA, bandsB);
 92:   const w = WEIGHTS[kind] || WEIGHTS.default;
 93:   const overall = w.structure * structure + w.color * color.score + w.detail * detail.score + w.bands * bands;
 94:   return {
 95:     overall: r4(overall),
 96:     structure: r4(structure),
 97:     color: r4(color.score),
 98:     colorIntersection: r4(color.intersection),
 99:     paletteMatch: r4(color.paletteMatch),
100:     detail: r4(detail.score),
101:     detailRaw: r4(detail.rawScore ?? detail.score),
102:     detailAdded: r4(detail.addedFraction),
103:     bands: r4(bands),
104:     _detail: detail,
105:     _bands: { comp: bandsA, build: bandsB },
106:   };
107: }
108: /** Kinds that carry the direction: a wrong one is the wrong page, whatever the mean says. */
109: export const DIRECTION_KINDS = new Set(['plate', 'image', 'text']);
110: /** Best small global translation (build relative to comp), in pixels, by blurred-gray SSIM. */
111: export function bestShift(comp, build, workWidth = 256) {
112:   const h = Math.max(8, Math.round((comp.height / comp.width) * workWidth));
113:   const a = blurGray(toGray(resize(comp, workWidth, h)), 2);
114:   const b = blurGray(toGray(resize(build, workWidth, h)), 2);
115:   const maxShift = Math.max(2, Math.round(workWidth * 0.04));
116:   let best = { dx: 0, dy: 0, score: ssimShifted(a, b, 0, 0) };
117:   for (const dy of [-maxShift, -maxShift / 2, 0, maxShift / 2, maxShift]) {
118:     for (const dx of [-maxShift, -maxShift / 2, 0, maxShift / 2, maxShift]) {
119:       const sc = ssimShifted(a, b, Math.round(dx), Math.round(dy));
120:       if (sc > best.score + 0.01) best = { dx: Math.round(dx), dy: Math.round(dy), score: sc };
121:     }
122:   }
123:   const scale = comp.width / workWidth;
124:   return { dx: Math.round(best.dx * scale), dy: Math.round(best.dy * scale), score: best.score };
125: }
126: export function verdictFor(s, kind = null) {
127:   const painted = kind === 'plate' || kind === 'image' || kind === 'texture';
128:   // Nothing drawn where the comp drew something is missing whatever the
129:   // palette says: a footer strip the build pushed below the fold read as
130:   // 'drift' on ground colour alone (detail 4%, structure 92%). detailRaw is
131:   // 1 when the comp region itself is calm, so a low value already means the
132:   // comp had material there.
133:   if (s.detailRaw != null && s.detailRaw < 0.15) return 'missing';
134:   if (painted && s.detail < 0.5) return 'missing';
135:   // For text, chrome, and controls "missing" means the build has nothing
136:   // there, not that a thin strip sits a few pixels off: require the build's
137:   // own energy to be near zero relative to the comp (rawScore, before the
138:   // added-detail penalty), and drift for a mere misalignment.
139:   if (!painted && s.detail < 0.35 && s.structure < 0.6) {
140:     if (s.detailRaw != null && s.detailRaw < 0.2) return 'missing';
141:     // low detail with structure and palette both holding is grain the build
142:     // renders flatter (a spine of rotated type on textured red), not a
143:     // different composition
144:     if (s.structure >= 0.5 && s.color >= 0.5) return 'drift';
145:     return 'contradicted';
146:   }
147:   if (s.detail < 0.35 && s.structure < 0.6) return 'missing';
148:   // Structure is the one thing a wrong-but-busy region cannot fake: noise,
149:   // a mirrored crop, a swapped column, a tile shuffle all keep color and
150:   // energy and lose structure. Below the floor it is contradicted whatever
151:   // the weighted mean says; painted regions with invented detail likewise.
152:   if (s.structure < 0.3) return 'contradicted';
153:   if (painted && (s.structure < 0.45 || s.detailAdded > 0.4)) return 'contradicted';
154:   // Text is set in a substitute face at a slightly different metric almost
155:   // always, and blurred SSIM reads glyph shape; a text region with its
156:   // structure above the swap floor and its palette intact is drift at worst.
157:   // Chasing it past that point is what burned eight to thirteen hero attempts
158:   // per build in the first simulated round.
159:   if (kind === 'text' && s.color >= 0.5) return s.overall >= 0.8 ? 'match' : 'drift';
160:   // Chrome and controls are thin strips whose "detail" is mostly ground grain
161:   // (a paper texture the build renders flatter, a scanline). When their
162:   // structure and palette hold, low detail is drift, not contradiction.
163:   if ((kind === 'chrome' || kind === 'control') && s.structure >= 0.5 && s.color >= 0.5) return s.overall >= 0.8 ? 'match' : 'drift';
164:   if (s.overall >= 0.8) return 'match';
165:   if (s.overall >= 0.6) return 'drift';
166:   return 'contradicted';
167: }
168: const r4 = (v) => Math.round(v * 10000) / 10000;
169: /** Regions from a spec (normalized boxes) or derived from the comp's bands. */
170: export function resolveRegions(comp, spec) {
171:   const regions = [];
172:   if (spec && Array.isArray(spec.regions) && spec.regions.length) {
173:     for (const r of spec.regions) {
174:       const box = r.box || r;
175:       if ([box.x, box.y, box.w, box.h].some((v) => typeof v !== 'number')) continue;
176:       regions.push({ id: r.id || `region-${regions.length + 1}`, x: box.x, y: box.y, w: box.w, h: box.h, kind: r.kind || null });
177:     }
178:     if (regions.length) return regions;
179:   }
180:   const bands = horizontalBands(comp).filter((b) => b.strength > 0.2);
181:   const cuts = [0, ...bands.map((b) => b.y), 1].filter((v, i, arr) => i === 0 || v - arr[i - 1] > 0.06);
182:   if (cuts[cuts.length - 1] !== 1) cuts.push(1);
183:   for (let i = 0; i + 1 < cuts.length; i++) {
184:     regions.push({ id: `band-${i + 1}`, x: 0, y: cuts[i], w: 1, h: cuts[i + 1] - cuts[i], kind: 'band' });
185:   }
186:   if (regions.length < 2) {
187:     return [
188:       { id: 'top', x: 0, y: 0, w: 1, h: 0.5, kind: 'band' },
189:       { id: 'bottom', x: 0, y: 0.5, w: 1, h: 0.5, kind: 'band' },
190:     ];
191:   }
192:   return regions;
193: }
194: /** Crop a normalized region; regions thinner than 48px in either axis are grown to that so tiny strips do not swing on subpixel noise. */
195: /** Bounding box of ink (pixels darker/lighter than the region's ground by a margin) within a crop, in px. */
196: export function inkBox(img) {
197:   const g = toGray(img);
198:   // ground = median gray; ink = |v - ground| > 48
199:   const sample = []; for (let i = 0; i < g.data.length; i += Math.max(1, Math.floor(g.data.length / 4000))) sample.push(g.data[i]);
200:   sample.sort((p, q) => p - q); const ground = sample[Math.floor(sample.length / 2)] || 255;
201:   let x0 = img.width, y0 = img.height, x1 = -1, y1 = -1;
202:   for (let y = 0; y < img.height; y++) for (let x = 0; x < img.width; x++) {
203:     if (Math.abs(g.data[y * img.width + x] - ground) > 48) { if (x < x0) x0 = x; if (x > x1) x1 = x; if (y < y0) y0 = y; if (y > y1) y1 = y; }
204:   }
205:   if (x1 < 0) return null;
206:   return { x: x0, y: y0, w: x1 - x0 + 1, h: y1 - y0 + 1 };
207: }
208: function regionCrop(img, r) {
209:   const minPx = 48;
210:   let x = r.x * img.width, y = r.y * img.height, w = r.w * img.width, h = r.h * img.height;
211:   if (h < minPx) { y -= (minPx - h) / 2; h = minPx; }
212:   if (w < minPx) { x -= (minPx - w) / 2; w = minPx; }
213:   return crop(img, x, y, w, h);
214: }
215: const HEAT_LABEL = { match: [40, 160, 80, 255], drift: [220, 160, 30, 255], missing: [200, 40, 40, 255], contradicted: [200, 40, 40, 255] };
216: export function renderSideBySide(comp, build, label, score) {
217:   const gap = 24, pad = 48;
218:   const targetW = Math.min(comp.width, 1400);
219:   const a = fit(comp, targetW, 100000), b = resize(build, a.width, a.height);

316: function summarize(report) {

334: async function main() {

353:   if (files) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'report.json'), JSON.stringify(report, null, 2));
354:   if (flag('json')) console.log(JSON.stringify(report, null, 2));
355:   else console.log(summarize(report));

358:     if (!flag('json')) console.log(`BELOW THRESHOLD ${(threshold * 100).toFixed(0)}%: the reproduction is not done. Fix the worst regions and re-run; do not build past the hero.`);
359:     process.exit(3);

361: }
362: // realpath on both sides: a skill mounted through a symlink (Cursor, a

364: const isMain = (() => {

366:   catch { return !!process.argv[1] && path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === path.resolve(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname); }
367: })();
368: if (isMain) main();
````

````javascript
 14:  * This script rolls them from outside, the same trick that made the
 15:  * palette seed work:
 16:  *   - ASSIGNED INDEX: which entry of the model's own resonance-ordered
 17:  *     shortlist gets built. The assignment is the dice: it never chooses an
 18:  *     ungrounded ingredient, it only refuses the argmax rut. Attended runs
 19:  *     present the assigned direction and offer re-roll instead of a ranked
 20:  *     lineup, because a lineup hands selection back to a taste function
 21:  *     (model or user) and taste functions pick the safest card.
 22:  *   - CHALLENGERS (6): outside forms from concept-ingredients.json, two from
 23:  *     each challenger tier (graphic system, instrument language, atmosphere
 24:  *     world), fused with the product first (challenger supplies form and
 25:  *     system grammar, product supplies every fact, clarity wins conflicts),
 26:  *     then weighed against the derived candidates on audience identification
 27:  *     and product clarity. They win only when they beat the grounded list;
 28:  *     measured behavior is that they lose to strong cultural material and
 29:  *     win over thin categories, which is the intended shape.
 30:  *   - RE-ROLL (--reroll <n>): round n of the same base key. The script
 31:  *     recomputes what rounds 0..n-1 drew, excludes all of it, and rolls a
 32:  *     fresh assigned index, challengers, and compositions. One base key therefore
 33:  *     reproduces the entire chain of rounds.
 34:  *   - REGISTER (--register safer|bolder): the user's steering on the
 35:  *     familiar-to-bold axis, applied to a re-roll round. A register changes
 36:  *     only what this round instructs, never what it dealt: the same key and
 37:  *     reroll count reproduce the same deal whatever the register, so the
 38:  *     exclusion chain never forks. bolder presents the dealt foreign forms
 39:  *     as the whole hand (first-dealt leads, dice-assigned by deal order);
 40:  *     safer spends the dealt hand unseen and presents the familiar register,
 41:  *     the model's conventional grounded candidates plus the canon against
 42:  *     named competitors, the one sanctioned lineup of the model's own list.
 43:  *     Registers are user-requested, never pre-selected by the model.
 44:  *   - RATINGS: the reviewer's approval ratings weight the challenger draw
 45:  *     (3-star doubles the odds, 1-star sits out); the approved pool itself
 46:  *     is unchanged.
 47:  *
 48:  * Usage:
 49:  *   node scripts/concept-seed.mjs --scope direction --mode persuade
 50:  *   node scripts/concept-seed.mjs --scope surface --mode operate --from <key>
 51:  *   node scripts/concept-seed.mjs --scope surface --mode operate --grain flow
 52:  *   node scripts/concept-seed.mjs --scope direction --candidate-count 6
 53:  *   node scripts/concept-seed.mjs --scope direction --mode persuade --from <key> --reroll 1
 54:  *   node scripts/concept-seed.mjs --scope direction --mode persuade --from <key> --reroll 1 --register bolder
 55:  *   node scripts/concept-seed.mjs --chosen <challenger-id> --kind challenger --from <key> --scope direction
 56:  *   node scripts/concept-seed.mjs --kind assigned --from <key> --scope direction
 57:  *
 58:  * --grain names how much of the product is in play: product, flow, view, or
 59:  * region. A docs site, an onboarding flow, a landing page and a data table are
 60:  * four different amounts of product and want different compositions. Grain is a
 61:  * preference: it deals matching compositions first and tops up from the rest of
 62:  * the register, and the rendered seed says how many actually matched so a
 63:  * borrowed structure is never mistaken for a supplied one.
 64:  *
 65:  * --platform names the delivery target (web, ios, android). Unlike grain this is
 66:  * a hard filter: a composition that needs hover or a pointer does not degrade on
 67:  * a phone, it stops working. --mode also gates which worlds are eligible, for
 68:  * worlds whose reviewer marked them as carrying only some modes.
 69:  *
 70:  * --mode names the requested surface's mode (persuade, operate, read,
 71:  * experience) so the appended compositions match its register of work; omitted,
 72:  * they roll from the full approved pool.
 73:  *
 74:  * Challenger data resolves in order: a local catalog directory (the private
 75:  * service repo, evals, and tests set IMPECCABLE_CATALOG_DIR), then the roll
 76:  * API at impeccable.style, then a degraded assignment-only seed when both are
 77:  * unavailable. The anonymous choice ping fires once per resolved attended
 78:  * round on API-dealt rolls: --kind names which card class won (assigned,
 79:  * pick, challenger, canon) so share metrics have a denominator, --chosen
 80:  * carries the catalog id when a dealt challenger won, and --register rides
 81:  * along when the round came from a steered hand. Grounded candidates' names
 82:  * never leave the machine. DO_NOT_TRACK or IMPECCABLE_NO_TELEMETRY disables
 83:  * the ping entirely.
 84:  *
 85:  * Env vars:
 86:  *   IMPECCABLE_CONCEPT_SEED — same as --from; for reproducible eval runs.
 87:  *   IMPECCABLE_CATALOG_DIR  — directory holding the four catalog JSON files.
 88:  *   IMPECCABLE_API_URL      — roll API base (default https://impeccable.style/api).
 89:  *   IMPECCABLE_NO_TELEMETRY — disables the choice ping (DO_NOT_TRACK also honored).
 90:  */
 91: import crypto from 'node:crypto';
 92: import { dirname, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path';
 93: import { readFileSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs';

 96:   approvedPoolRevision,
 97:   readConceptCatalog,

 99:   WELL_TIERS,
100: } from './lib/concept-catalog.mjs';
101: import { readCompositionCatalog } from './lib/composition-catalog.mjs';
102: import {
103:   COMPOSITION_GRAINS,
104:   COMPOSITION_PLATFORMS,
105:   runSyncSelection,
106:   selectApprovedChallengers as selectApprovedChallengersCore,
107:   selectApprovedCompositions as selectApprovedCompositionsCore,
108: } from './lib/roll-selection.mjs';
109: const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
110: // Data resolution order: a local catalog (the private service repo, evals, and
111: // tests point IMPECCABLE_CATALOG_DIR at one), then the roll API, then a
112: // degraded assignment-only seed. The full catalog does not ship with the skill.
113: const CATALOG_DIR = process.env.IMPECCABLE_CATALOG_DIR || here;
114: const API_BASE = (process.env.IMPECCABLE_API_URL || 'https://impeccable.style/api').replace(/\/$/, '');
115: const API_TIMEOUT_MS = Number(process.env.IMPECCABLE_API_TIMEOUT || 4000);
116: // All API calls in one seed run share a single deadline so an unreachable
117: // network degrades after one timeout total, never one timeout per call.
118: let apiDeadline = null;
119: function apiBudgetMs() {
120:   if (apiDeadline === null) apiDeadline = Date.now() + API_TIMEOUT_MS;
121:   return Math.max(0, apiDeadline - Date.now());
122: }
123: const localStates = new Map();
124: function loadLocal(catalogDir = CATALOG_DIR) {
125:   if (localStates.has(catalogDir)) return localStates.get(catalogDir);
126:   let localState;
127:   try {
128:     const catalogState = readConceptCatalog(
129:       join(catalogDir, 'concept-ingredients.json'),
130:       join(catalogDir, 'concept-reviews.json')
131:     );
132:     const validation = validateConceptCatalog(catalogState.catalog, catalogState.reviewData);
133:     if (validation.errors.length > 0) {
134:       throw new Error(`invalid catalog: ${validation.errors.join('; ')}`);
135:     }
136:     const compositionState = readCompositionCatalog(
137:       join(catalogDir, 'composition-ingredients.json'),
138:       join(catalogDir, 'composition-reviews.json')
139:     );
140:     localState = {
141:       concepts: catalogState.concepts,
142:       compositions: compositionState.compositions,
143:     };
144:   } catch {
145:     localState = null;
146:   }
147:   localStates.set(catalogDir, localState);
148:   return localState;
149: }
150: function requireLocalConcepts() {
151:   const local = loadLocal();
152:   if (!local) {
153:     throw new Error('concept-seed: no local catalog (set IMPECCABLE_CATALOG_DIR or pass sourceConcepts)');
154:   }
155:   return local;
156: }
157: async function fetchRoll({ scope, key, mode, grain, platform, reroll }) {
158:   const params = new URLSearchParams({ scope, key, reroll: String(reroll) });
159:   if (mode) params.set('mode', mode);
160:   if (grain) params.set('grain', grain);
161:   if (platform) params.set('platform', platform);
162:   const controller = new AbortController();
163:   const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), apiBudgetMs());
164:   try {
165:     // Race the budget explicitly: abort signals do not reliably cancel the
166:     // TCP connect phase, so a blackholed route would otherwise stall ~10s.
167:     const response = await Promise.race([
168:       fetch(`${API_BASE}/roll?${params}`, { signal: controller.signal }),
169:       new Promise(resolveTimeout => setTimeout(() => resolveTimeout(null), apiBudgetMs())),
170:     ]);
171:     if (!response) return null;
172:     if (!response.ok) return null;
173:     const roll = await response.json();
174:     if (!Array.isArray(roll.challengers) || roll.challengers.length === 0) return null;
175:     return roll;
176:   } catch {
177:     return null;
178:   } finally {
179:     clearTimeout(timer);
180:   }
181: }
182: function telemetryDisabled() {
183:   return Boolean(process.env.IMPECCABLE_NO_TELEMETRY || process.env.DO_NOT_TRACK);
184: }
185: // Anonymous choice ping: one per resolved attended direction round. kind
186: // says which card class won (assigned / pick / challenger / canon), so
187: // pick-share and canon-share have a denominator; chosenId rides along only
188: // when a dealt catalog world won, and register only when the round came from
189: // a steered hand. Grounded candidates' names never leave the machine: they
190: // are derived from the user's project, so the ping carries the kind alone.
191: // Fire-and-forget; never fails the caller.
192: const PING_KINDS = new Set(['assigned', 'pick', 'challenger', 'canon']);
193: export async function pingChosen({ chosenId, key, scope, mode, kind, register }) {
194:   if (telemetryDisabled()) return false;
195:   if (kind && !PING_KINDS.has(kind)) return false;
196:   if (register && register !== 'safer' && register !== 'bolder') return false;
197:   // Legacy shape: a bare challenger id with no kind stays a valid ping.
198:   if (!chosenId && !kind) return false;
199:   if ((kind === 'challenger' || !kind) && !chosenId) return false;
200:   const controller = new AbortController();
201:   const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), apiBudgetMs());
202:   try {
203:     await fetch(`${API_BASE}/chosen`, {
204:       method: 'POST',
205:       headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
206:       body: JSON.stringify({
207:         ...(chosenId ? { chosenId } : {}),
208:         key,
209:         scope,
210:         mode,
211:         ...(kind ? { kind } : {}),
212:         ...(register ? { register } : {}),
213:       }),
214:       signal: controller.signal,
215:     });
216:     return true;
217:   } catch {
218:     return false;
219:   } finally {
220:     clearTimeout(timer);
221:   }
222: }
223: const CARD_BASE = process.env.IMPECCABLE_CARD_BASE || 'https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards';
224: export function renderChallenger(concept, index) {
225:   const system = concept.system.map(rule => `       - ${rule}`).join('\n');
226:   const board = concept.cardBoard || `${CARD_BASE}/${concept.id}.webp`;
227:   const hero = concept.cardHero || `${CARD_BASE}/${concept.id}-hero.webp`;
228:   return `  ${index + 1}. ${concept.form}
229:      SOURCE ID: ${concept.id}
230:      CREATIVE SPARK: ${concept.spark}
231:      SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
232: ${system}
233:      WEB LEVERAGE: ${concept.webLeverage}
234:      QUALITY BAR: board ${board} · hero ${hero}`;
235: }
236: export function renderComposition(composition, index = null) {
237:   const grammar = composition.grammar.map(rule => `       - ${rule}`).join('\n');
238:   return `  ${index == null ? '' : `${index + 1}. `}${composition.form}
239:      SOURCE ID: ${composition.id}
240:      SPARK: ${composition.spark}
241:      COMPOSITION GRAMMAR:
242: ${grammar}
243:      WEB LEVERAGE: ${composition.webLeverage}`;
244: }
245: // Selection itself lives in lib/roll-selection.mjs so this script and the roll
246: // API run one algorithm rather than two that drifted. These wrappers add only
247: // what is local to the skill: resolving the catalog when no pool is passed, and
248: // driving the generator with Node's synchronous hash, which keeps a local render
249: // synchronous for prepared eval sessions and tests.
250: function driveSelection(generator) {
251:   return runSyncSelection(generator, input => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(input).digest('hex'));
252: }
253: export function dealCompositions({ scope, key, reroll = 0, mode = null, grain = null, platform = null, sourceCompositions = null, count = 3 }) {
254:   const compositions = sourceCompositions ?? requireLocalConcepts().compositions;
255:   return driveSelection(selectApprovedCompositionsCore({ scope, key, reroll, mode, grain, platform, compositions, count }));
256: }
257: // Array-returning form, which is what every caller wanted before the match

259: export function selectApprovedCompositions(options) {
260:   return dealCompositions(options).picks;
261: }
262: // Compatibility for callers that need a single smoke-test sample.
263: export function selectApprovedComposition(options) {
264:   return selectApprovedCompositions({ ...options, count: 1 })[0] ?? null;
265: }
266: export function selectApprovedChallengers({ scope, key, reroll = 0, mode = null, sourceConcepts = null }) {
267:   const source = sourceConcepts ?? requireLocalConcepts().concepts;
268:   const { approved, picks } = driveSelection(selectApprovedChallengersCore({ scope, key, reroll, mode, concepts: source }));
269:   return {
270:     approved,
271:     picks,
272:     poolRevision: approvedPoolRevision(source),

275: }
276: const SEED_MODES = new Set(['persuade', 'operate', 'read', 'experience']);

278:   scope = 'surface',
279:   key = process.env.IMPECCABLE_CONCEPT_SEED || crypto.randomBytes(4).toString('hex'),
280:   reroll = 0,
281:   register = null,
282:   mode = null,
283:   grain = null,

285:   candidateCount = 7,

307:   // Grain needs no mode: how much of the product is in play is independent of

312:   if (platform !== null && !COMPOSITION_PLATFORMS.includes(platform)) {

391:   const promotedInstruction = scope === 'direction'
392:     ? `After ordering the grounded directions by resonance, build candidate
````

````javascript
244:     // closing one target cannot hide another target's live backlog. Once a
245:     // slug has any identity-aware snapshot, its older legacy records are no
246:     // longer independently routable and must not resurface as zombie work.
247:     const targetIdentity = snapshotTargetIdentity(snapshot);
248:     if (!targetIdentity && identifiedSlugs.has(snapshot.meta.slug)) continue;
249:     const streamKey = targetIdentity || `slug:${snapshot.meta.slug}`;
250:     latestByTarget.set(streamKey, snapshot);
251:   }
252:   return [...latestByTarget.values()]
253:     .filter((snapshot) => snapshot.meta.closed !== true)
254:     .sort((a, b) => a.path.localeCompare(b.path))
255:     .at(-1) || null;
256: }
257: /**
258:  * Return the last `limit` snapshots' frontmatter, oldest → newest.
259:  * Critique appends a one-line trend to its output using this.
260:  */
261: export function readTrend(slug, { limit = 5, cwd = process.cwd() } = {}) {
262:   const all = listSnapshots(`__${slug}.md`, cwd);
263:   const slice = all.slice(-limit);
264:   return slice.map((file) => parseFrontmatter(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf-8')));
265: }
266: // ---- CLI ---------------------------------------------------------------
267: // Accept either a ready slug or a concrete target (path/URL) everywhere, so
268: // callers never have to run the slug step separately. Anything containing a
269: // path or URL marker is resolved through slugFromTarget.
270: function isReadySlug(value) {
271:   return /^[a-z0-9-]+$/.test(value || '') && !value.includes('/');
272: }
273: function coerceSlug(value) {
274:   if (!value) return null;
275:   if (isReadySlug(value)) return value;
276:   return slugFromTarget(value);
277: }
278: function main(argv) {
279:   const [cmd, ...args] = argv;
280:   switch (cmd) {
281:     case 'slug': {
282:       const slug = slugFromTarget(args[0]);
283:       if (!slug) { process.stderr.write('no stable slug for input\n'); process.exit(1); }
284:       process.stdout.write(`${slug}\n`);
285:       return;
286:     }
287:     case 'write': {
288:       const [slugArg, bodyFile] = args;
289:       const slug = coerceSlug(slugArg);
290:       if (!slug || !bodyFile) { process.stderr.write('usage: write <slug-or-target> <body-file>\n'); process.exit(1); }
291:       const raw = fs.readFileSync(bodyFile, 'utf-8');
292:       // The body file may be a full report. The caller passes the meta as

301:       // This makes the snapshot describe the exact file bytes critique saw.
302:       delete meta.target_fingerprint;
303:       delete meta.target_path;
304:       delete meta.target_identity;
305:       const targetIdentity = resolveTargetIdentity(slugArg);
306:       if (targetIdentity) meta.target_identity = targetIdentity;
307:       const targetFingerprint = fingerprintTarget(slugArg);
308:       if (targetFingerprint) {
309:         meta.target_fingerprint = targetFingerprint;
310:         meta.target_path = resolveLocalTargetPath(slugArg);
311:       }
312:       const out = writeSnapshot({ slug, meta, body: raw });
313:       process.stdout.write(`${out}\n`);
314:       return;
315:     }
316:     case 'latest': {
317:       const target = args[0];
318:       const format = args[1];
319:       const slug = coerceSlug(target);
320:       if (!slug || (format && format !== '--json')) {
321:         process.stderr.write('usage: latest <slug-or-target> [--json]\n');
322:         process.exit(1);
323:       }
324:       const targetFingerprint = fingerprintTarget(target);
325:       const targetPath = resolveLocalTargetPath(target);
326:       const targetIdentity = resolveTargetIdentity(target);
327:       const readySlug = isReadySlug(target);
328:       const newestForSlug = readNewestSnapshot(slug);
329:       if (!newestForSlug) { process.exit(2); }
330:       // Concrete targets select the newest snapshot for their exact identity,
331:       // not merely the newest filename for a lossy slug. This keeps distinct
332:       // targets such as foo/bar and foo-bar from hiding each other's backlog.
333:       const exactSnapshot = readNewestSnapshotForIdentity(slug, targetIdentity);
334:       let latest = exactSnapshot;
335:       if (!latest && !readySlug) {
336:         // Legacy snapshots have no identity. Preserve their old explicit
337:         // path/URL behavior only when no known target identity was selected.
338:         latest = readNewestSnapshotForIdentity(slug, null);
339:       }
340:       if (!latest) latest = newestForSlug;
341:       if (latest.meta.closed === true) { process.exit(2); }
342:       const recordedTargetPath = latest.meta.target_path;
343:       const recordedTargetIdentity = snapshotTargetIdentity(latest);
344:       const matchingIdentity = recordedTargetIdentity === targetIdentity;
345:       // Bare slugs remain a supported lookup mode, including for URL
346:       // snapshots. But when a same-named local file exists, the request is
347:       // ambiguous unless that exact file owns the snapshot identity.
348:       if (readySlug && !recordedTargetIdentity) {
349:         process.stderr.write(
350:           'ambiguous legacy snapshot target; use an explicit ./path or full URL\n',
351:         );
352:         process.exit(2);
353:       }
354:       if (readySlug && targetPath && fs.existsSync(targetPath) && !matchingIdentity) {
355:         process.stderr.write(
356:           'ambiguous snapshot slug; use an explicit ./path or remove the local name collision\n',
357:         );
358:         process.exit(2);
359:       }
360:       const concreteTarget = !readySlug || matchingIdentity;
361:       if (concreteTarget && recordedTargetIdentity && !matchingIdentity) {
362:         process.exit(2);
363:       }
364:       const concreteLocalTarget = concreteTarget && targetPath;
365:       if (concreteLocalTarget && latest.meta.target_fingerprint !== targetFingerprint) {
366:         closeSnapshot(latest.path);
367:         process.exit(2);
368:       }
369:       if (format === '--json') {
370:         process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({
371:           snapshot_file: path.basename(latest.path),
372:           body: latest.body,
373:         }, null, 2) + '\n');
374:       } else {
375:         process.stdout.write(latest.body);
376:       }
377:       return;
378:     }
379:     case 'close': {
380:       const [slugArg, snapshotFile, ...extra] = args;
381:       const slug = coerceSlug(slugArg);
382:       if (!slug || !snapshotFile || extra.length > 0) {
383:         process.stderr.write('usage: close <resolved-target> <snapshot-file>\n');
384:         process.exit(1);
385:       }
386:       if (
387:         path.basename(snapshotFile) !== snapshotFile
388:         || !SNAPSHOT_FILENAME.test(snapshotFile)
389:         || !snapshotFile.endsWith(`__${slug}.md`)
390:       ) process.exit(2);
391:       // A slug and filename are not enough to prove ownership because two
392:       // distinct targets can normalize to the same slug. Modern snapshots
393:       // carry a canonical identity, so require the supplied resolved target
394:       // to match it before allowing the exact snapshot to be closed. Legacy
395:       // snapshots without identity retain their historical close behavior.
396:       const snapshotPath = path.join(getCritiqueDir(process.cwd()), snapshotFile);
397:       let snapshot;
398:       try {
399:         if (!fs.lstatSync(snapshotPath).isFile()) process.exit(2);
400:         snapshot = readSnapshot(snapshotPath);
401:       } catch {
402:         process.exit(2);
403:       }
404:       const recordedTargetIdentity = snapshotTargetIdentity(snapshot);
405:       if (
406:         recordedTargetIdentity
407:         && recordedTargetIdentity !== resolveTargetIdentity(slugArg)
408:       ) process.exit(2);
409:       const closed = closeSnapshot(snapshotFile);
410:       if (!closed) { process.exit(2); }
411:       process.stdout.write(`${closed}\n`);
412:       return;
413:     }
414:     case 'trend': {
415:       const rows = readTrend(coerceSlug(args[0]), { limit: args[1] ? Number(args[1]) : 5 });
416:       process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(rows, null, 2) + '\n');
417:       return;
418:     }
419:     default:
420:       process.stderr.write('usage: critique-storage.mjs <slug|write|latest|trend|close> [args]\n');
421:       process.exit(1);
422:   }
423: }
424: function isMainModule() {
425:   if (!process.argv[1]) return false;
426:   try {
427:     return fs.realpathSync(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) === fs.realpathSync(process.argv[1]);
428:   } catch {
429:     // pathToFileURL normalizes Windows paths; keep it as a fallback for any
430:     // environment where realpath is unavailable.
431:     return import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href;
432:   }
433: }
434: // Why the realpath check: generated skills are often reached through symlinked
435: // harness directories (for example a demo repo's `.agents` -> source `.agents`).
436: // Node resolves import.meta.url to the real file, while process.argv[1] keeps
437: // the symlink path. Comparing canonical paths prevents a silent exit-0 no-op.
438: if (isMainModule()) {
439:   main(process.argv.slice(2));
440: }
````

````javascript
  1: /**
  2:  * Scan a project tree for Content-Security-Policy signals and classify the
  3:  * shape so the agent knows which patch template to propose.
  4:  *
  5:  * Used at first-time `live.mjs` setup. Mechanical (grep-based) — no network,
  6:  * no dev server, no JS evaluation. The classification drives a user-facing
  7:  * consent prompt; the agent does the actual patch writing.
  8:  *
  9:  * Shapes are named by patch mechanism, not framework origin:
 10:  *   - "append-arrays":  CSP defined as structured directive arrays. Patch
 11:  *                       appends a dev-only localhost entry. Covers:
 12:  *                         - Monorepo helpers with additional*Src options
 13:  *                           (e.g. createBaseNextConfig for Next)
 14:  *                         - SvelteKit kit.csp.directives
 15:  *                         - nuxt-security module's contentSecurityPolicy
 16:  *   - "append-string":  CSP built as a literal value string. Patch splices
 17:  *                       a dev-only token into script-src and connect-src.
 18:  *                       Covers:
 19:  *                         - Inline Next.js headers() with CSP string
 20:  *                         - Nuxt routeRules / nitro.routeRules CSP headers
 21:  *   - "middleware":     CSP set dynamically in middleware.{ts,js}.
 22:  *                       Detected but not auto-patched in v1.
 23:  *   - "meta-tag":       <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"> in
 24:  *                       layout files. Detected but not auto-patched in v1.
 25:  *   - null:             no CSP signals found; no patch needed.
 26:  */
 27: import fs from 'node:fs';
 28: import path from 'node:path';
 29: const SKIP_DIRS = new Set([
 30:   'node_modules',
 31:   '.git',
 32:   '.next',
 33:   '.turbo',
 34:   '.svelte-kit',
 35:   '.nuxt',
 36:   '.astro',
 37:   'dist',
 38:   'build',
 39:   'out',
 40:   '.vercel',
 41: ]);
 42: const SCAN_EXTS = new Set(['.js', '.mjs', '.cjs', '.ts', '.mts', '.cts', '.tsx', '.jsx']);
 43: const LAYOUT_EXTS = new Set(['.tsx', '.jsx', '.astro', '.vue', '.svelte', '.html']);
 44: const MAX_DEPTH = 6;
 45: const MAX_READ_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
 46: // append-arrays signals: CSP expressed as structured directive arrays
 47: const MONOREPO_HELPER_SIGNALS = [
 48:   /\bbuildCSPConfig\b/,
 49:   /\bbuildSecurityHeaders\b/,
 50:   /\badditionalScriptSrc\b/,
 51:   /\badditionalConnectSrc\b/,
 52:   /\bcreateBaseNextConfig\b/,
 53: ];
 54: const SVELTEKIT_CSP_SIGNALS = [
 55:   /\bkit\s*:/,
 56:   /\bcsp\s*:/,
 57:   /\bdirectives\s*:/,
 58: ];
 59: const NUXT_SECURITY_SIGNALS = [
 60:   /['"]nuxt-security['"]/,
 61:   /\bcontentSecurityPolicy\b/,
 62: ];
 63: // append-string signals: CSP written as a literal value string
 64: const INLINE_HEADER_SIGNALS = [
 65:   /["']Content-Security-Policy["']/i,
 66:   /\bscript-src\b/,
 67:   /\bconnect-src\b/,
 68: ];
 69: const NUXT_ROUTE_RULES_SIGNALS = [
 70:   /\brouteRules\b/,
 71:   /Content-Security-Policy/i,
 72:   /\bscript-src\b/,
 73: ];
 74: const MIDDLEWARE_HINT = /headers\.set\(\s*["']Content-Security-Policy["']/i;
 75: const META_TAG_HINT = /http-equiv\s*=\s*["']Content-Security-Policy["']/i;
 76: /**
 77:  * @param {string} cwd Project root.
 78:  * @returns {{ shape: string|null, signals: string[] }}
 79:  */
 80: export function detectCsp(cwd = process.cwd()) {
 81:   const hits = { appendArrays: [], appendString: [], middleware: [], metaTag: [] };
 82:   walk(cwd, cwd, 0, (absPath, relPath, body) => {
 83:     const ext = path.extname(absPath);
 84:     const base = path.basename(absPath).toLowerCase();
 85:     const isConfig = (name) =>
 86:       new RegExp('(^|/)' + name + '\\.config\\.').test(relPath);
 87:     // === append-arrays candidates ===
 88:     // Monorepo CSP helper: packages/*/src/.../(config|security)/*
 89:     if (SCAN_EXTS.has(ext) &&
 90:         /packages\/[^/]+\/src\/.*(config|next-config|security)/.test(relPath) &&
 91:         MONOREPO_HELPER_SIGNALS.some((re) => re.test(body))) {
 92:       hits.appendArrays.push(relPath);
 93:       return;
 94:     }
 95:     // SvelteKit kit.csp.directives
 96:     if (SCAN_EXTS.has(ext) && isConfig('svelte') &&
 97:         SVELTEKIT_CSP_SIGNALS.every((re) => re.test(body))) {
 98:       hits.appendArrays.push(relPath);
 99:       return;
100:     }
101:     // Nuxt nuxt-security module
102:     if (SCAN_EXTS.has(ext) && isConfig('nuxt') &&
103:         NUXT_SECURITY_SIGNALS.every((re) => re.test(body))) {
104:       hits.appendArrays.push(relPath);
105:       return;
106:     }
107:     // === append-string candidates ===
108:     // Inline headers in Next/Nuxt/SvelteKit/Astro/Vite config
109:     if (SCAN_EXTS.has(ext) &&
110:         /(^|\/)(next|nuxt|vite|astro|svelte)\.config\./.test(relPath) &&
111:         INLINE_HEADER_SIGNALS.every((re) => re.test(body))) {
112:       // Nuxt routeRules is a sub-shape of append-string; we already covered
113:       // nuxt-security above via return, so any remaining Nuxt CSP match here
114:       // is a route-rules / inline-headers case. Either way, same patch
115:       // mechanism.
116:       hits.appendString.push(relPath);
117:       return;
118:     }
119:     // === detect-only shapes ===
120:     if ((base === 'middleware.ts' || base === 'middleware.js' || base === 'middleware.mjs') &&
121:         MIDDLEWARE_HINT.test(body)) {
122:       hits.middleware.push(relPath);
123:     }
124:     if (LAYOUT_EXTS.has(ext) && META_TAG_HINT.test(body)) {
125:       hits.metaTag.push(relPath);
126:     }
127:   });
128:   // Priority: append-arrays > append-string > middleware > meta-tag.
129:   // Structured patches are safer than string splices; runtime and HTML
130:   // injection patches are less reliable and v1 doesn't auto-apply them.
131:   if (hits.appendArrays.length > 0) {
132:     return { shape: 'append-arrays', signals: hits.appendArrays };
133:   }
134:   if (hits.appendString.length > 0) {
135:     return { shape: 'append-string', signals: hits.appendString };
136:   }
137:   if (hits.middleware.length > 0) {
138:     return { shape: 'middleware', signals: hits.middleware };
139:   }
140:   if (hits.metaTag.length > 0) {
141:     return { shape: 'meta-tag', signals: hits.metaTag };
142:   }
143:   return { shape: null, signals: [] };
144: }
145: function walk(root, dir, depth, visit) {
146:   if (depth > MAX_DEPTH) return;
147:   let entries;
148:   try { entries = fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }); }
149:   catch { return; }
150:   for (const entry of entries) {
151:     const abs = path.join(dir, entry.name);
152:     if (entry.isDirectory()) {
153:       if (SKIP_DIRS.has(entry.name)) continue;
154:       walk(root, abs, depth + 1, visit);
155:       continue;
156:     }
157:     if (!entry.isFile()) continue;
158:     const ext = path.extname(entry.name);
159:     if (!SCAN_EXTS.has(ext) && !LAYOUT_EXTS.has(ext)) continue;
160:     let body;
161:     try {
162:       const fd = fs.openSync(abs, 'r');
163:       try {
164:         const buf = Buffer.alloc(MAX_READ_BYTES);
165:         const n = fs.readSync(fd, buf, 0, MAX_READ_BYTES, 0);
166:         body = buf.slice(0, n).toString('utf-8');
167:       } finally { fs.closeSync(fd); }
168:     } catch { continue; }
169:     visit(abs, path.relative(root, abs), body);
170:   }
171: }
172: // CLI mode
173: const _running = process.argv[1];
174: if (_running?.endsWith('detect-csp.mjs') || _running?.endsWith('detect-csp.mjs/')) {
175:   const result = detectCsp(process.cwd());
176:   console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
177: }
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/detect.mjs
````javascript
 1: #!/usr/bin/env node
 2: import fs from 'node:fs';
 3: import path from 'node:path';
 4: import { pathToFileURL, fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
 5: const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
 6: const candidates = [
 7:   path.join(__dirname, 'detector', 'detect-antipatterns.mjs'),
 8:   path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'cli', 'engine', 'detect-antipatterns.mjs'),
 9: ];
10: const detectorPath = candidates.find(p => fs.existsSync(p));
11: if (!detectorPath) {
12:   process.stderr.write('Error: bundled detector not found.\n');
13:   process.exit(1);
14: }
15: const { detectCli } = await import(pathToFileURL(detectorPath));
16: // A comp-led build with its comp round or hero gate still open is not a page
17: // the detector can pass: say so after the scan (stderr, so --json stays
18: // parseable), on the same condition context.mjs reports at boot.
19: try {
20:   const { compRoundOpen } = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(__dirname, 'build-phase.mjs')));
21:   const open = compRoundOpen(process.cwd());
22:   if (open) process.stderr.write(`COMP_ROUND_OPEN: ${open.reason}. A detector pass is not a finish: run node ${__dirname}/build-phase.mjs status and follow its NEXT line before treating this page as built.\n`);
23: } catch { /* build-phase absent */ }
24: await detectCli();
````

````javascript
  1: #!/usr/bin/env node
  2: /**
  3:  * Deep staleness pass over Impeccable's own project artifacts.
  4:  *
  5:  *   node doctor.mjs                 # human-readable report
  6:  *   node doctor.mjs --json          # machine-readable, for the skill command
  7:  *   node doctor.mjs --fix           # apply the mechanical migrations only
  8:  *   node doctor.mjs --target <path> # pick a monorepo workspace
  9:  *
 10:  * The boot check in context.mjs reports what a session can afford to measure.
 11:  * This runs everything: git drift, per-workspace sweep, ignore-list validation
 12:  * against the live rule registry, hook script resolution.
 13:  *
 14:  * `--fix` is deliberately narrow. It performs only the migrations marked
 15:  * severity 'auto', the ones with no judgment in them: stamp the product record,
 16:  * move a sidecar out of a retired location. Anything that needs an answer from
 17:  * the user (a platform value, whether an inherited record still describes an
 18:  * app, whether a document has drifted from the code) is reported and left
 19:  * alone. Exit code is 0 unless the run itself failed; findings are not errors.
 20:  */

 22: import path from 'node:path';
 23: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

 27: import { parseDesignMd } from './lib/design-parser.mjs';

 32: } from './lib/artifact-schema.mjs';

 39:   checkDesignCoverage,

 61:     else if (arg === '--help' || arg === '-h') flags.help = true;

 65: }

 69:     '',

 71:     'installed version reads: PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar,',
 72:     '.impeccable/config.json, surface briefs, and the design hook.',
 73:     '',
 74:     '  --json           Emit findings as JSON.',
 75:     '  --fix            Apply the mechanical migrations (severity "auto") only.',
 76:     '  --target <path>  Select a workspace in a monorepo.',
 77:   ].join('\n');
 78: }
 79: async function collect(cwd, targetOptions) {
 80:   const ctx = loadContext(cwd, targetOptions);
 81:   const projectRoot = ctx.projectRoot || cwd;
 82:   const absProductPath = ctx.productPath ? path.resolve(cwd, ctx.productPath) : null;
 83:   const absDesignPath = ctx.designPath ? path.resolve(cwd, ctx.designPath) : null;
 84:   const sidecarCandidates = designSidecarCandidatesFor(projectRoot, ctx.contextDir);
 85:   const knownRuleIds = await loadKnownRuleIds(SCRIPTS_DIR);
 86:   const selection = resolveTargetSelection(cwd, targetOptions);
 87:   const workspaceCandidates = selection?.targetCandidates || [];

101:   const findings = [
102:     ...bootFindings.product,
103:     ...bootFindings.nativePlatform,
104:     ...bootFindings.designSidecar,

106:     ...checkDesignCoverage({ design: ctx.design, designPath: ctx.designPath, parseDesignMd }),
107:     ...bootFindings.config,
108:     ...bootFindings.buildPath,
109:     ...checkDetectorIgnores({ projectRoot, knownRuleIds }),
110:     ...bootFindings.surfaceBriefs,

251: async function cli() {

253:   try {

255:   } catch (err) {

258:   }
259:   if (parsed.flags.help) {
````
