````javascript
 529:     leaseEvent(entry, poll.leaseMs).then(poll.resolve, (error) => {
 530:       console.error('[live] lease failed for ' + (entry.event?.id || 'unknown') + ': ' + (error?.message || error));
 531:       poll.resolve({ type: 'timeout' });
 532:     });
 533:     changed = true;
 534:   }
 535:   scheduleLeaseFlush();
 536:   if (changed) broadcastAgentPollingIfChanged();
 537: }
 538: function isLeased(entry) {
 539:   return !!(entry?.leaseUntil && entry.leaseUntil > Date.now());
 540: }
 541: function agentPollingConnected() {
 542:   // A leased event only proves that a poll returned once. The foreground task
 543:   // may have ended immediately afterward, so only an actively waiting poll is
 544:   // evidence that steering can wake the task right now.
 545:   return state.pendingPolls.length > 0;
 546: }
 547: function broadcastAgentPollingIfChanged() {
 548:   const connected = agentPollingConnected();
 549:   if (state.lastAgentPollingBroadcast === connected) return;
 550:   state.lastAgentPollingBroadcast = connected;
 551:   broadcast({ type: 'agent_polling', connected });
 552: }
 553: /** Push a message to all connected SSE clients. */
 554: function broadcast(msg) {
 555:   const data = 'data: ' + JSON.stringify(msg) + '\n\n';
 556:   for (const res of state.sseClients) {
 557:     try { res.write(data); } catch { /* client gone */ }
 558:   }
 559: }
 560: function recordManualEditActivity(type, details = {}) {
 561:   const entry = {
 562:     seq: state.nextManualEditSeq++,
 563:     type,
 564:     ts: new Date().toISOString(),
 565:     ...details,
 566:   };
 567:   state.manualEditActivity = entry;
 568:   if (DEBUG_MANUAL_EDIT_EVENTS) {
 569:     try {
 570:       const filePath = path.join(getLiveDir(process.cwd()), 'manual-edit-events.jsonl');
 571:       fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true });
 572:       fs.appendFileSync(filePath, JSON.stringify(entry) + '\n');
 573:     } catch {
 574:       /* diagnostics are best-effort; never block live mode on observability */
 575:     }
 576:   }
 577:   broadcast(entry);
 578:   return entry;
 579: }
 580: function getManualEditStatus() {
 581:   try {
 582:     const { totalCount, perPage } = countPendingByPage(process.cwd());
 583:     return { totalCount, perPage, lastActivity: state.manualEditActivity };
 584:   } catch (err) {
 585:     return {
 586:       totalCount: null,
 587:       perPage: {},
 588:       lastActivity: state.manualEditActivity,
 589:       error: err.message,
 590:     };
 591:   }
 592: }
 593: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 594: // Load scripts
 595: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 596: function loadBrowserScripts() {
 597:   // Detection script: prefer the skill-bundled detector, then fall back to
 598:   // source/npm package locations for local development and older installs.
 599:   // This one IS cached — detect.js rarely changes during a session.
 600:   const detectPaths = [
 601:     path.join(__dirname, 'detector', 'detect-antipatterns-browser.js'),
 602:     path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'cli', 'engine', 'detect-antipatterns-browser.js'),
 603:     path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', '..', 'cli', 'engine', 'detect-antipatterns-browser.js'),
 604:     path.join(process.cwd(), 'node_modules', 'impeccable', 'cli', 'engine', 'detect-antipatterns-browser.js'),
 605:   ];
 606:   let detectScript = '';
 607:   for (const p of detectPaths) {
 608:     try { detectScript = fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf-8'); break; } catch { /* try next */ }
 609:   }
 610:   // Browser script parts: DO NOT cache. Return paths so the /live.js handler
 611:   // can re-read every part on each request. Editing browser code during
 612:   // iteration should land on the next tab reload, not require a server restart.
 613:   const liveScriptParts = resolveLiveBrowserScriptParts(__dirname);
 614:   try {
 615:     assertLiveBrowserScriptParts(liveScriptParts);
 616:   } catch (err) {
 617:     process.stderr.write('Error: ' + err.message + '\n');
 618:     process.exit(1);
 619:   }
 620:   return { detectScript, liveScriptParts };
 621: }
 622: function hasProjectContext() {
 623:   // PRODUCT.md carries brand voice / anti-references — that's what determines
 624:   // whether variants are brand-aware. DESIGN.md (visual tokens) is a separate
 625:   // concern, surfaced by the design panel's own empty state.
 626:   return !!resolveProjectContext().hasProduct;
 627: }
 628: function statOrNull(filePath) {
 629:   try { return fs.statSync(filePath); } catch { return null; }
 630: }
 631: // Strict loopback-origin test for CORS. Parses the Origin as a URL (never a
 632: // substring match, so `http://localhost.evil.com` and `http://127.0.0.1.evil.com`
 633: // fail) and accepts only http/https on localhost, 127.0.0.1, or the IPv6 loopback.
 634: function isLoopbackOrigin(origin) {
 635:   if (typeof origin !== 'string' || origin.length === 0) return false;
 636:   let parsed;
 637:   try { parsed = new URL(origin); } catch { return false; }
 638:   if (parsed.protocol !== 'http:' && parsed.protocol !== 'https:') return false;
 639:   const host = parsed.hostname.toLowerCase();
 640:   return host === 'localhost' || host === '127.0.0.1' || host === '::1' || host === '[::1]';
 641: }
 642: // HTTP request handler
 643: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 644: function createRequestHandler({ detectScript, liveScriptParts }) {
 645:   return (req, res) => {
 646:     const url = new URL(req.url, `http://localhost:${state.port}`);
 647:     // Token-or-loopback CORS. Reflect the caller's Origin when it is a
 648:     // loopback origin OR the request carries the valid session token, always
 649:     // paired with `Vary: Origin` so an intermediary cache never serves a
 650:     // response authorized for one origin to another. A remote page (e.g.
 651:     // https://evil.example probing the port from a tab open on the same
 652:     // machine) has no token and gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so its
 653:     // JS-initiated fetch cannot read any response. The token branch exists for
 654:     // dev servers on non-localhost loopback aliases (ddev's *.ddev.site,
 655:     // Valet's *.test, hosts-file entries): the injected classic <script src>
 656:     // delivers the token to the page regardless of origin, every overlay
 657:     // request carries it in the query string (preflights included, since
 658:     // OPTIONS hits the same URL), and a token bearer is already fully
 659:     // authorized on every route — the token is the security boundary, not the
 660:     // origin. Requests with no Origin header (script tags, curl, the agent's
 661:     // own fetches) are not subject to CORS and keep working; no ACAO header
 662:     // is needed for them.
 663:     const origin = req.headers.origin;
 664:     if (origin && (isLoopbackOrigin(origin) || url.searchParams.get('token') === state.token)) {
 665:       res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', origin);
 666:       res.setHeader('Vary', 'Origin');
 667:     }
 668:     res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Methods', 'GET, POST, OPTIONS');
 669:     res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Headers', 'Content-Type');
 670:     if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') { res.writeHead(204); res.end(); return; }
 671:     const p = url.pathname;
 672:     // --- Scripts ---
 673:     if (p === '/live.js') {
 674:       // Token-gated: the script body embeds state.token, which unlocks every
 675:       // token-guarded route. Serving it unauthenticated let any local page read
 676:       // the token and drive the session. The injected <script src> carries
 677:       // `?token=...` (see live-inject.mjs). A missing/wrong token → 401.
 678:       if (url.searchParams.get('token') !== state.token) {
 679:         res.writeHead(401, { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain' });
 680:         res.end('Unauthorized');
 681:         return;
 682:       }
 683:       // Re-read from disk each request so edits to live-browser.js land on
 684:       // the next tab reload. No-store headers prevent browser caching across
 685:       // sessions — during iteration, a cached old script silently breaks
 686:       // every subsequent session.
 687:       let parts;
 688:       try {
 689:         parts = readLiveBrowserScriptParts(liveScriptParts);
 690:       } catch (err) {
 691:         res.writeHead(500, { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain' });
 692:         res.end('Error reading live browser scripts: ' + err.message);
 693:         return;
 694:       }
 695:       const body = assembleLiveBrowserScript({
 696:         token: state.token,
 697:         port: state.port,
 698:         vocabulary: LIVE_COMMANDS,
 699:         commandPrefix: IMPECCABLE_COMMAND_PREFIX,
 700:         appRoot: process.cwd(),
 701:         parts,
 702:         // Read per request rather than cached, so editing the config and
 703:         // reloading the tab is enough to pick up a new waiver. Config comes
 704:         // from every root the session spans (appRoot, contextRoot, repoRoot):
 705:         // in a monorepo the hook and the CLI key it at the repo root, which
 706:         // is not the appRoot this process chdir'd onto.
 707:         projectIgnores: collectProjectDetectorIgnores({
 708:           appRoot: process.cwd(),
 709:           contextRoot: LIVE_ROOTS?.contextRoot,
 710:           repoRoot: LIVE_ROOTS?.repoRoot,
 711:           scriptsDir: __dirname,
 712:         }),
 713:       });
 714:       res.writeHead(200, {
 715:         'Content-Type': 'application/javascript; charset=utf-8',
 716:         'Cache-Control': 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0',
 717:         'Pragma': 'no-cache',
 718:       });
 719:       res.end(body);
 720:       return;
 721:     }
 722:     if (p === '/detect.js' || p === '/') {
 723:       if (!detectScript) { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not available'); return; }
 724:       res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/javascript; charset=utf-8' });
 725:       res.end(detectScript);
 726:       return;
 727:     }
 728:     // --- Vendored modern-screenshot (UMD build) ---
 729:     // Lazy-loaded by live.js when the user clicks Go; exposes
 730:     // window.modernScreenshot.domToBlob(...) for capture.
 731:     if (p === '/modern-screenshot.js') {
 732:       const vendorPath = path.join(__dirname, 'modern-screenshot.umd.js');
 733:       try {
 734:         res.writeHead(200, {
 735:           'Content-Type': 'application/javascript',
 736:           'Cache-Control': 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable',
 737:         });
 738:         res.end(fs.readFileSync(vendorPath));
 739:       } catch {
 740:         res.writeHead(404); res.end('Vendor script not found');
 741:       }
 742:       return;
 743:     }
 744:     // --- Annotation upload (browser → server, raw PNG body) ---
 745:     // Client generates the eventId, POSTs the PNG, then POSTs the generate
 746:     // event with screenshotPath already set. Keeps bytes out of the SSE/poll
 747:     // bridge and preserves the "one shot from the user's POV" UX.
 748:     if (p === '/annotation' && req.method === 'POST') {
 749:       const token = url.searchParams.get('token');
 750:       if (token !== state.token) { res.writeHead(401); res.end('Unauthorized'); return; }
 751:       const eventId = url.searchParams.get('eventId');
 752:       if (!eventId || !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(eventId)) {
 753:         res.writeHead(400, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 754:         res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Invalid eventId' }));
 755:         return;
 756:       }
 757:       if ((req.headers['content-type'] || '').toLowerCase() !== 'image/png') {
 758:         res.writeHead(415, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 759:         res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Content-Type must be image/png' }));
 760:         return;
 761:       }
 762:       if (!state.sessionDir) {
 763:         res.writeHead(500, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 764:         res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Session dir unavailable' }));
 765:         return;
 766:       }
 767:       const chunks = [];
 768:       let total = 0;
 769:       let aborted = false;
 770:       req.on('data', (c) => {
 771:         if (aborted) return;
 772:         total += c.length;
 773:         if (total > MAX_ANNOTATION_BYTES) {
 774:           aborted = true;
 775:           res.writeHead(413, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 776:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Payload too large' }));
 777:           req.destroy();
 778:           return;
 779:         }
 780:         chunks.push(c);
 781:       });
 782:       req.on('end', () => {
 783:         if (aborted) return;
 784:         const absPath = path.join(state.sessionDir, eventId + '.png');
 785:         try {
 786:           fs.writeFileSync(absPath, Buffer.concat(chunks));
 787:         } catch (err) {
 788:           res.writeHead(500, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 789:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Write failed: ' + err.message }));
 790:           return;
 791:         }
 792:         res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 793:         res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, path: absPath }));
 794:       });
 795:       req.on('error', () => {
 796:         if (!aborted) {
 797:           res.writeHead(500, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 798:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Upload failed' }));
 799:         }
 800:       });
 801:       return;
 802:     }
 803:     // --- Health ---
 804:     if (p === '/status') {
 805:       const token = url.searchParams.get('token');
 806:       if (token !== state.token) { res.writeHead(401, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Unauthorized' })); return; }
 807:       const sessions = activeSessionSummaries();
 808:       res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 809:       res.end(JSON.stringify({
 810:         status: 'ok',
 811:         port: state.port,
 812:         connectedClients: state.sseClients.size,
 813:         pendingEvents: state.pendingEvents.map((entry) => summarizePendingEventForStatus(entry)),
 814:         agentPolling: agentPollingConnected(),
 815:         activeSessions: sessions,
 816:         manualEdits: getManualEditStatus(),
 817:       }));
 818:       return;
 819:     }
 820:     if (p === '/health') {
 821:       res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 822:       res.end(JSON.stringify({
 823:         status: 'ok', port: state.port, mode: 'variant',
 824:         hasProjectContext: hasProjectContext(),
 825:         connectedClients: state.sseClients.size,
 826:       }));
 827:       return;
 828:     }
 829:     // --- Design system (unified v2 response) + raw ---
 830:     //   /design-system.json    returns both parsed DESIGN.md and .impeccable/design.json
 831:     //                          sidecar when present. Panel merges them:
 832:     //                            { present, parsed, sidecar, hasMd, hasSidecar,
 833:     //                              mdNewerThanJson, parseError?, sidecarError? }
 834:     //                          - parsed: output of parseDesignMd (frontmatter
 835:     //                            + the canonical sections) when DESIGN.md exists.
 836:     //                          - sidecar: .impeccable/design.json contents when present.
 837:     //                            Expected shape: schemaVersion 2, carrying
 838:     //                            extensions + components + narrative.
 839:     //   /design-system/raw     returns DESIGN.md markdown verbatim
 840:     if (p === '/design-system.json' || p === '/design-system/raw') {
 841:       const token = url.searchParams.get('token');
 842:       if (token !== state.token) { res.writeHead(401); res.end('Unauthorized'); return; }
 843:       const projectContext = resolveProjectContext();
 844:       const mdPath = projectContext.resolvedDesignPath;
 845:       const jsonPath = resolveDesignSidecarPath(process.cwd(), projectContext.designContextDir || projectContext.contextDir) || getDesignSidecarPath(process.cwd());
 846:       const mdStat = statOrNull(mdPath);
 847:       const jsonStat = statOrNull(jsonPath);
 848:       if (p === '/design-system/raw') {
 849:         if (!mdStat) { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found'); return; }
 850:         res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/markdown; charset=utf-8' });
 851:         res.end(fs.readFileSync(mdPath, 'utf-8'));
 852:         return;
 853:       }
 854:       if (!mdStat && !jsonStat) {
 855:         res.writeHead(404, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 856:         res.end(JSON.stringify({ present: false }));
 857:         return;
 858:       }
 859:       const response = {
 860:         present: true,
 861:         hasMd: !!mdStat,
 862:         hasSidecar: !!jsonStat,
 863:         mdNewerThanJson: !!(mdStat && jsonStat && mdStat.mtimeMs > jsonStat.mtimeMs + 1000),
 864:       };
 865:       if (mdStat) {
 866:         try {
 867:           response.parsed = parseDesignMd(fs.readFileSync(mdPath, 'utf-8'));
 868:         } catch (err) {
 869:           response.parseError = err.message;
 870:         }
 871:       }
 872:       if (jsonStat) {
 873:         try {
 874:           response.sidecar = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(jsonPath, 'utf-8'));
 875:         } catch (err) {
 876:           response.sidecarError = 'Failed to parse .impeccable/design.json: ' + err.message;
 877:         }
 878:       }
 879:       res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 880:       res.end(JSON.stringify(response));
 881:       return;
 882:     }
 883:     // --- Source file (no-HMR fallback) ---
 884:     if (p === '/source') {
 885:       const token = url.searchParams.get('token');
 886:       if (token !== state.token) { res.writeHead(401); res.end('Unauthorized'); return; }
 887:       const filePath = url.searchParams.get('path');
 888:       if (!filePath || filePath.includes('..')) { res.writeHead(400); res.end('Bad path'); return; }
 889:       const absPath = path.resolve(process.cwd(), filePath);
 890:       let realRoot, realTarget;
 891:       try {
 892:         realRoot = fs.realpathSync(process.cwd());
 893:         realTarget = fs.realpathSync(absPath);
 894:       } catch {
 895:         res.writeHead(404); res.end('File not found'); return;
 896:       }
 897:       // Confine to the project root after symlink resolution. A bare
 898:       // `startsWith(cwd)` string check lets a sibling dir whose name extends the
 899:       // root name (projeto -> projeto-backup) slip through; compare on the
 900:       // relative path instead (same pattern as sessionFileMetadataFromPollReply
 901:       // below). An empty rel means the request resolved to the root directory
 902:       // itself, which this file route never serves.
 903:       const rel = path.relative(realRoot, realTarget);
 904:       if (!rel || rel.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(rel)) { res.writeHead(403); res.end('Forbidden'); return; }
 905:       let content;
 906:       try { content = fs.readFileSync(realTarget, 'utf-8'); }
 907:       catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('File not found'); return; }
 908:       res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' });
 909:       res.end(content);
 910:       return;
 911:     }
 912:     // --- SSE: server→browser push (replaces WebSocket) ---
 913:     if (p === '/events' && req.method === 'GET') {
 914:       const token = url.searchParams.get('token');
 915:       if (token !== state.token) { res.writeHead(401); res.end('Unauthorized'); return; }
 916:       clearTimeout(state.exitTimer);
 917:       state.exitTimer = null;
 918:       cancelQueuedAnonymousExitEvents();
 919:       res.writeHead(200, {
 920:         'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
 921:         'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
 922:         'Connection': 'keep-alive',
 923:       });
 924:       res.write('data: ' + JSON.stringify({
 925:         type: 'connected',
 926:         hasProjectContext: hasProjectContext(),
 927:         agentPolling: agentPollingConnected(),
 928:         activeSessions: activeSessionSummaries(),
 929:       }) + '\n\n');
 930:       state.sseClients.add(res);
 931:       // Keepalive: SSE comment every 30s prevents silent connection drops.
 932:       const heartbeat = setInterval(() => {
 933:         try { res.write(': keepalive\n\n'); } catch { clearInterval(heartbeat); }
 934:       }, SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL);
 935:       req.on('close', () => {
 936:         clearInterval(heartbeat);
 937:         state.sseClients.delete(res);
 938:         if (state.sseClients.size === 0) {
 939:           clearTimeout(state.exitTimer);
 940:           state.exitTimer = setTimeout(() => {
 941:             if (state.sseClients.size === 0) enqueueEvent({ type: 'exit' });
 942:           }, 8000);
 943:         }
 944:       });
 945:       return;
 946:     }
 947:     if (manualEditRoutes(req, res, url)) return;
 948:     // --- Browser→server events (replaces WebSocket messages) ---
 949:     if (p === '/events' && req.method === 'POST') {
 950:       let body = '';
 951:       req.on('data', (c) => { body += c; });
 952:       req.on('end', () => {
 953:         let msg;
 954:         try { msg = JSON.parse(body); } catch {
 955:           res.writeHead(400, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 956:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Invalid JSON' }));
 957:           return;
 958:         }
 959:         if (msg.token !== state.token) {
 960:           res.writeHead(401, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 961:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Unauthorized' }));
 962:           return;
 963:         }
 964:         // Defense in depth: manual copy edits must use the staged stash/apply
 965:         // endpoints. The direct Save event path is disabled in the browser.
 966:         if (msg.type === 'manual_edits') {
 967:           res.writeHead(400, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 968:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'manual_edits must POST to /manual-edit-stash, not /events' }));
 969:           return;
 970:         }
 971:         if (msg.type === 'manual_edit_apply') {
 972:           res.writeHead(400, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 973:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'manual_edit_apply is disabled; use /manual-edit-stash then /manual-edit-commit' }));
 974:           return;
 975:         }
 976:         const error = validateEvent(msg);
 977:         if (error) {
 978:           res.writeHead(400, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 979:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ error }));
 980:           return;
 981:         }
 982:         stripPollerOwnedEventFields(msg);
 983:         if (msg.type === 'agent_phase') {
 984:           recordAgentPhase(msg.id, msg.phase, {
 985:             ...(Number.isFinite(msg.durationMs) ? { durationMs: msg.durationMs } : {}),
 986:             owner: typeof msg.owner === 'string' ? msg.owner : undefined,
 987:           });
 988:           res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
 989:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: true }));
 990:           return;
 991:         }
 992:         // Only the events that START a session may create its journal.
 993:         // Everything else (checkpoints, mount acks, accept/discard) must
 994:         // reference a session THIS store already knows: appendEvent creates a
 995:         // journal for any id it is handed, so without this gate a browser
 996:         // resuming another project's session from per-origin storage (two
 997:         // apps sharing a localhost port) materializes a ghost session here
 998:         // that keeps reattaching after every discard.
 999:         if (msg.id && state.sessionStore
1000:             && !SESSION_CREATING_EVENT_TYPES.has(msg.type)
1001:             && !state.sessionStore.has(msg.id)) {
1002:           res.writeHead(404, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
1003:           res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'unknown_session', id: msg.id }));
1004:           return;
1005:         }
1006:         const missedCompletion = detectMissedGenerationCompletion(msg);
1007:         if (state.sessionStore && msg.id) {
1008:           try {
1009:             state.sessionStore.appendEvent(msg);
1010:           } catch (err) {
1011:             res.writeHead(500, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });

1072: // Agent poll endpoints (unchanged from WS version)

1074: function parsePollTypes(value) {
1075:   if (!value) return null;
1076:   const types = String(value).split(',').map((type) => type.trim()).filter(Boolean);
1077:   return types.length > 0 ? new Set(types) : null;
1078: }
1079: function handlePollGet(req, res, url) {
1080:   const token = url.searchParams.get('token');
1081:   if (token !== state.token) {
1082:     res.writeHead(401, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
1083:     res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Unauthorized' }));
1084:     return;
1085:   }
1086:   state.lastPollAt = Date.now();
1087:   const timeout = parseInt(url.searchParams.get('timeout') || DEFAULT_POLL_TIMEOUT, 10);
1088:   const leaseMs = parseInt(url.searchParams.get('leaseMs') || '30000', 10);
1089:   const types = parsePollTypes(url.searchParams.get('types'));
1090:   const available = findAvailablePendingEvent(Date.now(), types);
1091:   if (available) {
1092:     // Do not await inline: leaseEvent may scaffold source, and this handler runs
1093:     // on the server's only thread. The client can disconnect during that window,
1094:     // so check the socket before replying.
1095:     leaseEvent(available, leaseMs).then((event) => {
1096:       if (res.writableEnded || res.destroyed) return;
1097:       res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
1098:       res.end(JSON.stringify(event));
1099:     }, (error) => {
1100:       console.error('[live] lease failed for ' + (available.event?.id || 'unknown') + ': ' + (error?.message || error));
1101:       if (res.writableEnded || res.destroyed) return;
1102:       res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
1103:       res.end(JSON.stringify({ type: 'timeout' }));
1104:     });
1105:     return;
1106:   }
1107:   const poll = { resolve, leaseMs, types };
1108:   const timer = setTimeout(() => {
1109:     const idx = state.pendingPolls.indexOf(poll);
1110:     if (idx !== -1) state.pendingPolls.splice(idx, 1);
1111:     broadcastAgentPollingIfChanged();
1112:     res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
1113:     res.end(JSON.stringify({ type: 'timeout' }));
1114:   }, timeout);
1115:   function resolve(event) {
1116:     clearTimeout(timer);
1117:     state.lastPollAt = Date.now();
1118:     res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
1119:     res.end(JSON.stringify(event));
1120:   }
1121:   state.pendingPolls.push(poll);
1122:   broadcastAgentPollingIfChanged();
1123:   scheduleLeaseFlush();
1124:   req.on('close', () => {
1125:     clearTimeout(timer);
1126:     const idx = state.pendingPolls.indexOf(poll);
1127:     if (idx !== -1) state.pendingPolls.splice(idx, 1);
1128:     broadcastAgentPollingIfChanged();
1129:   });
1130: }
1131: function sessionFileMetadataFromPollReply(file) {
1132:   if (!file || typeof file !== 'string') return { file };
1133:   const normalized = file.split(path.sep).join('/');
1134:   const base = { file: normalized };
1135:   const metadataFile = normalized;
1136:   if (!metadataFile.endsWith('/manifest.json') && metadataFile !== 'manifest.json') return base;
1137:   if (!metadataFile.includes('.impeccable/live/previews/')
1138:       && !metadataFile.includes('node_modules/.impeccable-live/')
1139:       && !metadataFile.includes('src/lib/impeccable/')
1140:       && !metadataFile.includes('/.impeccable-live/')) return base;
1141:   let full;
1142:   try {
1143:     full = path.resolve(process.cwd(), metadataFile);
1144:     const rel = path.relative(process.cwd(), full);
1145:     if (!rel || rel.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(rel)) return base;
1146:   } catch {
1147:     return base;
1148:   }
1149:   try {
1150:     const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(full, 'utf-8'));
1151:     if (manifest?.previewMode !== 'svelte-component'
1152:         || !manifest.sourceFile) return base;
1153:     return {
1154:       file: String(manifest.sourceFile).split(path.sep).join('/'),
1155:       sourceFile: String(manifest.sourceFile).split(path.sep).join('/'),
1156:       previewFile: normalized,
1157:       previewMode: manifest.previewMode,
1158:     };
1159:   } catch {
1160:     return base;
1161:   }
1162: }
1163: function inferSourceEventType(msg = {}, pendingEvents = state.pendingEvents) {
1164:   const entriesForId = pendingEvents.filter((entry) => entry.event?.id === msg.id);
1165:   const pendingTypes = new Set(entriesForId.map((entry) => entry.event?.type));
1166:   if (msg.type === 'discarded' || msg.type === 'discard') return 'discard';
1167:   if (msg.type === 'complete') {
1168:     if (pendingTypes.has('carbonize_cleanup')) return 'carbonize_cleanup';
1169:     return pendingTypes.has('accept') ? 'accept' : (pendingTypes.has('generate') ? 'generate' : undefined);
1170:   }
1171:   if (msg.type === 'steer_done') return 'steer';
1172:   // `agent_done` can be the automatic acknowledgement for a carbonize Accept.
1173:   // New pollers send sourceEventType explicitly; default to generate only for
1174:   // older callers so a late worker cannot acknowledge a queued Accept.
1175:   if (msg.type === 'agent_done' || msg.type === 'done') {
1176:     // A `done` reply to a mount failure is the republish that unblocks the
1177:     // browser. Without this the ack would look for a `generate` that was
1178:     // already retired, the mount-failure event would stay queued, and the next
1179:     // poll would hand the same failure back to the agent forever.
1180:     if (!pendingTypes.has('generate') && pendingTypes.has('variant_mount_failed')) return 'variant_mount_failed';
1181:     return 'generate';
1182:   }
1183:   // `error` is reference/live.md's documented failure reply, and parseReplyArgs
1184:   // never sets sourceEventType on it (the poller is a fresh process that cannot
1185:   // know what it leased). Returning undefined here makes acknowledgePendingEvent
1186:   // match *any* event for this id: a stale generate worker's failure silently
1187:   // consumed the user's queued Accept, which was then never delivered to any
1188:   // agent and left the browser in SAVING forever. Attribute the failure to the
1189:   // event this agent actually holds a lease on, and otherwise to `generate` —
1190:   // never to a wildcard. If that generate was already retired by an Accept, the
1191:   // ack simply finds no match, which is the correct outcome for a stale reply.
1192:   if (msg.type === 'error') {
1193:     return entriesForId.find(isLeased)?.event?.type || 'generate';
1194:   }
1195:   return undefined;
1196: }

1373: let httpServer = null;

1377:   if (state.leaseTimer) clearTimeout(state.leaseTimer);

1389: function cleanupSvelteComponentSessionsBeforeExit() {

1391:     removeAllSvelteComponentSessions(process.cwd());

1394:   }

1400:  */

1402:   try {

1409:     }

1412:   }

1414: // Accept receipts are a short-lived idempotency record for a single accept.
1415: // Nothing reads one after the session that wrote it is gone, so they only need
1416: // to outlive a crash-and-retry window.
1417: const ACCEPT_RECEIPT_MAX_AGE_MS = 14 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

1419:   try {
1420:     const dir = path.join(getLiveDir(process.cwd()), 'accept-receipts');

1422:     const cutoff = Date.now() - ACCEPT_RECEIPT_MAX_AGE_MS;
1423:     let removed = 0;
1424:     for (const name of fs.readdirSync(dir)) {
1425:       if (!name.endsWith('.json') && !name.endsWith('.tmp')) continue;
1426:       const file = path.join(dir, name);
1427:       try {
1428:         if (fs.statSync(file).mtimeMs >= cutoff) continue;

1449: // Main

1451: const args = process.argv.slice(2);
1452: if (args.includes('--help') || args.includes('-h')) {
1453:   console.log(`Usage: node live-server.mjs [options]
1454: Start the live variant mode server (zero dependencies).
1455: Commands:
1456:   (default)     Start the server (foreground)
1457:   stop          Stop the server and remove the injected live.js script tag
1458:   stop --keep-inject   Stop the server only (leave the script tag in the HTML entry)
1459: Options:
1460:   --background  Start detached, print connection JSON to stdout, then exit
1461:   --port=PORT   Use a specific port (default: auto-detect starting at 8400)
1462:   --keep-inject Only with stop: skip live-inject.mjs --remove
1463:   --help        Show this help
1464: Endpoints:
1465:   /live.js             Browser script (element picker + variant cycling)
1466:   /detect.js           Detection overlay (backwards compatible)
1467:   /modern-screenshot.js Vendored modern-screenshot UMD build (lazy-loaded by live.js)
1468:   /annotation          POST raw image/png to stage a variant screenshot
1469:   /events              SSE stream (server→browser) + POST (browser→server)
1470:   /poll                Long-poll for agent CLI
1471:   /manual-edit-stash   Stage browser copy edits
1472:   /manual-edit-commit  Apply staged browser copy edits
1473:   /manual-edit-discard Discard staged browser copy edits
1474:   /source              Raw source file reader (no-HMR fallback)

1476:   /health              Health check`);
1477:   process.exit(0);
1478: }

1484:     if (res.ok) console.log(`Stopped live server on port ${info.port}.`);
1485:   } catch {
````

````javascript
 1: #!/usr/bin/env node
 2: /**
 3:  * Print durable recovery status for Impeccable live sessions.
 4:  */
 5: import { createLiveSessionStore } from './live/session-store.mjs';
 6: import { readLiveServerInfo } from './lib/impeccable-paths.mjs';
 7: import { manualApplyResumeHint, mountFailureAction, renderSummary } from './live-resume.mjs';
 8: import { enterLiveRoot } from './live/roots.mjs';
 9: function readServerInfo() {
10:   return readLiveServerInfo(process.cwd())?.info || null;
11: }
12: async function fetchServerStatus(info) {
13:   if (!info) return null;
14:   try {
15:     const res = await fetch(`http://localhost:${info.port}/status?token=${info.token}`);
16:     if (!res.ok) return null;
17:     return await res.json();
18:   } catch {
19:     return null;
20:   }
21: }
22: export async function statusCli() {
23:   const info = readServerInfo();
24:   const server = await fetchServerStatus(info);
25:   const store = createLiveSessionStore({ cwd: process.cwd() });
26:   const activeSessions = store.listActiveSessions();
27:   const manualApply = findPendingManualApply(server, activeSessions);
28:   const sessions = server?.activeSessions || activeSessions;
29:   const renderFailure = sessions.find((session) => session?.renderState === 'failed') || null;
30:   const payload = {
31:     liveServer: server ? {
32:       status: server.status,
33:       port: server.port,
34:       connectedClients: server.connectedClients,
35:       agentPolling: server.agentPolling,
36:       pendingEvents: server.pendingEvents,
37:     } : null,
38:     activeSessions: sessions,
39:     render: sessions.map((session) => ({ id: session?.id ?? null, ...renderSummary(session) })),
40:     recoveryHint: recoveryHint({ server, manualApply, renderFailure }),
41:   };
42:   console.log(JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2));
43: }
44: function recoveryHint({ server, manualApply, renderFailure }) {
45:   if (manualApply) return manualApplyResumeHint(manualApply);
46:   if (renderFailure) return mountFailureAction(renderFailure);
47:   if (server) {
48:     return 'Run live-poll.mjs to continue pending work, or live-complete.mjs --id <session> after manual cleanup.';
49:   }
50:   return 'Start live-server.mjs to requeue pending durable events, then run live-poll.mjs.';
51: }
52: function findPendingManualApply(server, activeSessions) {
53:   const fromServer = server?.pendingEvents?.find((event) => event?.type === 'manual_edit_apply');
54:   if (fromServer) return fromServer;
55:   const fromSession = activeSessions
56:     ?.map((session) => session.pendingEvent)
57:     .find((event) => event?.type === 'manual_edit_apply');
58:   return fromSession || null;
59: }
60: const _running = process.argv[1];
61: if (_running?.endsWith('live-status.mjs') || _running?.endsWith('live-status.mjs/')) {
62:   enterLiveRoot();
63:   statusCli();
64: }
````

````javascript
794:     if (!tag || self[1] === tag) return matchLine;
795:     return -1;
796:   }
797:   const MAX_BACKWALK = 10;
798:   for (let i = matchLine - 1; i >= Math.max(0, matchLine - MAX_BACKWALK); i--) {
799:     const opener = lines[i].match(OPENER_RE);
800:     if (!opener) continue;
801:     if (!tag || opener[1] === tag) return i;
802:     // Different tag name than requested — abort; we're inside a non-target opener.
803:     return -1;
804:   }
805:   return -1;

807: /**
808:  * Starting from a line with an opening tag, find the line with the matching
809:  * closing tag by counting tag nesting depth.
810:  */
811: function findClosingLine(lines, start) {
812:   const openMatch = lines[start].match(OPENER_RE);
813:   if (!openMatch) return start; // caller passed a non-opener; nothing to span
814:   const tagName = openMatch[1];
815:   let depth = 0;
816:   const openRe = new RegExp('<' + tagName + '(?=[\\s/>]|$)', 'g');
817:   const selfCloseRe = new RegExp('<' + tagName + '[^>]*/>', 'g');
818:   const closeRe = new RegExp('</' + tagName + '\\s*>', 'g');
819:   for (let i = start; i < lines.length; i++) {
820:     const line = lines[i];
821:     const opens = (line.match(openRe) || []).length;
822:     const selfCloses = (line.match(selfCloseRe) || []).length;
823:     const closes = (line.match(closeRe) || []).length;
824:     depth += opens - selfCloses - closes;
825:     if (depth <= 0) return i;
826:   }
827:   // If we can't find the close, return a reasonable guess
828:   return Math.min(start + 50, lines.length - 1);
829: }
830: // Auto-execute when run directly (node live-wrap.mjs ...)
831: const _running = process.argv[1];
832: if (_running?.endsWith('live-wrap.mjs') || _running?.endsWith('live-wrap.mjs/')) {
833:   enterLiveRoot();
834:   wrapCli();

838:   buildSearchQueries,

840:   findClosingLine,
841:   detectCommentSyntax,
842:   findAllElements,
843:   filterByText,
844:   findFileWithQuery,
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/palette.mjs
````javascript
  1: #!/usr/bin/env node
  2: /**
  3:  * Brand-seed picker. Returns one OKLCH seed color + the mood it most
  4:  * naturally evokes, and teaches the model how to compose a full palette
  5:  * around it.
  6:  *
  7:  * The seed is the brand's anchor color. The 5-role palette (bg, surface,
  8:  * ink, accent, muted) is composed by the caller at runtime using their
  9:  * judgment + the brief (PRODUCT.md / DESIGN.md / user prompt), NOT picked
 10:  * from a frozen 4-color preset.
 11:  *
 12:  * Why: 4-color frozen palettes drift toward safe defaults (warm-cream bg,
 13:  * complementary accent on near-white) regardless of brief. A single seed +
 14:  * the model's own composition lets the same seed produce a dark-mode jazz
 15:  * club or a light-mode hospitality brand depending on what the brief calls
 16:  * for. Tested empirically against curated 4-color palettes; seed approach
 17:  * wins on mood-fit in 3 of 5 cases and ties on the rest.
 18:  *
 19:  * Usage:
 20:  *   node scripts/palette.mjs                  # pick at random
 21:  *   node scripts/palette.mjs --id seed-021    # pick a specific seed
 22:  *   node scripts/palette.mjs --from <key>     # hash <key> to a seed (deterministic)
 23:  *
 24:  * Env vars:
 25:  *   IMPECCABLE_PALETTE_SEED — same as --from; useful for the eval harness
 26:  *     to make runs reproducible.
 27:  */
 28: import crypto from 'node:crypto';
 29: // Seeds are inlined (129 entries, hand-curated via a tinder review of
 30: // ~400 candidates from ColorHunt + synthesis + Radix/brand/Pantone anchors).
 31: // Each carries a mood + strategy the judging model produced — surfaced as
 32: // hints, not commands; the brief still drives composition.

419: function parseArgs(argv) {
420:   const args = { id: null, from: null };
421:   for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
422:     const a = argv[i];
423:     if (a === '--id' && argv[i + 1]) { args.id = argv[++i]; }
424:     else if (a === '--from' && argv[i + 1]) { args.from = argv[++i]; }
425:   }
426:   return args;
427: }
428: // Hash a key into a stable float in [0, 1) for deterministic weighted picks.
429: function hashUnit(key) {
430:   const h = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(key).digest();
431:   return h.readUInt32BE(0) / 0x100000000;
432: }
433: // The curated library is hue-skewed (more reds/oranges than teals/magentas)
434: // because that's where the source material + taste landed. Left uniform, a
435: // random pick would land on red ~1/3 of the time. Inverse-frequency weighting
436: // gives each seed a weight of 1/(count in its 30° hue bucket), so each hue
437: // ZONE is roughly equally likely to be chosen regardless of how many seeds it
438: // holds — fair rainbow exposure across runs without pruning the library.
439: function buildWeights(seeds) {
440:   const bucketCount = {};
441:   const bucketOf = (s) => Math.floor(((s.oklch[2] % 360) + 360) % 360 / 30);
442:   for (const s of seeds) { const b = bucketOf(s); bucketCount[b] = (bucketCount[b] || 0) + 1; }
443:   const weights = seeds.map((s) => 1 / bucketCount[bucketOf(s)]);
444:   const total = weights.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
445:   return { weights, total };
446: }
447: function weightedPick(seeds, unit) {
448:   const { weights, total } = buildWeights(seeds);
449:   let target = unit * total;
450:   for (let i = 0; i < seeds.length; i++) {
451:     target -= weights[i];
452:     if (target < 0) return seeds[i];
453:   }
454:   return seeds[seeds.length - 1];
455: }
456: function pickSeed(seeds, { id, from }) {
457:   if (id) {
458:     const found = seeds.find(s => s.id === id);
459:     if (!found) { console.error(`no seed with id "${id}"`); process.exit(2); }
460:     return found;
461:   }
462:   const envFrom = process.env.IMPECCABLE_PALETTE_SEED;
463:   const key = from || envFrom;
464:   const unit = key ? hashUnit(key) : Math.random();
465:   return weightedPick(seeds, unit);
466: }
467: function fmtOklch([L, C, H]) {
468:   return `oklch(${L.toFixed(3)} ${C.toFixed(3)} ${H.toFixed(1)})`;
469: }
470: function hueWord(H) {
471:   if (H < 15 || H >= 345) return 'pure red';
472:   if (H < 35)  return 'warm red / crimson';
473:   if (H < 55)  return 'warm coral / burnt orange';
474:   if (H < 80)  return 'orange / honey';
475:   if (H < 105) return 'warm amber / honey-gold';
476:   if (H < 135) return 'yellow-green / olive';
477:   if (H < 170) return 'green';
478:   if (H < 200) return 'teal';
479:   if (H < 230) return 'sky blue';
480:   if (H < 265) return 'cobalt / indigo';
481:   if (H < 295) return 'violet / purple';
482:   if (H < 330) return 'magenta / pink';
483:   return 'deep pink / rose';
484: }
485: // ---------------------------------------------------------------
486: const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
487: const seed = pickSeed(SEEDS, args);
488: const [L, C, H] = seed.oklch;
489: // The mood + strategy on each seed were derived by the model that
490: // originally judged it. We surface them as *hints*, not commands —
491: // the brief should still drive what the seed becomes.
492: const moodHint = seed.mood ? ` (one read: "${seed.mood}")` : '';
493: const strategyHint = seed.strategy ? `\n  - one example strategy: ${seed.strategy}` : '';
494: // ---------------------------------------------------------------
495: // Fat tool-exit response — what the model sees on stdout.
496: // ---------------------------------------------------------------
497: process.stdout.write(`BRAND SEED · ${seed.id}
498: Seed color (anchor for your primary brand color):
499:   ${fmtOklch(seed.oklch)} — ${hueWord(H)}${moodHint}
500: This is the brand's anchor — a single beautiful color. Compose the rest of
501: the palette around it using YOUR judgment, the brief (PRODUCT.md /
502: DESIGN.md / the user's prompt), and the color-strategy guidance already in
503: SKILL.md.
504: How to use:
505: 1. Read the brief. Write one specific phrase describing the mood this
506:    product calls for. Be granular. Good: "1970s travel poster — sun-baked
507:    warmth, considered", "midnight jazz club — smoky brass, saxophone
508:    light", "Scandinavian winter morning — quiet light through frost". Bad:
509:    "modern and clean", "warm and inviting". The first lets you compose; the
510:    second is generic and will produce generic palettes.
511: 2. The seed's hue (${H.toFixed(0)}°) anchors your primary brand color. You
512:    choose L and C to match the mood. The same hue can be deep-and-velvet,
513:    bright-and-confident, or pale-and-faded — pick the one the mood demands.
514:    Primary's hue should stay within ±10° of the seed.${strategyHint}
515: 3. Now compose the full palette in OKLCH (5 more roles):
516:      • bg       — the most important architectural choice.
517:                   CORE PRINCIPLE: the mood lives in the BRAND COLORS
518:                   (primary + accent) and typography, NOT in the surface.
519:                   A warm brand puts the warmth in its primary against a
520:                   pure surface. Putting warmth in BOTH primary AND bg is
521:                   the AI cliché.
522:                   DEFAULT A — PURE white: exactly oklch(1.000 0.000 0).
523:                     Not 0.99, not chroma 0.002. The most confident
524:                     brands in every field — fashion houses, galleries,
525:                     publishers, tool makers — use literal #ffffff.
526:                     Don't add hidden warmth.
527:                   DEFAULT B — PURE black/near-black: L 0.04-0.12,
528:                     chroma exactly 0.000. No hue tint. Pick L for the
529:                     mood (cinema dark, gallery dark, instrument-panel
530:                     dark); C stays 0.
531:                   ALT 2 — TINTED: chroma 0.015-0.05.
532:                     Use ONLY when:
533:                     (a) the mood is EXPLICITLY environmental — the surface
534:                         IS part of the brand (1920s lacquered interior,
535:                         leather library, ceramic studio, hotel lobby), or
536:                     (b) the seed itself is desaturated (chroma < 0.10) and
537:                         needs a tinted surface to read as a brand.
538:                     NOT for "feels warm" / "modern + warm" / "moody". If
539:                     your mood says "warm" but doesn't name a specific
540:                     environment, use PURE white and let primary carry
541:                     the warmth.
542:                   HEURISTIC: if the seed's chroma > 0.10 and the mood
543:                   doesn't name a specific environment, it's almost
544:                   always PURE white. Target distribution across many
545:                   palettes: ~50% pure white, ~25% pure black, ~25%
546:                   tinted.
547:      • surface  — bg pulled slightly toward ink (10-15% mix). Same hue
548:                   family as bg. Used for cards, panels, sections.
549:      • ink      — body text color. Must reach ≥7:1 contrast vs bg.
550:                   Can carry the brand hue at low chroma in light mode
551:                   (slight warmth or coolness toward the brand).
552:      • accent   — a SECOND brand color, distinct from primary in BOTH
553:                   hue AND lightness. Picked to complement the mood (not
554:                   default-complementary across the wheel). Used for
555:                   badges, status pills, links, accent rules.
556:      • muted    — secondary text. Ink pulled 40% toward bg, keeping ink's
557:                   hue. Must reach ≥3.5:1 contrast vs bg.
558: 4. Pick a color STRATEGY (the four steps from SKILL.md):
559:      • Restrained: tinted neutrals + accent ≤10% — product default
560:      • Committed: one saturated color carries 30-60% — identity-driven
561:      • Full palette: 3-4 named roles each used deliberately — brand work
562:      • Drenched: the surface IS the color — campaign, hero, statement
563:    The brief picks the strategy. A startup dashboard ≠ a perfume brand.
564: Hard rules (already in SKILL.md, recapped because the seed step is where
565: they actually bite):
566:   - OKLCH only — never hex. Never #RRGGBB.
567:   - ink-vs-bg WCAG contrast ≥ 7 (body text must be readable)
568:   - primary chroma ≤ 0.23 (above this, primary glows perceptually and
569:     no text on it is readable — acid-bright is a UI failure)
570:   - if primary L > 0.78, primary chroma ≤ 0.18 (the fluorescent zone)
571:   - primary-vs-accent contrast ≥ 1.7 (they must be visually distinct,
572:     not two variants of the same hue at similar lightness)
573:   - accent must carry readable text on a filled badge/pill: EITHER
574:     saturated (chroma ≥ 0.10) OR clearly light (L ≥ 0.85) OR clearly
575:     dark (L ≤ 0.30). Never a muddy mid-tone (L 0.45-0.72 + chroma < 0.10)
576:     — taupe/mushroom/dusty-grey accents read as weak and can't hold text
577:     either way. Saturate it or push its lightness to a clear light/dark.
578:   - avoid the saturated AI attractor zones: claude-beige (warm-cream bg
579:     + dusty brown primary), forest-green-on-cream, AI-purple-on-white,
580:     navy-cream-with-orange-accent
581: TEXT-ON-COLOR FILLS — pick by perceptual contrast, not just WCAG. The
582: rule applies to ANY element where text sits on a saturated color fill:
583: primary buttons, accent buttons, badges, status pills, tag highlights,
584: filled callouts. Don't only think "primary button" — apply consistently.
585: For any saturated mid-luminance color (L between 0.42 and 0.78, chroma ≥
586: 0.08), use WHITE text (or near-white from your bg), not dark text — even
587: if WCAG says dark technically passes. The Helmholtz-Kohlrausch effect
588: makes saturated colors appear brighter than their luminance suggests,
589: and dark text on a warm-or-cool-saturated fill reads as muddy.
590: Convention: saturated action fills in the wild, from fast-food reds to
591: status pills to filled badges, near-universally carry white text.
592: Dark text is correct only on PALE fills (L > 0.85) or PURE-NEUTRAL fills
593: (chroma near 0). Everything else: white text.
594: Return your composed palette in CSS custom properties using OKLCH, then
595: build with it. The seed is the start, not the recipe.
596: `);
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/pin.mjs
````javascript
  1: #!/usr/bin/env node
  2: /**
  3:  * Pin/unpin sub-commands as standalone skill shortcuts.
  4:  *
  5:  * Usage:
  6:  *   node <scripts_path>/pin.mjs pin <command>
  7:  *   node <scripts_path>/pin.mjs unpin <command>
  8:  *
  9:  * `pin audit` creates a lightweight audit skill that redirects to Impeccable's audit workflow.
 10:  * `unpin audit` removes that shortcut.
 11:  *
 12:  * The script discovers harness directories (.claude/skills, .cursor/skills, etc.)
 13:  * in the project root and creates/removes the pin in all of them.
 14:  */
 15: import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
 16: import { basename, join, resolve, dirname } from 'node:path';
 17: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
 18: const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
 19: // All known harness directories
 20: const HARNESS_DIRS = [
 21:   '.claude', '.cursor', '.gemini', '.codex', '.agents', '.agent', '.github', '.grok',
 22:   '.hermes',
 23:   '.trae', '.trae-cn', '.pi', '.opencode', '.kiro', '.rovodev', '.vibe', '.qoder',
 24: ];
 25: const CODEX_HARNESSES = new Set(['.codex', '.agents']);
 26: // Valid sub-command names
 27: const VALID_COMMANDS = [
 28:   'craft', 'init', 'extract', 'document', 'shape',
 29:   'critique', 'audit',
 30:   'polish', 'bolder', 'quieter', 'distill', 'harden', 'onboard', 'live',
 31:   'animate', 'colorize', 'typeset', 'layout', 'delight', 'overdrive',
 32:   'clarify', 'adapt', 'optimize',
 33: ];
 34: // Marker to identify pinned skills (so unpin doesn't delete user skills)
 35: const PIN_MARKER = '<!-- impeccable-pinned-skill -->';
 36: /**
 37:  * Walk up from startDir to find a project root.
 38:  */
 39: function findProjectRoot(startDir = process.cwd()) {
 40:   let dir = resolve(startDir);
 41:   while (dir !== '/') {
 42:     if (
 43:       existsSync(join(dir, 'package.json')) ||
 44:       existsSync(join(dir, '.git')) ||
 45:       existsSync(join(dir, 'skills-lock.json'))
 46:     ) {
 47:       return dir;
 48:     }
 49:     const parent = resolve(dir, '..');
 50:     if (parent === dir) break;
 51:     dir = parent;
 52:   }
 53:   return resolve(startDir);
 54: }
 55: /**
 56:  * Find harness skill directories that have an impeccable skill installed.
 57:  */
 58: function findHarnessDirs(projectRoot) {
 59:   const dirs = [];
 60:   for (const harness of HARNESS_DIRS) {
 61:     const skillsDir = join(projectRoot, harness, 'skills');
 62:     // Only pin in harness dirs that already have impeccable installed
 63:     const impeccableDir = join(skillsDir, 'impeccable');
 64:     if (existsSync(impeccableDir) || existsSync(join(skillsDir, 'i-impeccable'))) {
 65:       dirs.push(skillsDir);
 66:     }
 67:   }
 68:   return dirs;
 69: }
 70: /**
 71:  * Load command metadata (descriptions for pinned skills).
 72:  */
 73: function loadCommandMetadata() {
 74:   const metadataPath = join(__dirname, 'command-metadata.json');
 75:   if (existsSync(metadataPath)) {
 76:     return JSON.parse(readFileSync(metadataPath, 'utf-8'));
 77:   }
 78:   return {};
 79: }
 80: /**
 81:  * Generate a pinned skill's SKILL.md content.
 82:  */
 83: function commandPrefixForSkillsDir(skillsDir) {
 84:   return CODEX_HARNESSES.has(basename(dirname(skillsDir))) ? '$' : '/';
 85: }
 86: function generatePinnedSkill(command, metadata, commandPrefix, isCodex) {
 87:   const desc = metadata[command]?.description || `Shortcut for ${commandPrefix}impeccable ${command}.`;
 88:   const hint = metadata[command]?.argumentHint || '[target]';
 89:   const providerFrontmatter = isCodex
 90:     ? `metadata:\n  argument-hint: "${hint}"`
 91:     : `argument-hint: "${hint}"\nuser-invocable: true`;
 92:   return `---
 93: name: ${command}
 94: description: "${desc}"
 95: ${providerFrontmatter}
 96: ---
 97: ${PIN_MARKER}
 98: This is a pinned shortcut for \`${commandPrefix}impeccable ${command}\`.
 99: Invoke ${commandPrefix}impeccable ${command}, passing along any arguments provided here, and follow its instructions.
100: `;
101: }
102: /**
103:  * Pin a command: create shortcut skill in all harness dirs.
104:  */
105: function pin(command, projectRoot) {
106:   const metadata = loadCommandMetadata();
107:   const harnessDirs = findHarnessDirs(projectRoot);
108:   if (harnessDirs.length === 0) {
109:     console.log('No harness directories with impeccable installed found.');
110:     return false;
111:   }
112:   let created = 0;
113:   for (const skillsDir of harnessDirs) {
114:     const commandPrefix = commandPrefixForSkillsDir(skillsDir);
115:     const content = generatePinnedSkill(command, metadata, commandPrefix, commandPrefix === '$');
116:     // Check if skill already exists (and isn't a pin)
117:     const skillDir = join(skillsDir, command);
118:     if (existsSync(skillDir)) {
119:       const existingMd = join(skillDir, 'SKILL.md');
120:       if (existsSync(existingMd)) {
121:         const existing = readFileSync(existingMd, 'utf-8');
122:         if (!existing.includes(PIN_MARKER)) {
123:           console.log(`  SKIP: ${skillDir} (non-pinned skill already exists)`);
124:           continue;
125:         }
126:       }
127:     }
128:     mkdirSync(skillDir, { recursive: true });
129:     writeFileSync(join(skillDir, 'SKILL.md'), content, 'utf-8');
130:     console.log(`  + ${skillDir}`);
131:     created++;
132:   }
133:   if (created > 0) {
134:     console.log(`\nPinned '${command}' as a standalone shortcut in ${created} location(s).`);
135:     console.log('Use the pinned command directly in each harness.');
136:   }
137:   return created > 0;
138: }
139: /**
140:  * Unpin a command: remove shortcut skill from all harness dirs.
141:  */
142: function unpin(command, projectRoot) {
143:   const harnessDirs = findHarnessDirs(projectRoot);
144:   let removed = 0;
145:   for (const skillsDir of harnessDirs) {
146:     const skillDir = join(skillsDir, command);
147:     if (!existsSync(skillDir)) continue;
148:     const skillMd = join(skillDir, 'SKILL.md');
149:     if (!existsSync(skillMd)) continue;
150:     // Safety: only remove if it's a pinned skill
151:     const content = readFileSync(skillMd, 'utf-8');
152:     if (!content.includes(PIN_MARKER)) {
153:       console.log(`  SKIP: ${skillDir} (not a pinned skill)`);
154:       continue;
155:     }
156:     rmSync(skillDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
157:     console.log(`  - ${skillDir}`);
158:     removed++;
159:   }
160:   if (removed > 0) {
161:     console.log(`\nUnpinned '${command}' from ${removed} location(s).`);
162:     console.log(`Use Impeccable's '${command}' workflow directly to access it.`);
163:   } else {
164:     console.log(`No pinned '${command}' shortcut found.`);
165:   }
166:   return removed > 0;
167: }
168: // --- CLI ---
169: const [,, action, command] = process.argv;
170: if (!action || !command) {
171:   console.log('Usage: node pin.mjs <pin|unpin> <command>');
172:   console.log(`\nAvailable commands: ${VALID_COMMANDS.join(', ')}`);
173:   process.exit(1);
174: }
175: if (action !== 'pin' && action !== 'unpin') {
176:   console.error(`Unknown action: ${action}. Use 'pin' or 'unpin'.`);
177:   process.exit(1);
178: }
179: if (!VALID_COMMANDS.includes(command)) {
180:   console.error(`Unknown command: ${command}`);
181:   console.error(`Available commands: ${VALID_COMMANDS.join(', ')}`);
182:   process.exit(1);
183: }
184: const root = findProjectRoot();
185: if (action === 'pin') {
186:   pin(command, root);
187: } else {
188:   unpin(command, root);
189: }
````

## File: packages/setup-agentic-workflow/templates/skills/impeccable/scripts/serve-question.mjs
````javascript
   1: #!/usr/bin/env node
   2: /**
   3:  * Visual question server: present a decision to the user as a themed page
   4:  * instead of a plain-text prompt, then block until they answer.
   5:  *
   6:  * The script IS the wait: run it via the shell, it serves the page, prints
   7:  * the URL (and tries to open the default browser), and does not exit until
   8:  * the user chooses. The answer lands on stdout as one line:
   9:  *
  10:  *   ANSWER: {"optionId":"...","steer":"..."}
  11:  *
  12:  * Exit codes: 0 answered · 2 timed out, closed without answering, or no
  13:  * browser is available (IMPECCABLE_QUESTION_DISABLED, or a detected
  14:  * CI/headless/remote environment; IMPECCABLE_QUESTION_FORCE=1 overrides
  15:  * detection, --no-open skips it since the caller opens the URL itself).
  16:  *
  17:  * Payload (JSON file via --payload, or stdin):
  18:  * {
  19:  *   "title": "Choose the visual world",
  20:  *   "question": "The roll assigned Fillmore Handbill. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.",
  21:  *   "options": [
  22:  *     {
  23:  *       "id": "assigned",                  // returned verbatim
  24:  *       "label": "Fillmore Handbill",
  25:  *       "kicker": "THE ROLL",              // optional badge; the assigned option leads
  26:  *       "lineage": "1966-71 Fillmore ...", // optional
  27:  *       "thesis": "one line: the idea this direction owns",       // optional
  28:  *       "palette": ["#1a2f5e", "oklch(84% .19 80)", ...],         // optional, rendered as chips
  29:  *       "materials": ["letterpress", "newsprint"],                // optional, rendered as tags
  30:  *       "viewport": "one line: the first-viewport composition",   // optional
  31:  *       "case": "one line: the fusion verdict, honest",           // optional
  32:  *       "verdict": "competitive", // optional routing tier: "wins" |
  33:  *                                // "competitive" | "declined". Declined cards
  34:  *                                // render demoted after the full cards:
  35:  *                                // narrow, quiet, catalog art as a labeled
  36:  *                                // thumb, "Adopt anyway" instead of "Build
  37:  *                                // this". Still choosable; never deleted.
  38:  *       "kept": "one line: what the direction kept from this declined world",

  46:  *                                // full-fidelity direction comp (the legacy
  47:  *                                // key "sketch" is accepted as an alias). May
  48:  *                                // not exist yet: the page shimmer-waits and
  49:  *                                // polls the slot until the file lands, so
  50:  *                                // serve first and generate after
  51:  *       "hero": "https://... or /abs/path.webp",   // optional inspiration image;
  52:  *                                // rides picture-in-picture when a comp exists
  53:  *       "board": "https://... or /abs/path.webp"   // optional secondary image
  54:  *     }, ...
  55:  *   ],
  56:  *   "reroll": true,          // adds a re-roll action (returns {"optionId":"reroll"})
  57:  *                            // or { "registers": ["safer", "bolder"] } to add
  58:  *                            // the register steers beside it: the answer then
  59:  *                            // carries "register" and the agent re-runs
  60:  *                            // concept-seed with --register <value>
  61:  *   "canon": true,           // adds the "Play it straight" standing exit;
  62:  *                            // direction rounds only (returns {"optionId":"canon"})

  64:  *                            // same anatomy (label, thesis, palette, comp, ...);
  65:  *                            // rendered last and visually subordinate. Without it,
  66:  *                            // canon stays a quiet footer action.
  67:  *   "steer": true,           // adds a free-text steer field returned with any answer
  68:  *   "followup": true         // this round's pick is not terminal: the server
  69:  *                            // stays open awaiting --update with the next
  70:  *                            // round (detached mode only), the page shows a
  71:  *                            // loading hand instead of goodbye, and the
  72:  *                            // answer carries followup:true so --wait knows
  73:  *                            // to keep the table. Use it when a decision has
  74:  *                            // a known second half, e.g. direction first,
  75:  *                            // then the execution contract.
  76:  * }
  77:  *
  78:  * Options render as large cards: the comp leads when present, with the
  79:  * inspiration image picture-in-picture; a hero alone renders full-bleed; a
  80:  * text-only direction gets its identity from the palette chips and tags.
  81:  * Local image paths are served by this server; nothing is uploaded anywhere.
  82:  *
  83:  * Modes:
  84:  *   (default)  block until answered; ANSWER on stdout; exit 0.
  85:  *   --schema   print the canonical payload example and exit.
  86:  *   --start    for harnesses that cannot leave a shell blocked: daemonize the
  87:  *              server, print QUESTION URL + QUESTION KEY, exit immediately.
  88:  *              Never auto-opens a browser: the agent routes the URL to the
  89:  *              best surface it has (in-app browser first, then the system
  90:  *              opener); pass --open to force the system browser instead.
  91:  *   --wait --key K [--poll 60]   poll for the answer: exit 0 + ANSWER line,
  92:  *              exit 3 WAITING (run --wait again), exit 2 server gone,
  93:  *              exit 4 PAGE CLOSED (the tab went away without an answer;
  94:  *              re-present, reopen the URL, or fall back).
  95:  *   --stop --key K               kill a daemonized question.
  96:  *   --update --key K --payload F deliver the next hand after a re-roll: the
  97:  *              live page swaps to loading cards when the user re-rolls, and
  98:  *              reloads into this new payload the moment it lands. Always the
  99:  *              same key the round started with; a second --start serves a new
 100:  *              URL and strands the open tab on a hand that never arrives.
 101:  *
 102:  * --timeout bounds the wait for a page to arrive, never the user's decision:
 103:  * once the page heartbeats, the server lives while the page does, and exits
 104:  * only after --idle-grace seconds (default 600) pass with no beat, wide
 105:  * enough to survive a closed laptop lid mid-decision.
 106:  *
 107:  *   node serve-question.mjs --payload question.json [--timeout 900] [--idle-grace 600] [--no-open] [--port 0]
 108:  */

 803:   /* Catalog art standing in for a comp-less card is a reference, and says so

 879:   button.choose { margin-top: auto; align-self: start; background: var(--ks-kinpaku); color: var(--ks-dark-ink); border: 0; font-family: var(--ks-font); font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.35; padding: 10px 38px; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background .15s; }

 885:   #steer { flex: 1; min-width: 16rem; background: var(--ks-lacquer-raised); color: var(--ks-text); border: 1px solid var(--ks-rule); border-radius: 7px; padding: .6rem .85rem; font: inherit; }
````
